1) Pour tout entier $n \geqslant 1$, montrer que toute suite unitaire de longueur $2n + 1$ est inscriptible dans $[0, 2 - \frac{1}{2^{n}}]$.

2) Pour tout entier $n \geqslant 1$, construire une suite unitaire de longueur $4n + 3$ qui n'est pas inscriptible dans $[0, 2 - \frac{1}{2^{n}}]$.

Déterminer tous les polynômes $P \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ tels que :

(i) $P(n) > 0$ pour tout $n \geqslant 1$

(ii) le nombre de facteurs premiers de $P(mn)$ est égal à celui de $P(m) P(n)$ pour tous $m, n \geqslant 1$.

Soit $n$ un entier naturel avec $n \geqslant 3$. Lucie place $n$ feuilles en cercle et y inscrit un nombre réel. Déterminer tous les entiers $k$ tels que $1 \leqslant k \leqslant n$ pour lesquels la condition suivante est satisfaite : Si au moins un nombre n'est pas nul, il existe $k$ feuilles adjacentes dont la somme est non nulle.

Soit $a > 0$ et $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$, montrer que
$$
\frac{a^{n}}{\sum_{k=0}^{2 n} a^k} < \frac{1}{2 n}
$$

Un entier $n \geqslant 1$ est dit nippon s'il possède trois diviseurs distincts $d_{1}, d_{2}, d_{3}$ vérifiant $1 \leqslant d_{1} < d_{2} < d_{3}$ et $d_{1} + d_{2} + d_{3} = 2022$. Déterminer le plus petit entier $n$ qui est nippon.
Soit $a$, $b$ et $c$ trois nombres réels tels que $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=1$. Déterminer les valeurs extrêmes du nombre réel $ab+bc-ca$.

Soit $f_{n}$ la somme des restes de la division de $n$ par chaque entier $k$ avec $1 \leq k \leq n$. Par exemple, $f_{5} = 0+1+2+1+0=4$. Déterminer tous les entiers $n \geq 2$ tels que $f_{n} = f_{n-1} + n - 2$.

Soit $ABCD$ un parallélogramme avec $AC = BC$. Soit $P$ un point sur la demi-droite $[AB)$, prolongée au-delà de $B$. Soit $Q$ le point d'intersection, distinct de $D$, entre $(PD)$ et le cercle circonscrit à $ACD$. Soit $R$ le point d'intersection, distinct de $P$, entre $(PC)$ et le cercle circonscrit à $APQ$. Montrer que les droites $(AQ)$, $(BR)$ et $(CD)$ sont concourantes.

Soient $m$ et $n$ deux entiers tels que $m > n \geqslant 3$. Morgane dispose $m$ jetons en cercle et souhaite les colorier avec $n$ couleurs différentes. Elle exige que tout ensemble de $n+1$ jetons adjacents contienne au moins une fois chaque couleur. On dit alors que $m$ est $n$-coloriable. Démontrer que pour tout $n \geqslant 3$, il n'existe qu'un nombre fini non nul d'entiers $m$ non $n$-coloriables, et déterminer le plus grand $m$ non $n$-coloriable.

Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif. Soit $k = 4n + 2$. Anna a sélectionné $k$ entiers strictement distincts dans l'intervalle $[0, 5^n]$. Démontrer qu'il existe trois nombres $a, b$ et $c$ tels que $a < b < c$ et $c + 2a > 3b$.

Un ensemble $E$ de nombres entiers strictement positifs est dit "intéressant" si, pour tout $n \geq 1$ et pour tout sous-ensemble $\{x_1, \ldots, x_n\} \subset E$ avec $x_i$ distincts, la moyenne arithmétique $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$ et la moyenne géométrique $\left(\prod_{i=1}^{n} x_i\right)^{1/n}$ sont des entiers.

1. Peut-on construire un ensemble $E$ intéressant composé de 2022 éléments?
2. Peut-on construire un ensemble $E$ intéressant contenant une infinité d'éléments?

Soient $m$ et $n$ deux entiers tels que $m > n \geqslant 3$. Morgane dispose $m$ jetons en cercle et souhaite les colorier avec $n$ couleurs différentes. Elle exige que tout ensemble de $n+1$ jetons adjacents contienne au moins une fois chaque couleur. On dit alors que $m$ est $n$-coloriable. Démontrer que pour tout $n \geqslant 3$, il n'existe qu'un nombre fini non nul d'entiers $m$ non $n$-coloriables, et déterminer le plus grand $m$ non $n$-coloriable.

Soit $A, B, C$ et $D$ quatre points cocycliques sur un cercle $\Omega$. Soit $E$ et $F$ les intersections de $[B A)$ et $[B C)$ avec la tangente à $\Omega$ en $D$. Soit $T$ un point intérieur au triangle $A B C$ tel que $T E \parallel C D$ et $T F \parallel A D$. Soit $K$ le point du segment $[D F]$, distinct de $D$, tel que $T K = T D$. Démontrer que les droites $A C$, $D T$ et $B K$ sont concourantes.
Soit $a \geqslant 1$ un entier. Déterminer tous les diviseurs $k \geqslant 1$ de $3 a^{2}$ tels que $a^{2} + k$ soit un carré parfait.

Soit $k = 3n$ avec $n \geqslant 2$. Une grenouille se déplace dans une grille de $k \times k$ cases, en ne pouvant aller que vers le haut ou vers la droite. Elle part de l'angle inférieur gauche $S$ et veut arriver à l'angle supérieur droit $F$. Certaines cases sont piégées, et si la grenouille y atterrit, elle est capturée.

Un ensemble de cases piégées est dit bloquant s'il rend impossible le trajet de $S$ à $F$. Un tel ensemble est dit minimal s'il n'est plus bloquant dès qu'une de ses cases est retirée.

a) Montrer qu'il existe un ensemble bloquant minimal contenant au moins $k(n - 1)$ cases.

b) Montrer qu'aucun ensemble bloquant minimal ne contient plus de $kn$ cases.

Soit $\left(a_{n}\right)_{n \geqslant 1}$ une suite d'entiers naturels non nuls vérifiant $a_{n+k} \mid a_{n}+a_{n+\frac{k}{2}}$ pour tout $n \geqslant 1$ et tout entier pair $k \geqslant 2$. Montrer que la suite est ultimement périodique, c'est-à-dire qu'il existe $N \geqslant 1$ et $d \geqslant 1$ tels que $a_{n} = a_{n+d}$ pour tout $n \geqslant N$.

Soit $n \geqslant 1$ un entier strictement positif. On place $n$ clous sur un mur et on colore chaque arête entre deux clous avec une couleur choisie parmi $n$ couleurs. On dit que la coloration est complète si, pour tout ensemble de trois couleurs distinctes $a, b, c$, il existe trois clous tels que les arêtes entre ces clous soient coloriées avec $a$, $b$ et $c$.

- Peut-on avoir une coloration complète pour $n=6$ ?
- Peut-on avoir une coloration complète pour $n=7$ ?

Soit $n \geqslant 2$ un entier. On considère $n$ entiers distincts $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$. On constate que la somme de n'importe $n-1$ d'entre eux est congrue à $0$ modulo $n$. Montrer que la somme de tous les $n$ entiers est divisible par $n$.

Déterminer tous les triplets $(x, y, z)$ avec $x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}^*$ tels que
$$
2^{y} = z! - x!
$$
Déterminer tous les quadruplets de réels $(x, y, z, w)$ vérifiant les équations suivantes : $$x = y z + z w, \quad y = z w + w x, \quad z = w x + x y \text{ et } w = x y + y z$$
Déterminez le nombre de permutations $\sigma$ de $\{1, 2, \ldots, 2023\}$ telles que $\sigma(k) > k$ est vrai pour exactement un indice $k$.

Déterminer tous les triplets $(x, y, z)$ avec $x, y, z \in \mathbb{N}^*$ tels que
$$
2^{y} = z! - x!
$$

Soit $ABC$ un triangle dont tous les angles sont strictement inférieurs à $\frac{\pi}{2}$, avec $AB \neq CB$. Soit $O$ le centre du cercle circonscrit de $ABC$. Soit $P$ le second point d'intersection de la droite $(AB)$ avec le cercle circonscrit de $BOC$. Montrer que $PA = PC$.
Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif et $x \geqslant n$ un réel. Démontrer que $\frac{x^2 + n}{x} \geqslant n+1$ et préciser les conditions d'égalité.

Soit $(x_{n})$ une suite de réels. On suppose que $x_{0}=1$ et que pour tout $n \geqslant 1$, $x_{n}$ est la plus petite solution strictement positive de
$$
\left(x_{n}-x_{n-1}\right)\left(x_{n}+x_{n-1}-2 \sqrt{n}\right)=2 .
$$
Déterminer le plus petit entier $n$ tel que $x_{n} \geqslant 2022$.

Soit $n \geqslant 3$ et soient $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n}$ des réels. Montrer que
$$
2\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_{i}\right)^{2} \leqslant n\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_{i}^{2} + \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_{i} x_{(i \mod n)+1}\right)
$$
Pour tout entier $k \geqslant 1$, on définit $s_{k} = \sum_{i=1}^{k} i!$. Démontrer que l'ensemble des nombres premiers qui divisent au moins un terme de la suite $\left(s_{k}\right)$ est infini.

Soient $c_{1}, \ldots, c_{n}$ des réels positifs ou nuls tels que $c_{1}+c_{2}+\ldots+c_{n}=2$. Soient $x_{0}, x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n}$ des nombres réels tels que $x_{0}=x_{n}=0$. Supposons que pour tout $i$ compris entre $1$ et $n$ inclus,
$$
\left|x_{i}-x_{i-1}\right| \leqslant c_{i}
$$
Montrer que l'on a
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left(x_{i-1}+x_{i}\right) c_{i} \leqslant 2
$$

Soit $k \geqslant 1$ un entier. Déterminer le plus petit entier $n$ tel que, pour toute configuration de $n$ points dans le plan, on puisse en extraire un sous-ensemble $S$ de $k$ points tel que soit $\forall P, Q \in S$, $\|P - Q\| \leq 2$, soit $\forall P, Q \in S$, $\|P - Q\| > 1$.

Soit $\beta \neq 0$. Trouver toutes les fonctions $g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ telles que pour tous réels $u, v$,
$$
g\left(u^{2}+v+g(v)\right)=g(u)^{2}+\beta v
$$

Soit $\left(b_{k}\right)_{k \geqslant 1}$ une suite d'entiers strictement positifs telle que $b_{1}$ et $b_{2}$ soient premiers entre eux et, pour tout $k \geqslant 1$, $b_{k+2}=b_{k} b_{k+1}+1$. Montrer que pour tout entier $p>1$, il existe $q>p$ tel que $b_{p}^{p} \mid b_{q}^{q}$. Le résultat est-il encore vrai lorsque $p=1$ ?

Déterminer toutes les fonctions $f: \mathbb{N}^{\star} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}^{\star}$ vérifiant : (1) $\gcd(f(1), f(2), \ldots) = 1$. (2) Il existe $M \in \mathbb{N}^{\star}$ tel que pour tout $n \geqslant M$, $f(n) > 1$ et pour tous $a, b \in \mathbb{N}^{\star}$, $$f(a)^{n} \mid f(a+b)^{a^{n-1}}-f(b)^{a^{n-1}}$$

Soit $ABC$ un triangle avec $AC > AB$ et $\Gamma$ son cercle circonscrit. La tangente à $\Gamma$ en $A$ coupe $(BC)$ en $T$. On note $M$ le milieu de $[BC]$ et $R$ le symétrique de $A$ par rapport à $B$. On définit $S$ tel que $SABT$ est un parallélogramme. La droite parallèle à $(AB)$ passant par $M$ coupe $(SB)$ en $P$. Si $P$ appartient à $\Gamma$, démontrer que la droite $(AC)$ est tangente au cercle circonscrit du triangle $SRT$.
Soient $x$, $y$ et $z$ des réels strictement positifs. Montrer que $$ 4\left(x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}+3\right) \geqslant 3(x+1)(y+1)(z+1). $$

Anna et Baptiste jouent à un jeu avec 2022 cases numérotées de 1 à 2022. Ils les colorient à tour de rôle, en commençant par Anna, en choisissant soit la couleur rouge, soit la couleur bleu. Une fois toutes les cases coloriées, on compte le nombre d'entiers $a$ tels que $1 \leqslant a \leqslant 2019$ et les cases $a$ et $a+3$ sont de la même couleur. Anna veut maximiser ce nombre, Baptiste veut le minimiser. Quel est le meilleur score que Anna peut garantir, indépendamment des choix de Baptiste?

Soit $ABC$ un triangle dont tous les angles sont strictement inférieurs à $\frac{\pi}{2}$, avec $AB \neq CB$. Soit $O$ le centre du cercle circonscrit de $ABC$. Soit $P$ le second point d'intersection de la droite $(AB)$ avec le cercle circonscrit de $BOC$. Montrer que $PA = PC$.
Soient $x$ et $y$ deux réels tels que $x + \lfloor x \rfloor = y + \lfloor y \rfloor$. Montrer que $x = y$.

Alice place 200 boîtes dans une pièce, chacune contenant un entier naturel non nul, pas nécessairement distincts. À chaque minute, tant que possible, elle choisit trois boîtes avec des nombres $a$, $b$ et $c$ tels que $a + b = c$, et un entier $k \geqslant 2$ arbitraire, puis remplace $c$ par $k \times c$. Démontrer qu'indépendamment de la configuration initiale et des choix d'Alice, le processus s'arrêtera finalement.
\text{Soit } a, b, c \text{ trois réels positifs, tels que } a \leqslant 1. \text{ Démontrer que: } \quad a b + b + 2 c \geqslant 4 \sqrt{a b c}
Soit $k \geqslant 6$. Démontrer qu'il est possible de diviser un carré en $k$ carrés distincts (pas nécessairement de dimensions identiques).

\text{Soit } a, b, c > 0 \text{ tels que } ab + bc + ca = 3.\text{ Démontrer que} \quad \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a+3}{b+c} + 3 \geqslant 27 \cdot \frac{(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c})^{2}}{(a+b+c)^{3}}
Déterminer tous les entiers $n > 0$ tels qu'il existe un entier $k$ vérifiant $222k$ et $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} d_i^2 = n$, où $d_i$ sont les chiffres de $222k$.
Déterminer tous les triplets d'entiers $(x, y, n)$ tels que $n^{2} = 17 (x^{2})^{2} - 32 x^{2} y^{2} + 41 (y^{2})^{2}$.
Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif et $x \geqslant n$ un réel. Démontrer que $\frac{x^2 + n}{x} \geqslant n+1$ et préciser les conditions d'égalité.

Soit $n \in \mathbb{N}^*$ un entier. Émilie commence avec $n$ piles, chacune contenant une seule pièce. À chaque étape, elle peut choisir deux piles, enlever un nombre égal de pièces de chacune, puis en regrouper les pièces pour en former une nouvelle pile. Déterminer, en fonction de $n$, le minimum de piles non vides pouvant être obtenues après un nombre fini de tels mouvements.

Soient $a \geqslant 2$ et $d \geqslant 2$ deux entiers premiers entre eux. On définit une suite $(y_n)_{n \geq 1}$ par $y_1 = 1$ et, pour tout $n \geq 1$, $y_{n+1} = y_n / a$ si $a \mid y_n$, et $y_{n+1} = y_n + d$ sinon. Déterminer, en fonction de $a$ et $d$, la plus grande puissance $\ell$ telle que $a^{\ell}$ divise un terme de la suite $(y_n)$.

Soient $a$, $b$, $c$ des réels strictement positifs tels que $ab + bc + ca = 1$. Montrer que
$$
2\left(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}\right)+\frac{4}{3}\left(\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{1}{a^{2}+1}\right) \geqslant 5
$$

Soit $n \geqslant 3$ un entier. On dispose d'un tableau de dimensions $(n-2) \times n$, où chaque ligne contient exactement une fois chaque entier de 1 à $n$, et chaque colonne ne contient que des éléments distincts. Démontrer qu'il est possible d'ajouter deux lignes supplémentaires de sorte que le tableau final de taille $n \times n$ soit un carré de Latin.
Soit $a, b, c$ trois nombres réels tels que $a+b+c=2$ et $ab+bc+ca=1$. Trouver la valeur maximale de $a-b$.

Soient $x$ et $y$ deux réels. On définit les suites $\left(x_{n}\right)$ et $\left(y_{n}\right)$ par $x_{0}=x$, $y_{0}=y$ et pour tout $n$ entier naturel, $x_{n+1}=x_{n}+y_{n}$, $y_{n+1}=x_{n} y_{n}$. Trouver toutes les paires $(x, y)$ telles que $x_{2022}=x_{0}$ et $y_{2022}=y_{0}$.
Déterminer tous les triplets $(x, y, z) \in \mathbb{N}^{3}$ tels que $1517^{x} + 15^{y} = 1532^{z}$.

Soient $c_{1}, \ldots, c_{n}$ des réels positifs ou nuls avec $\sum_{i=1}^{n} c_{i} = 2$. Soient $x_{0}, x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n}$ des nombres réels tels que $x_{0} = x_{n} = 0$. Supposons que pour chaque $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$, on ait $|x_{i} - x_{i-1}| \leq c_{i}$. Démontrer que
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_{i-1} + x_{i}) c_{i} \leq 2
$$

Soient $a$ et $b$ deux réels positifs. Montrer que
$$
\left(a^{2}+a+1\right)\left(b^{2}+b+1\right) \geqslant 9 a b.
$$
Pour quelles valeurs de $a$ et $b$ l'égalité a-t-elle lieu?
Soit la suite $\left(b_{n}\right)$ définie par $b_{0}=b_{1}=b_{2}=1$ et pour $n \geq 3$ : $$ b_{n}=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{b_{n-1} \cdot b_{n-2} \cdot b_{n-3}}\right\rfloor $$ Calculer $b_{2022}$.
Trouver toutes les fonctions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ vérifiant, pour tous réels $a$ et $b$, l'identité $$ f(a) f(b) f(a - b) = a^{2} f(b) - b^{2} f(a). $$

Soit $k \geqslant 1$ un entier. On dispose de $4k$ jetons, $2k$ rouges et $2k$ bleus. Un mouvement consiste à échanger un bloc de jetons rouges consécutifs avec un bloc de jetons bleus consécutifs, de même longueur. Par exemple, la configuration rbbbrrrb peut être transformée en rrrbrbbb par un seul mouvement. Déterminer le plus petit entier $n = n(k)$ tel que, quelle que soit la configuration initiale des $4k$ jetons, on peut l’atteindre à l’état final où les $2k$ premiers jetons sont rouges en au plus $n$ mouvements.
Soit $k \geqslant 7$ un entier impair. On colorie $\frac{k-1}{2}$ sommets d'un $k$-gone régulier. Montrer qu'il existe trois sommets coloriés tels que le triangle formé est isocèle.

Soit $\left(P_{n}\right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ une suite de polynômes à coefficients rationnels. On suppose qu'il existe un polynôme unitaire $Q$ à coefficients rationnels tel que $P_{n} - P_{n+1} = -Q$ pour tout $n \geqslant 0$. On suppose de plus que chaque $P_{n}$ admet une racine rationnelle. Montrer qu'on est dans un des deux cas suivants : 
- $P_{0}$ et $Q$ ont une racine rationnelle en commun
- Il existe un polynôme à coefficients rationnels $R$ tel que $P_{0} = RQ$ et $\deg(R) = 1$.

Soit $x, y, z > 0$ tels que $x^{2} < 16 y z$, $y^{2} < 16 x z$ et $z^{2} < 16 x y$. Montrer que
$$
x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} < 2(x y + y z + x z)
$$
Trouver toutes les fonctions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ vérifiant, pour tout $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, $$ f\left(a^{2}+a b+f\left(b^{2}\right)\right)=a f(b)+f\left(a^{2}\right)+b^{2} $$

Soit $n \geqslant 2$ un entier et $C>0$ une constante réelle. On suppose qu'il existe une suite $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ de réels non tous nuls telle que : $a_{2} + a_{3} + \ldots + a_{n} = a_{1}$. Pour tout indice $1 \leqslant i \leqslant n$, on a soit $a_{i} \leqslant a_{i+1}$, soit $a_{i} \leqslant a_{i+1} + C a_{i+2}$ (où on définit $a_{n+1} = a_{1}$ et $a_{n+2} = a_{2}$ ).

1. Montrer que nécessairement $C \geqslant 2$.
2. On suppose que $C=2$, montrer que $n$ est nécessairement pair.

Soient $a, b$ deux entiers tels que $\mathrm{pgcd}(a, b)$ a au moins deux diviseurs premiers distincts. Soit $S=\{x \in \mathbb{N} \mid x \equiv a \mod b\}$. Un élément de $S$ est dit irréductible s'il ne peut pas être décomposé en un produit de deux éléments de $S$ ou plus (non nécessairement distincts). Démontrer qu'il existe un entier $N > 0$ tel que tout élément de $S$ puisse s'exprimer comme produit d'au plus $N$ éléments irréductibles de $S$ (non nécessairement distincts).

Soit $\{\mathcal{C}_1, \mathcal{C}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{C}_n\}$ un ensemble de cercles de rayon égal dans le plan, tels que deux cercles quelconques ne sont jamais tangents et que l'ensemble est connexe au sens où l'on peut toujours se déplacer entre deux cercles via une chaîne de cercles intersectant. Soit $S$ l'ensemble des points d'intersection entre les cercles. Démontrer que $|S| \geq n$.

Soit $ABC$ un triangle et $\omega_{A}$ son cercle $A$-exinscrit, tangent à $BC$ en $A_{1}$, à $AB$ en $C_{1}$ et à $AC$ en $B_{1}$. Posons $P$ le milieu de $[B_{1}C_{1}]$. Soit $X$ le second point d'intersection de $(A_{1}P)$ avec $\omega_{A}$. Si $R$ est le point d'intersection des tangentes en $A$ au cercle circonscrit de $ABC$ et en $X$ à $\omega_{A}$, démontrer que $RX = RP$.
Soit $n$ un entier vérifiant $n \geqslant 2$. Soit $d$ le plus grand diviseur strict de $n$. On suppose que $d > 1$. Montrer que $n + d$ n'est pas une puissance de 2.
Soient $x$ et $y$ deux nombres réels tels que $x^2 + 2x = y^2 + 2y$. Démontrer que si $x$ est un entier relatif, alors $y$ l'est également.
Trouver tous les entiers naturels $n$ pour lesquels $n! + 2023$ est le carré d'un entier.

Montrer qu'il n'existe pas de réels $a, b, c$ strictement positifs tels que
$$
\left(2 a^{2}+b c\right)\left(2 b^{2}+a c\right)\left(2 c^{2}+a b\right)=26 a^{2} b^{2} c^{2}
$$

Soient $x$, $y$ et $z$ des réels tels que $0 \leqslant x, y, z \leqslant 2$. Démontrer que
$$
(x-y)(y-z)(x-z) \leqslant 2
$$

Soit $n \geqslant 2$ et $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n} \in [0,1]$ des réels. Déterminer la plus grande valeur possible du minimum parmi les expressions
$$
 x_{1}(1 - x_{2}),\ x_{2}(1 - x_{3}),\ \ldots,\ x_{n}(1 - x_{1})
$$

Soit $n$ un entier strictement positif avec $n \geqslant 2$. À chaque étape, on remplace $n$ par $n + \frac{n}{p}$, où $p$ est un diviseur premier de $n$. Démontrer que $p=3$ est utilisé un nombre infini de fois.
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a}{9bc + 1} \geq \frac{a + b + c}{1 + (a + b + c)^2}

Soient $x, y, z$ trois réels strictement positifs. Démontrer que
$$
\frac{x^{4}+1}{y^{3}+y^{2}+y}+\frac{y^{4}+1}{z^{3}+z^{2}+z}+\frac{z^{4}+1}{x^{3}+x^{2}+x} \geqslant 2
$$

Soient $x, y, z, w$ quatre réels tels que $|x|>1, |y|>1, |z|>1$ et $|w|>1$. Supposons que $(x+1)(y+1)(z+1)(w+1) = (x-1)(y-1)(z-1)(w-1)$. Montrer que $$\frac{1}{x-1} + \frac{1}{y-1} + \frac{1}{z-1} + \frac{1}{w-1} > 0$$

Soit $n \geqslant 1$ un entier et $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n}$ des réels positifs. Montrer que
$$
\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{x_{k}}{k}\right)\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n} k x_{k}\right) \leqslant \frac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n} x_{k}\right)^{2}
$$
Pour quelles valeurs d'égalité cela est-il vrai?

Soit $ABC$ un triangle, $\omega$ son cercle inscrit, $D$, $E$ et $F$ les points de tangence de $\omega$ sur $BC$, $CA$ et $AB$ respectivement. Soit $M$ le point d'intersection de la perpendiculaire en $C$ à $(BC)$ avec $(EF)$, et $N$ celui de la perpendiculaire en $B$ à $(BC)$ avec $(EF)$. Soit $P$ le second point d'intersection de $(DM)$ avec $\omega$ et $Q$ celui de $(DN)$ avec $\omega$. Montrer que $DP = DQ$.

Zwei Sehnen $AC$ und $BD$ in einem Kreis mit Mittelpunkt $M$ schneiden sich in $P$. Der Umkreis des Dreiecks $PBC$ hat den Mittelpunkt $E$, und der Umkreis des Dreiecks $PDA$ hat den Mittelpunkt $F$. Die beiden Umkreise schneiden sich erneut in $Q$. Zeigen Sie, dass $\overline{QE} = \overline{MF}$ gilt.

Sei $n$ eine natürliche Zahl, deren positive Teiler in aufsteigender Reihenfolge $1 = d_{1} < d_{2} < d_{3} < \ldots < d_{k} = n$ notiert sind. Bestimme alle solchen $n$, für die gilt: $n = d_{13} + d_{14} + d_{15}$ und $\left(d_{5} + 1\right)^{3} = d_{15} + 1$.

Es sei $n \geq 2$. Die Zahlen $1$ bis $n^{2}$ werden zufällig in ein $n \times n$-Gitter platziert. Für jedes Paar von Zahlen in derselben Zeile oder Spalte berechnet man das Verhältnis der größeren zur kleineren Zahl. Die Charakteristik $C$ ist definiert als der minimale solche Quotient unter allen $n^{2}(n-1)$ Paaren. Bestimme den maximal möglichen Wert von $C$. (Begründung ist erforderlich.)

Seien $a, b, c$ positive ganze Zahlen mit $b > 2a$ und $c > 2b$. Zeigen Sie, dass es eine reelle Zahl $r$ gibt, so dass $\{ra\}, \{rb\}, \{rc\} \in \left( \frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{3} \right)$ gilt, wobei $\{x\}$ den gebrochenen Teil von $x$ bezeichnet.
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a}{\sqrt{(a+b)(a+c)}} \leq \frac{3}{2}.
Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl und $t(n)$ die Anzahl der positiven Teiler von $n$. Bestimme alle $n$, für die $t(n)^3 = 4n$ gilt.
Sei $x$, $y$, $z$ die Längen der Winkelhalbierenden eines Dreiecks mit Umfang $6$. Zeigen Sie: $$ \frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{y^{2}} + \frac{1}{z^{2}} \geq 1 $$
Finde alle Funktionen $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, welche für alle $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ die Gleichung $$ f(f(a)+b) = 2 a + f(f(b)-a) $$ erfüllen.
Gegeben ist eine Funktion $f$ mit $f\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right)+f(x)=x+1$ für $x \in \mathbb{R} \backslash\{0,1\}$. Bestimme eine explizite Darstellung von $f$.

Sei $ABC$ ein Dreieck mit $AD$ als Seitenhalbierende auf $BC$ ($D \in BC$) und $E$ ein Punkt auf $AC$. Der Punkt $F$ sei der Schnittpunkt von $BE$ und $AD$. Zeigen Sie: Ist $\frac{BF}{FE} = 1 + \frac{BC}{AB}$, so ist $BE$ Winkelhalbierende des Winkels $\angle ABC$.

Seien $n$ und $k$ positive ganze Zahlen. In der Ebene sind $n$ Kreise ($n \geq 2$) so angeordnet, dass jeder Kreis jeden anderen Kreis an genau zwei Punkten schneidet, wobei alle Schnittpunkte paarweise verschieden sind. Jeder dieser Schnittpunkte wird mit einer von $n$ Farben gefärbt, wobei jede Farbe mindestens einmal vorkommt und auf jedem Kreis genau $k$ verschiedene Farben auftreten. Bestimme alle Paare $(n, k)$, für die eine solche Färbung existiert.
Beweise: Wenn $a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = 4^n \cdot 7$ mit $n, a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$, dann ist $a^2, b^2, c^2, d^2 \geq 4^{n-1}$.

Bestimme mit Begründung alle Funktionen $f: \mathbb{R}^{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+}$, welche für alle $x, y > 0$ die Gleichung
$$
2 f(x + y f(x)) = f(x) f(y)
$$
erfüllen.

Sei $ABC$ ein Dreieck mit $\overline{AB} + \overline{BC} = 3 \overline{AC}$. Der Inkreis mit Mittelpunkt $I$ berührt $AB$ in $D$ und $BC$ in $E$. Die Punkte $K$ und $L$ entstehen durch Spiegelung von $D$ und $E$ an $I$. Zeige, dass die Punkte $A$, $C$, $K$ und $L$ auf einem Kreis liegen.

Sei $R$ ein Rechteck mit $m$ Zeilen und $n$ Spalten, also insgesamt $mn$ Einheitsquadraten. Ein Pfad ist eine Folge von Einheitsquadraten, bei der benachbarte Quadrate eine gemeinsame Kante teilen. Jedes Quadrat wird entweder weiß oder schwarz gefärbt.
Sei $N$ die Anzahl der Färbungen, bei denen ein schwarzer Pfad von der linken zur rechten Kante existiert. Sei $M$ die Anzahl der Färbungen, bei denen es mindestens zwei disjunkte schwarze Pfade von links nach rechts gibt.
Zeigen Sie, dass $N^2 \geq M \cdot 2^{mn}$.

Bestimme alle Tupel positiver ganzer Zahlen ($a, b, x, y$) mit der Bedingung
$$
 x^{a} y^{b} = (x+y)^{2} + 1
$$

Gegeben sei ein gleichschenkliges Trapez $ABCD$ mit $AB \parallel CD$ und $\overline{BC} = \overline{AD}$. Die durch $B$ verlaufende Parallele zu $AD$ schneidet die zu $AD$ senkrechte Gerade durch $D$ im Punkt $X$. Zudem schneidet die durch $A$ verlaufende Parallele zu $BD$ die zu $BD$ senkrechte Gerade durch $D$ im Punkt $Y$. Zeigen Sie, dass $C$, $X$, $D$ und $Y$ konzyklisch sind.

Ein Quadrat sei in $n > 1$ Rechtecke zerlegt, wobei alle Rechtecke die Seiten des Quadrats parallel haben. Für jede Gerade, die parallel zu einer Quadratseite ist und das Quadratinnere schneidet, muss sie mindestens ein Rechteck im Inneren durchlaufen. Zeigen Sie, dass es unter diesen Bedingungen immer mindestens ein Rechteck gibt, das weder eine horizontale noch eine vertikale Kante mit dem Quadratrand gemeinsam hat.
Sei $p > 7$ eine Primzahl mit $p \equiv 1 \pmod{6}$. Definiere $m = 2^p - 1$. Zeige, dass $2^{m-1} - 1$ durch $127m$ teilbar ist.

Sei $ABCD$ eine Raute mit spitzen Winkel bei $A$. Auf $AC$ und $BC$ liegen Punkte $M$ und $N$ mit $|DM| = |MN|$. $P$ sei der Schnittpunkt von $AC$ und $DN$, und $R$ der Schnittpunkt von $AB$ und $DM$. Zeige: $|RP| = |PD|$.

Es liegen 2009 Karten in einer Reihe vor, nummeriert von $1$ bis $2009$, wobei die Vorderseite weiß und die Rückseite schwarz ist. Spieler $A$ und $B$ ziehen abwechselnd, wobei $A$ beginnt. Ein Zug besteht darin, eine Karte $k$ ($k < 1969$) mit weißer Vorderseite auszuwählen und die Karten $k$ bis $k+40$ umzudrehen. Der Spieler, der den letzten Zug ausführen kann, gewinnt. a) Muss das Spiel unbedingt enden? b) Welcher Spieler hat eine Gewinnstrategie?

Sei $\mathbb{Q}^{+}$ die Menge der positiven rationalen Zahlen. Eine Funktion $f: \mathbb{Q}^{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}^{+}$ werde als elastisch bezeichnet, wenn für alle $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}^{+}$ gilt:
$$
 f(a) + f(b) \geq 4 f(a + b).
$$

a. Zeigen Sie: Ist $f$ elastisch und $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}^{+}$, so folgt $f(a) + f(b) + f(c) \geq 8 f(a + b + c)$.

b. Existiert eine elastische Funktion $f$ sowie $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}^{+}$ mit $f(a) + f(b) + f(c) < 9 f(a + b + c)$?

Ein reguläres $n$-Eck sei so bezeichnet, dass Ecke $i$ mit Kante $i$ verbunden ist ($1 \leq i \leq n$). Die Ecken seien durch nichtnegative ganze Zahlen $e_{i}$ und die Kanten durch nichtnegative ganze Zahlen $k_{i}$ belegt, wobei gilt: (1) Die Folgen $(e_{1}, e_{2}, \ldots, e_{n})$ und $(k_{1}, k_{2}, \ldots, k_{n})$ sind zyklische Permutationen voneinander. (2) Für alle $i$ mit $1 \leq i \leq n$ ist $k_{i} = |e_{i+1} - e_{i}|$ mit $e_{n+1} = e_{1}$. a) Zeigen Sie, dass für $n \geq 3$ nichttriviale Lösungen existieren. b) Für jede positive ganze Zahl $m$ finden Sie die kleinste Zahl $n$, sodass in $(e_{1}, \ldots, e_{n})$ und $(k_{1}, \ldots, k_{n})$ alle Zahlen von $0$ bis $m$ vorkommen.

Gegeben seien neun verschiedene positive ganze Zahlen $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{9}$. Das Polynom $P(n) = \prod_{i=1}^{9} (n + a_i)$ sei definiert. Zeigen Sie, dass eine ganze Zahl $N$ existiert, sodass für alle $n \geq N$ der Wert $P(n)$ durch mindestens eine Primzahl $p > 20$ teilbar ist.

Gegeben sei ein $m \times n$-Gitter, wobei $m, n \geq 4$ ganze Zahlen sind. Ein geschlossener, nicht-selbstüberschneidender Weg $P$ durchlaufe alle $(m-1)(n-1)$ inneren Ecken, ohne eine äußere Ecke zu nutzen. Es bezeichne $A$ die Anzahl der inneren Ecken, an denen $P$ gerade verläuft, $B$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, von denen $P$ genau zwei parallele Seiten nutzt, und $C$ die Anzahl der Gitterquadrate, von denen $P$ keine Seite nutzt. Zeige: $A = B - C + m + n - 1$.

Zwei konzentrische Kreise mit Radien $r_{1}=13$ und $r_{2}=8$ liegen in der Ebene. $AB$ ist ein Durchmesser des äußeren Kreises, und $BC$ ist eine Sehne, die den inneren Kreis tangiert. Bestimme die Länge der Strecke $AD$.

Sei $n$ eine positive ganze Zahl. Betrachte disjunkte Paare $(a, b)$ mit $a, b \in \{1,2, \ldots, n\}$, wobei $a \neq b$ und $a + b \leq n$. Man bestimme die maximale Anzahl solcher Paare, bei denen alle Paarsummen eindeutig sind.

Sei $a_{1} \leqslant a_{2} \leqslant \ldots$ eine monoton wachsende Folge positiver ganzer Zahlen. Eine Zahl $n \in \mathbb{N}$ wird verlässlich genannt, falls es ein $i \in \mathbb{N}$ gibt mit $n = \frac{i}{a_i}$. Zeigen Sie: Ist 2013 verlässlich, so auch 20.

Sei $ABC$ ein spitzwinkliges Dreieck mit $AB \neq AC$. Die Punkte $D$ und $E$ seien die Mittelpunkte von $AB$ und $AC$, jeweils. Die Umkreise von $BCD$ und $BCE$ schneiden den Umkreis von $ADE$ in weiteren Punkten $P$ und $Q$. Zeigen Sie, dass $AP = AQ$.
Bestimme alle positiven ganzen Zahlen $m$, so dass die rekursive Folge $a_{0} = \frac{2m+1}{2}$, $a_{k+1} = a_{k} \left\lfloor a_{k} \right\rfloor$ mindestens einen ganzzahligen Term enthält.

Es seien $k$ und $n$ positive ganze Zahlen mit $n > k$. Ein Binärstring der Länge $n$ besteht aus $n$ Zeichen, die entweder 0 oder 1 sind. Anja wählt einen solchen String und schreibt alle Strings der Länge $n$ an die Tafel, die sich von ihrem ausgewählten String in genau $k$ Positionen unterscheiden. Bernhard tritt später ein und wird von Anja über $k$ informiert. Er möchte das ursprünglich ausgewählte Binärstring bestimmen. Wie viele verschiedene Strings muss Bernhard im schlimmsten Fall mindestens überprüfen, um das richtige mit Sicherheit zu identifizieren?

Gegeben sei eine positive ganze Zahl $d$ und eine surjektive, injektive Abzählung $\left(a_{i}\right)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ der positiven ganzen Zahlen. Es gelte ferner $\left|a_{i+1} - a_{i}\right| \leq 2d$ für alle $i > N$, wobei $N = 10^{100}$. Zeigen Sie, dass unendlich viele $j$ existieren mit $\left|a_{j} - j\right| < d$.

Sei $\mathbb{Q}^{+}$ die Menge aller positiven rationalen Zahlen. Bestimme alle Funktionen $f: \mathbb{Q}^{+} \rightarrow \mathbb{Q}^{+}$, welche für alle $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}^{+}$ die Gleichung
$$
f\left(x^{2} f(y)^{2}\right) = f\left(x^{2}\right) \cdot f(y)
$$
erfüllen.

Sei $n = 2019$, und seien $r_{1}, r_{2}, \ldots, r_{n} \in \mathbb{R}$ mit $\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i = 0$ und $\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i^2 = 1$. Definiere $a = \min \{ r_i \mid i = 1, 2, \ldots, n \}$ und $b = \max \{ r_i \mid i = 1, 2, \ldots, n \}$. Zeige, dass $ab \leq \frac{-1}{n}$.
Existiert eine Menge $M$ aus positiven ganzen Zahlen, sodass jede positive rationale Zahl $r < 1$ eindeutig als Summe von Kehrwerten einer endlichen Teilmenge von $M$ dargestellt werden kann?
Zeigen Sie, dass für jede nichtnegative ganze Zahl $z$ ein eindeutiges geordnetes Paar $(m, n)$ positiver ganzer Zahlen existiert mit $2 z = (m+n)^2 - m - 3 n$.

Sei $ABC$ ein gleichschenkliges Dreieck mit $\overline{BC}=\overline{CA}$. Ein Punkt $D$ liege innerhalb der Seite $AB$ mit $\overline{AD}<\overline{DB}$. Auf $BC$ und $CA$ seien Punkte $P$ und $Q$ so gewählt, dass $\angle DPB=\angle AQD=90^\circ$. Die Mittelsenkrechte von $PQ$ schneide $CQ$ in $E$, und die Umkreise von $ABC$ und $QPC$ schneiden sich in $C$ und einem weiteren Punkt $F$. Zeigen Sie: Wenn $P, E$ und $F$ auf einer Geraden liegen, dann ist $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.

Sei $m$ eine positive ganze Zahl und $A$ eine Teilmenge von $\{0,1,2, \ldots, 5^{m}\}$ mit $\lvert A \rvert = 4m+1$. Zeigen Sie, dass es Elemente $a, b, c \in A$ mit $a < b < c$ und $2a + c > 3b$ gibt.

Given a triangle $AB\Gamma$ where $AB < A\Gamma$, let $I$ be the incenter. If the angle bisector $A\Delta$ intersects the circumcircle $C$ of triangle $B\Gamma$ again at a point $N$ ($N \neq I$), determine:
(i) the angles of triangle $B\Gamma N$ in terms of the angles of triangle $AB\Gamma$,
(ii) the center of the circle $C$.

Given triangle $AB\Gamma$ with $\hat{A} = 105^\circ$ and $\hat{\Gamma} = \frac{1}{4} \hat{B}$.

α. Find the measures of the angles $\hat{B}$ and $\hat{\Gamma}$.

β. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $AB\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be the point diametrically opposite $B$. Show that the perpendicular distance from $\Gamma$ to the line $B\Delta$ is $\frac{1}{4} B\Delta$.

Given a circular ring with outer radius $R$ and inner radius $R - 2r$, where $R = 11r$, find the maximum number of circles of radius $r$ that can be placed inside the ring such that each is tangent to both the inner and outer boundary of the ring and no two overlap. (It is given that $9.94 < \sqrt{99} < 9.95$)

\text{Two tangent circles with centers } K_1 \text{ and } K_2 \text{ and radii } r_1 \text{ and } r_2 \text{ are also tangent to the sides of the rectangle } AB\Gamma\Delta, \text{ where } AB = a \text{ and } B\Gamma = b.\text{ (i) Determine } a \text{ and } b \text{ in terms of } r_1 \text{ and } r_2.\text{ (ii) If the common internal tangent of the circles passes through vertex } \Delta, \text{ find } \frac{r_1}{r_2} \text{ and the length of } \Delta K.
Find all integers $ n $ such that $ \frac{9n^2 + 31}{n^2 + 7} $ is an integer.

Let triangle $\Gamma AB$ be given with circumcenter $O$, and let $A_1, B_1, \Gamma_1$ be the midpoints of $\Gamma B, A\Gamma$, and $AB$, respectively. Define points $A_2, B_2, \Gamma_2$ such that $\overrightarrow{OA_2} = k \cdot \overrightarrow{OA_1}$, $\overrightarrow{OB_2} = k \cdot \overrightarrow{OB_1}$, and $\overrightarrow{O\Gamma_2} = k \cdot \overrightarrow{O\Gamma_1}$, where $k > 0$. Prove that the lines $AA_2, BB_2, \Gamma\Gamma_2$ are concurrent.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a scalene triangle with $AB < AC$, with circumcircle $\Gamma$. A circle centered at $A$ with radius $AB$ intersects $BC$ at $E$ and $\Gamma$ at $F$. The line $EF$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at $D$ and $AC$ at $M$. The line $AD$ intersects $BC$ at $K$. The circumcircle of $\triangle BKD$ meets $AB$ again at $L$. Show that $K, L, M$ are collinear and that this line is parallel to $BF$.
\text{Find all integer solutions } (x, y) \text{ such that } x^3 y^2 (2y - x) + 36 = x^2 y^4.
Let $A$ be a finite set of positive real numbers. Define $B = \left\{\frac{a}{b}: a, b \in A\right\}$ and $C = \left\{ab: a, b \in A\right\}$. Prove that $|A| \cdot |B| \le |C|^2$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$, inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$ centered at $O$. Extending the altitude $AD$ beyond $D$, it intersects $\Gamma$ again at $E$. Let $\mu$ be the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, and let it intersect $AD$ at point $L$. If $BL$ intersects $AC$ at $M$ and $\Gamma$ at $N$, and if $EN$ intersects $\mu$ at $Z$, prove that:
$$
MZ \perp BC \Leftrightarrow (CA = CB \text{ or } Z \equiv O).
$$
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a + b + c = 12$. Show that $$ \frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{c} + \frac{c}{a} + 3 \ge \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + \sqrt{c}. $$ Determine when equality holds.

Let $\triangle AB\Gamma$ be an acute-angled triangle where $AB < A\Gamma$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $B\Gamma$. A point $\Delta$ is selected on $AB$ such that the intersection point $E$ of $\Gamma\Delta$ and $AM$ satisfies $A\Delta = \Delta E$. Prove that the length $AB$ is equal to $\Gamma E$.

Let triangle $ABC$, with $AB < AC$, be inscribed in a circle $c(O, R)$. Let $c_1(B, AB)$ intersect $AC$ at $K$ and $c$ at $E$. The intersection of $KE$ with $c$ is $F$. Let $BO$ meet $KE$ at $L$ and $AC$ at $M$, and let $AE$ meet $BF$ at $D$. Show that $DLMF$ and $BDKME$ are cyclic.

Prove that
$$
\left(x+2y+\frac{2}{x+1}\right)\left(y+2x+\frac{2}{y+1}\right) \ge 16,
$$
for all positive real numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $xy \ge 1$.

Let $A = abcd = a \cdot 1000 + b \cdot 100 + c \cdot 10 + d$ be a four-digit positive integer with $a \ge 7$ and $a > b > c > d > 0$. Define $B = \overline{dcba} = d \cdot 1000 + c \cdot 100 + b \cdot 10 + a$. If the sum $A + B$ results in a number with all digits being odd, find all such values of $A$.

Let $G$ be a graph where vertices represent competitors and an edge connects two competitors if they are friends. A cycle $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ ($n \ge 3$) is called a weekly-friendly cycle if $A_i$ is not adjacent to $A_{i+1}$ for all $i$ ($A_{n+1} = A_1$), and no other pair of vertices in the cycle is non-adjacent.

Given that for any vertex $C$ and any weekly-friendly cycle $\mathcal{A}$ not containing $C$, the set of vertices in $\mathcal{A}$ not adjacent to $C$ has size at most one, prove that the graph $G$ can be partitioned into at most three cliques.
\text{Find all positive integer solutions } (x, y, z) \text{ to the equation: } \frac{1}{x} + 2\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) - 4\left(\frac{1}{z}\right) = 1

Let $(x_n)$, $n \ge 1$, be a sequence of real numbers with $x_1 = 1$, defined recursively by $x_{n+1} =  rac{3x_n}{2} +  rac{\sqrt{5x_n^2 - 4}}{2}$, for $n=1,2,3,...$
a. Prove that all terms of the sequence are natural numbers.


β. Determine if there exists a term of the sequence divisible by $2011$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $M$ as the midpoint of side $BC$. A parallelogram $BCDE$ is constructed outside the triangle with $BE \parallel AM$ and $BE = AM / 2$. Show that the line segment $EM$ intersects the segment $AD$ at its midpoint.

Let $P(x) = a x^3 + (b - a) x^2 - (c + b) x + c$, $Q(x) = x^4 + (b - 1) x^3 + (a - b) x^2 - (c + a) x + c$ be polynomials in $x$, where $a, b, c$ are nonzero real numbers and $b > 0$. If the cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has three distinct real roots $x_0, x_1, x_2$, which are also shared with the quartic polynomial $Q(x)$, then:
(a) Prove that: $abc > 28$.
(b) If $a, b, c$ are nonzero integers with $b > 0$, find all possible combinations of such values.
Find all nonnegative integers $m, n$ with $m \ge n$ such that $(m+n)^3$ divides $2n(3m^2 + n^2) + 8$.

Let $AB\Gamma$ be an acute triangle with $AB < A\Gamma$ and let $O$ be its circumcenter. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $AB\Gamma$, and let $O_1$ be the circumcenter of triangle $BH\Gamma$. Prove that the quadrilateral $AHO_1O$ is a parallelogram.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB \le AC$ and $\omega$ its circumcircle. The perpendicular from $A$ to the tangent of $\omega$ at $C$ intersects the tangent at point $D$.

(a) If $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = AC$, prove that: $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$.

(b) If $CD = \frac{BC}{2}$, prove that $ABC$ is isosceles.

Let triangle $AB\Gamma$ be isosceles and acute with $AB = A\Gamma$. Let $\Delta$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $\Gamma$ to $AB$. The circle centered at $\Gamma$ with radius $\Gamma\Delta$ intersects $A\Gamma$ at point $K$ and its extension at point $Z$. This circle also intersects the circle centered at $B$ with radius $B\Delta$ at point $E$. The segment $\Delta Z$ intersects the circle centered at $B$ at point $M$. Prove that

a. $Z\hat{\Delta}E = 45^\circ$

b. The points $E$, $M$, and $K$ lie on a straight line.

c. The lines $BM$ and $E\Gamma$ are parallel.

Let $AB\Gamma\Delta$ ($A\Delta\parallel B\Gamma$) be a right trapezium with $\angle A = \angle B = 90^\circ$ and $A\Delta < B\Gamma$. Let $E$ be the intersection of the legs $AB$ and $\Gamma\Delta$, and let $Z$ be the reflection of $A$ over $B\Gamma$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $EZ$. Given that $\Gamma M \perp \Delta Z$, prove that $Z\Gamma \perp \Gamma E$.

Let $ABCD$ be a square of side $\alpha$. On side $AD$, points $E$ and $Z$ are placed such that $DE = \frac{\alpha}{3}$ and $AZ = \frac{\alpha}{4}$. If the lines $BZ$ and $CE$ intersect at point $H$, express the area of triangle $BC H$ as a function of $\alpha$.

Given triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$ inscribed in a circle centered at $O$, let $G$ be the centroid and $D, E, F$ the feet of the perpendiculars from $A, B, C$. If the lines $AG$ and $GD$ meet the circle again at $M$ and $N$, respectively, show that $F, E, M, N$ lie on a circle.
Show that $\frac{4n!}{n!\ 2n!}$ is an integer for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and divisible by $2^{n+1}$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be inscribed in a circle centered at $O$ with radius $R$, and let $F$ be a point on segment $AB$ such that $AF < \frac{1}{2} AB$. Let $c_1$ be the circle centered at $F$ with radius $FA$. Suppose $c_1$ intersects the ray $OA$ at a point $A' \ne A$ and intersects the circumcircle $c$ of triangle $ABC$ at a point $K$. Prove that the points $B$, $K$, $F$, $A'$, and $O$ lie on a single circle.
Determine all integer solutions $(a, b, c)$, where $a > 0 > b > c$ and $a + b + c = 0$, such that the expression $2017 - a^3b - b^3c - c^3a$ is the square of an integer.

Let $ p $ be a prime number greater than or equal to 2. Two players, A and B, take turns writing a digit (0 through 9) in one of $ p $ adjacent empty boxes. Player A moves first and the game ends when all boxes are filled, forming a $ p $-digit number $ M $ (which may have leading zeros). A wins if $ M $ is divisible by $ p $, and B wins otherwise. Show that A has a strategy to guarantee a win.

Let $\triangle AB\Gamma$ be a triangle with $AB > A\Gamma$. Place point $\Delta$ on $AB$ such that $\Delta B = \Gamma A$. Construct a circle $\gamma$ through $\Delta$ that is tangent to $A\Gamma$ at $A$. The circumcircle $\omega$ of $\triangle AB\Gamma$ intersects $\gamma$ again at $E$. Show that $E$ lies at the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of $B\Gamma$ and $A\Delta$.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle of side length $k$ cm. The triangle is subdivided into $k^2$ smaller equilateral triangles of side length $1$ cm by drawing lines parallel to the sides. Each small triangle contains a distinct positive integer from $1$ to $k^2$. A regular hexagon of side $1$ cm is formed using the vertices of the grid. The value of a hexagon is defined as the sum of the numbers in its six constituent small triangles. Determine the maximum total value of all such hexagons as a function of $k$.

Let $\{\alpha_i\}_{i=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of integers with $0 \le \alpha_i \le i$ for all $i$. Suppose for every $\kappa \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, the identity $\sum_{i=0}^{\kappa} \binom{\kappa}{\alpha_i} = 2^\kappa$ holds. Prove that for all $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$, there exists some $i$ such that $\alpha_i = n$.

In triangle $ABC$ with $AB < AC$, the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ meets $AB$ and $AC$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $ABC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $BC$ and $PQ$. Prove that the intersection of $HM$ and $AN$ lies on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

Let $n > 1$, a positive integer. In an $n \times n$ grid, each cell contains an integer that satisfies:

a. Each entry is congruent to $1$ modulo $n$.

b. The sum of the entries in each row and each column is congruent to $n$ modulo $n^2$.

Let $P_i$ be the product of the entries in the $i^\text{th}$ row, and $Q_j$ be the product of the entries in the $j^\text{th}$ column. Prove that $P_1 + P_2 + \dots + P_n$ and $Q_1 + Q_2 + \dots + Q_n$ are congruent modulo $n^4$.

Let $P$ be an interior point of an equilateral triangle with height $1$. Let the perpendicular distances from $P$ to the three sides be $a$, $b$, and $c$. Show that:
$$
 a^2 + b^2 + c^2 \geq a^3 + b^3 + c^3 + 6abc.
$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $BE$ and $CF$ be the altitudes of $\triangle ABC$. The line $EF$ intersects $BC$ at point $G$.

a. Determine the angles of triangle $EDF$ in terms of angle $\angle A$.

b. Determine the angle $BGD$ in terms of angles $\angle B$ and $\angle C$.

\text{(A) Let } P(x) = x^3 - kx + 2. \text{ Given that } 2 \text{ is a root of } P(x), \text{ find the real number } k. \text{ Using this value of } k, \text{ factor } P(x) \text{ into two polynomials with integer coefficients.}\\\text{(B) Given that } a, b \text{ are positive real numbers such that } 2a + b + \frac{4}{ab} = 10, \text{ determine the maximum possible value of } a.

Let $\Gamma AB$ be an isosceles triangle with $\hat{\Gamma} = \hat{B}$, and a point $\Delta$ inside the triangle such that $\angle \Delta B \Gamma = 30^\circ$, $\angle \Delta B A = 50^\circ$, and $\angle B \Gamma \Delta = 55^\circ$.

a. Show that $\hat{B} = \hat{\Gamma} = 80^\circ$.

b. Determine the measure of $\angle \Delta A \Gamma$.

Let $n > 4$ be a positive integer divisible by $4$. Define $A_n$ as the sum of all odd positive divisors of $n$, and $B_n$ as the sum of all even positive divisors of $n$ excluding $n$ itself. Determine the minimal possible value of $f(n) = B_n - 2A_n$, and find all such $n$ that yield this value.

Given a $3n \times 3n$ chessboard where the coloring is such that every third diagonal starting from the top-left corner is black and the rest are white, we define a move as selecting a $2 \times 2$ subgrid and applying the transformation: white $\to$ orange, orange $\to$ black, black $\to$ white. Prove:
a) It is impossible to reach a fully inverted coloring (black $\leftrightarrow$ white) for $n = 3$.
b) It is possible to reach such an inversion for $n = 2$.

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy the inequality
$$
\quad f(a + b)f(a - b) \geq f(a)^2 - f(b)^2
$$
for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose there exist real numbers $a_0, b_0$ such that
$$
\quad f(a_0 + b_0)f(a_0 - b_0) > f(a_0)^2 - f(b_0)^2.
$$
Prove that $f(x) \geq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ or $f(x) \leq 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Let triangle $AB\Gamma$ have circumcircle $\omega(O, R)$. A circle $\gamma$ passes through $O$ and $B$ and is tangent to $AB$ at $B$. A second circle intersects $\omega$ at $P \neq B$. A third circle passes through $P$ and $\Gamma$ and is tangent to $A\Gamma$ at $\Gamma$, intersecting $\gamma$ at $M \neq P$. Show that $MP = M\Gamma$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$. Let $M_A, M_B, M_C$ be the midpoints of $BC, CA, AB$, and $H_A, H_B, H_C$ the feet of the altitudes from $A, B, C$. Let $\ell_b$ be the tangent to the circumcircle at $B$, and $\ell'_b$ its reflection in $BI$. Let $P_B$ be the intersection of $M_A M_C$ with $\ell_b$, and $Q_B$ the intersection of $H_A H_C$ with $\ell'_b$. Define $\ell_c, \ell'_c, P_C, Q_C$ analogously. If $R = P_B Q_B \cap P_C Q_C$, show that $RB = RC$.
\frac{abc(a + b + c + \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2})}{(a^2 + b^2 + c^2)(ab + bc + ca)} \le \frac{3 + \sqrt{3}}{9},

Let the internal angle bisectors of $\angle A$, $\angle B$, and $\angle C$ in triangle $ABC$ meet the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ again at points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ respectively. Prove that the sum of the lengths $AP + BQ + CR$ is greater than the perimeter of triangle $ABC$.
Show that the sum $T = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{2k + 1}$ is never an integer for any $n \ge 1$.

\text{Let triangle ABC be given. On each side of ABC, an isosceles triangle is constructed outwardly such that ABX, BCY and CAZ are similar, with XA = XB, YB = YC and ZC = ZA. Show that the lines AY, BZ, and CX meet at a single point.}

Let $F$ be a function defined on the positive reals with the following properties: (1) $F(1) = 1$, (2) $F(x + 1) = x F(x)$, and (3) $F(x) = 10^{h(x)}$, where $h(x)$ is a function defined on the reals satisfying $$h(ty + (1-t)z) \leq t h(y) + (1-t) h(z)$$ for all $y$ and $z$ and for $0 \leq t \leq 1$.

a. Prove that $t [h(n) - h(n-1)] \leq h(n+t) - h(n) \leq t [h(n+1) - h(n)]$ where $n$ is an integer and $0 \leq t \leq 1$.

b. Prove that $\frac{4}{3} \leq F\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \leq \frac{4}{3} \sqrt{2}$.

Let $G$ be a complete graph with $n$ vertices, and let each edge be assigned a colour from a set of $k$ distinct colours.

a. For $n = 6$ and $k = 3$, demonstrate that it is possible to assign the colours such that no monochromatic cycle exists.

b. Show that for any integer $k \ge 1$, if $n \ge 2k+1$, then any such edge colouring will contain at least one monochromatic cycle.

Let quadrilateral $ABCD$ have $AB \parallel CD$ with $AB > CD$, and $AD > BC$. Prove that
i. $\angle ABC > \angle BAD$,
ii. the diagonal $AC$ is longer than diagonal $BD$.

Let there be $n$ ($n \ge 3$) subjects, each with a test paper taken by students. In every subject, precisely three students achieve the top score, and for any pair of subjects, there is exactly one student who achieves the top score in both. Find the smallest value of $n$ for which the conditions ensure that there is exactly one student who achieves the top score in all $n$ subjects.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$, with side lengths satisfying $AB > AC > BC$. Let $D$ be a point on the minor arc $BC$ (not containing $A$) of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, with $AD$ not being a diameter. Let $E$ and $F$ lie on segment $AD$ such that $OE \perp AB$ and $OF \perp AC$. Let $P$ be the intersection of lines $BE$ and $CF$. If $PB = PC + PO$, show that $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$.
Determine all integers $ n \ge 3 $ for which there exists a polygon with $ n $ vertices, all lying at integer coordinates, and each side of the polygon has the same length.

\text{Given triangle } ABC \text{ with } BC > AB > AC, \text{ let } D \text{ lie on } BC \text{ and } E \text{ lie on the extension of } BA \text{ beyond } A \text{ such that } BD = BE = AC. \text{ Let } P \text{ be on } AC \text{ such that points } E, B, D, P \text{ lie on a circle, and let } Q \text{ be the second intersection of } BP \text{ with the circumcircle of } \triangle ABC. \text{ Show that } AQ + CQ = BP.
\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{x}{y+z} \ge \frac{3}{2}.

\triangle ABC is isosceles with $AB = AC$. Let $D$ lie on the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $\angle ABD < 90^\circ$. Let $E$ be the point on $BD$ such that $AE \perp BD$. Prove that $BE = ED + DC$.

Determine the largest real $K$ such that for all positive real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfying $a^2 > 4bc$, the inequality
$$
(a^2 - 4bc)^2 > K(2b^2 - ac)(2c^2 - ab)
$$
holds. Justify your result.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $M$ the midpoint of $AC$. A point $D$ lies on $AB$, and the lines $BM$ and $CD$ intersect at $O$, where $AB = CO$. A point $E$ is on $AC$ such that $DE$ is parallel to $BM$. Show that $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$ is equivalent to the concyclicity of $A$, $D$, $O$, and $M$.

Let $n \ge 2$ and $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n, b_{n+1}$ be positive numbers in arithmetic progression. Prove that
$$
\sum_{k=2}^{n} \frac{1}{b_k^2} \le \frac{n-1}{2} \cdot \frac{b_1 b_n + b_2 b_{n+1}}{b_1 b_2 b_n b_{n+1}}
$$
and find when equality occurs.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. We define $n$ to be *good* if there exist positive integers $x$ and $y$ such that $x + y = n$ and $xy$ is divisible by $n$. If $x$ and $y$ can be chosen to differ, then $n$ is *very good*. For example, $9$ is good because $3 + 6 = 9$ and $3 \times 6$ is divisible by $9$.

a. Given that $2003$ is a prime, show that $2003$ is not good.

b. Is $2002$ good?

c. Determine all positive integers $n$ that are good but not very good, and justify your answer.

Let $f(n)$ count the number of $2n$-digit numbers where $n$ digits are $1$ and $n$ digits are $2$. Let $g(n)$ count the number of $n$-digit numbers where each digit is in $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and the count of $1$'s equals the count of $2$'s. Prove that $f(n) = g(n)$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with altitude $AD$ from $A$ to side $BC$. Using $AD$ as the diameter, construct a circle intersecting $AB$ and $AC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $EF$ intersect $AD$ at $G$, and extend $AD$ to intersect the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at point $H$. Prove that $AG \cdot AH = AD^2$.

In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $M$ denote the intersection of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Suppose the angle bisector of $\angle ACD$ intersects the extension of $AB$ at $K$. Given that $MA \cdot (MC + CD) = MB \cdot MD$, prove that $\angle BKC = \angle CDB$.

Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{b+c} + \frac{1}{c+a} + \frac{1}{a+b} \ge \frac{9}{2(a+b+c)}
$$
Using the result above, prove that for any $n > 1$,
$$
\frac{a^n}{b+c} + \frac{b^n}{c+a} + \frac{c^n}{a+b} \ge \frac{(a+b+c)^{n-1}}{2 \cdot 3^{n-2}}
$$
Determine all integer pairs $(x, y)$ satisfying $3(x^2 - xy + y^2) = 7(x + y)$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be given with circumradius $R$. Let the side lengths be $AB = c$, $BC = a$, and $CA = b$. Let $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ be circles passing through $C$ and tangent to $AB$ at $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $\omega$ be a circle with radius $r$, externally tangent to $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$, and tangent to the line $AB$.

a. Express $r$ in terms of $a, b, c$, and $R$.

b. If $r = \frac{R}{4}$, find $\angle C$.

Let $D$ be a point on side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$ satisfying $AB + BD = AC + CD$. Suppose the incircle of triangle $ABC$ intersects segment $AD$ at two points $X$ and $Y$, with $X$ closer to $A$. Let $E$ denote the point where the incircle touches $BC$. Prove that
(i) $EY$ is perpendicular to $AD$,
(ii) the segment $XD$ is twice the length of $IA'$, where $I$ is the incenter of triangle $ABC$ and $A'$ is the midpoint of side $BC$.
Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $AB = AD + BC$. Prove that the point where the angle bisectors of $\angle ADC$ and $\angle BCD$ meet lies on segment $AB$.

Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be real numbers such that
(i) $\sin x \cos y + |\cos x \sin y| = \sin x |\cos x| + |\sin y \cos y|$,
(ii) $\tan z$ and $\cot z$ are defined.
Find the minimum value of $(\tan z - \sin x)^2 + (\cot z - \cos y)^2$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with sides $BC = a$, $CA = b$, and $AB = c$. Prove that
$$
\frac{\cos A}{a^3} + \frac{\cos B}{b^3} + \frac{\cos C}{c^3} \ge \frac{3}{2abc}.
$$

In an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $AB = AC$, let the incircle centred at $O$ touch $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $K$, $L$, and $M$ respectively. Let $N$ be the intersection of $OL$ with $KM$, and define $Q$ as the intersection of $BN$ with $CA$. Let $P$ be the perpendicular foot from $A$ to $BQ$, and suppose that $BP = AP + 2PQ$. Find the possible value(s) of $\frac{AB}{BC}$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle C = 90^\circ$. Let $D$ lie on $AB$ such that $CD \perp AB$. The circumcircle of $\triangle BCD$ is denoted by $\omega$. There is a circle $\omega_1$ inside $\triangle ACD$ that is tangent to $AC$ and $AD$ at $N$ and $M$ respectively, and also tangent to $\omega$.
(i) Prove the identity $BD \cdot CN + BC \cdot DM = CD \cdot BM$.
(ii) Prove that $BM = BC$.
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $xyz = 1$. Show that $$\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{1}{x^2(y+z)} \ge \frac{3}{2}.$$

Let $O$ be the center of the $A$-excircle of $\triangle ABC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and let $P$ be the point where the line $MO$ intersects $BC$. If $\angle BAC = 2\angle ACB$, prove that $AB = BP$.
Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, with $AB > AC$. A line through $I$ perpendicular to $AI$ intersects the extension of $BC$ at point $P$. Prove that $IP^2 = BP \cdot CP$.

In triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$. A circle through $A$ is tangent to $BC$ at $M$, and intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$ respectively. If points $B, C, D, E$ lie on a circle, prove that $AB = AC$.

Let $a_1 = 4$ and $a_{n+1} - a_n \ge n + 2$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{2010} \frac{1}{a_k} < \frac{3}{2}.
$$

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ and $w$ be real numbers such that $x, y, z, w \ge 1$. Prove that

a.  $xyzw(x+y+z+w-4)^4 \ge (x-1)(y-1)(z-1)(w-1)(x+y+z+w)^4$,

b.  $\dfrac{w}{x+y+z} + \dfrac{x}{y+z+w} + \dfrac{y}{z+w+x} + \dfrac{z}{w+x+y} \ge \dfrac{4}{3}$.
Determine a function $f : \mathbb{R}^{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}^{\ge 0}$ such that $f(2x + 1) - 4f(x) = 9$ for all $x \ge 0$.
Let $g$ be a function defined on nonzero real numbers such that for any nonzero $x$, $$\frac{2}{x}g(-x) + g\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) = x.$$ Determine $g(8)$.

Suppose $p$, $q$, $r$ are distinct nonzero real numbers. If the equations $p x^3 + q x + r = 0$, $q x^3 + r x + p = 0$, and $r x^3 + p x + q = 0$ share a common root, show that at least one of these equations has three real roots (not necessarily distinct).

Find all integer solutions $(a, b)$ such that
$$
(b^2 + 11a - 11b)^2 = a^3 b.
$$

\triangle ABC has area 1 and satisfies AB > AC. The angle bisector of \angle A intersects BC at D. Let C' be the reflection of C over line AD. If \triangle DBC' \sim \triangle ABC, determine AB when the perimeter of \triangle ABC is minimised.

Let $ k $ be a real number with $ -1 < k < 1 $. The intersection points of the line $ y = x + k $ and the parabola $ y = 1 - x^2 $ are labeled $ A $ and $ B $. Given a fixed point $ C = (1, 0) $, determine the maximum area of triangle $ ABC $.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $\angle ABC > \angle BCA$ and $\angle C \ge 30^\circ$. Let $D$ and $E$ be points on $AC$ and $AB$, respectively, such that $BD$ and $CE$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle ABC$ and $\angle BCA$. If $BD \cap CE = P$ and $PD = PE$, and the inradius of triangle $ABC$ is 1, find the maximum possible value of $BC$.

In triangle $ABC$, let $D$ lie on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$ such that $DE \parallel BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $P$ be a point such that $DP = DB$, $EP = EC$, and the segment $AP$ intersects $BC$ internally. Given that $\angle BPD = \angle CME$, prove that $\angle CPE = \angle BMD$.
Let $\triangle ABC$ have $\angle A = 54^\circ$ and $\angle C = 24^\circ$. A point $P$ lies on side $AC$ with $AP = BC$. Determine the measure of $\angle CBP$.

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Consider $n$ distinct circles in the plane with the property that any two intersect at two distinct points, and no three intersect at the same point. Initially, each intersection point has a coin. Players $X$ and $Y$ take turns removing a coin, starting with $X$, under the rule that no coin may be removed from the same circle as the one just removed by the opponent. The player who cannot move loses. For which values of $n$ does player $Y$ have a winning strategy?

\text{In triangle } ABC \text{ with integer side lengths, let } M \text{ be the midpoint of } BC. \text{ The incircle centered at } I \text{ touches } AB \text{ and } AC \text{ at } E \text{ and } F, \text{ respectively. } D \text{ is the foot of the perpendicular from } M \text{ onto } EF. \text{ Given that quadrilateral } ADMI \text{ is a parallelogram and the perimeter of } ABC \text{ is } 65, \text{ find the product } AB \times BC \times CA.

\text{In trapezoid } ABCD \text{ with } AB \parallel CD, M \text{ and } N \text{ are the midpoints of } AB \text{ and } CD \text{ respectively. Given that } AC = 6, BD = 8, \text{ and the distance between } M \text{ and } N \text{ is } 4, \text{ determine the area of } ABCD.
Let $ k $ be an integer. Suppose the quadratic $ kx^2 + (4k - 2)x + (4k - 7) = 0 $ has at least one integer solution. Determine the sum of all such $ k $.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcircle center $O$. Let $E = AC \cap BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the arcs $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, that do not contain any other vertices. Let $P = EO \cap MN$. Given $BC = 5$, $AC = 11$, $BD = 12$, and $AD = 10$, determine $\frac{MN}{NP}$.

Let the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ in triangle $ABC$ intersect $BC$ at $D$. Consider a circle $\Gamma$ passing through $A$ and tangent to $BC$ at $D$. This circle intersects $AB$ and $AC$ again at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $BF$ and $CE$ intersect $\Gamma$ again at $P$ and $Q$. The lines $AP$ and $AQ$ intersect $BC$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the segment $XY$ is half the length of $BC$.
Let $a_1 = 5$ and $a_{n+1} = a_n(a_n - 3) + 3$ for all $n \geq 1$. Show that $a_n > 3^{2^{n-1}}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Let $\{b_n\}$ be a sequence of integers such that for all positive integers $n$, the identity $b_n + b_{n+1} = 2b_{n+2}b_{n+3} + 2016$ holds. Determine all possible values of $b_1$ and $b_2$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral. Extend $AD$ and $CD$ beyond $D$ to points $P$ and $Q$ such that $AP = BC$ and $CQ = AB$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $PQ$. Prove that $\angle AMC = 90^\circ$.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $AB = AC$. A circle $\Gamma$ is tangent to line $AC$ at point $C$ and lies outside triangle $ABC$. A point $D$ is selected on $\Gamma$ so that the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$ is tangent from the inside to $\Gamma$. If segment $AD$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at $E$, show that line $BE$ is tangent to $\Gamma$.
Determine all integers $n \ge 3$ such that there exists a set of $n$ distinct points in the plane where every point is the circumcenter of some triangle defined by three of the points in the set.
Let $a$ be a real number. Consider the function $f(x) = \frac{1}{x-6} + \frac{1}{x-2} + \frac{a}{x-1}$ defined on $3 < x < 5$. If $f(x)$ has a maximum at $x = 4$, determine the value of $a$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be isosceles with $AB = AC$. The incircle $\Gamma$ is tangent to $AB$ at $F$ and to $AC$ at $E$, and its center is $I$. Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $AFE$. Suppose the external common tangents of $\Gamma$ and $\Omega$ meet at $P$, and one of these tangents is parallel to $AC$. Prove that $\angle PBI = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$ with $AD = AB$. A point $E$ lies on segment $CD$ such that $DE = BC$. The line $AE$ intersects $\Gamma$ again at $F$. Let $M$ be the intersection of $AC$ and $BF$. If $P$ is the reflection of $C$ across $M$, show that $PE \parallel BF$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ satisfy $AC = kAB$, with $k > 1$. If the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects $BC$ at $D$, and the circle on diameter $AC$ intersects the extension of $AD$ at $E$, find $\frac{AD}{AE}$ in terms of $k$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be acute with $BC > AB$. Suppose point $D$ lies on $AC$ such that $BD = BA$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. If the tangents from $D$ and $M$ to the circumcircle of $\triangle CDM$ meet at $E$, and line $BE$ intersects $AC$ at $F$, show that points $A$, $B$, $M$, and $F$ lie on a circle.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcircle $\Gamma$, and let $P$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$. Let $AP$ meet $BC$ at $D$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Let $E$ be the point such that $\angle AEB = 90^\circ$ and $\angle EBM = 90^\circ$. Prove that $AE = DE$.

Consider a square grid of size $n \times n$, where $n$ is an even number greater than or equal to 4. The grid is two-coloured in the standard checkerboard pattern. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are interior cells of opposite colours. Show that there exists a Hamiltonian path from $A$ to $B$ traversing every cell exactly once.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, with $G$ as its centroid and $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. Let $D$ lie on segment $GM$. A line through $D$ intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively, with $E, F \ne A$. Prove that
$$
[BEGF] + [CFGE] \ge \frac{4}{9}[ABC].
$$
Determine the condition for equality.
Let $n$ be an integer, and let $A$ be a subset of $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots, 5^n\}$ with $|A| = 4n+2$. Show that there are elements $a, b, c \in A$ such that $a < b < c$ and $c + 2a - 3b > 0$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle B$ acute. A circle is tangent to sides $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$. The diagonal $AC$ intersects the circle at points $M$ and $N$, with $M$ closer to $A$ than $N$. If the distances are $AM = 9$, $MN = 16$, and $NC = 2$, determine the area of $ABCD$.

In triangle $ABC$, with $AB < AC$, the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects $BC$ at $D$, and the external angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ intersects the extension of $BC$ at $E$. Given $EB = 2022$ and $BD$, $DC$ are integers, find the number of possible integer values for $BD$.

Let $c$ and $d$ be the two roots of the equation $x^{\frac{4}{3}} - 2022x^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2023 = 0$. If $r = c + 3c^{\frac{1}{3}}d^{\frac{2}{3}}$ and $s = d + 3c^{\frac{2}{3}}d^{\frac{1}{3}}$, find the value of $(r+s)^{\frac{1}{3}} + (r-s)^{\frac{1}{3}}$.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Suppose $\{a_n\}$ is defined recursively by $a_0 = 0$ and $a_n = P(a_{n-1})$ for $n \ge 1$. If there is some positive integer $k$ such that $a_k = 0$, prove that either $a_1 = 0$ or $a_2 = 0$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersecting at point $E$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on segment $AC$ such that the order of the points is $A$, $E$, $Q$, $P$, $C$. It is given that $BP$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and $DQ$ bisects $\angle ADC$. If $AE = 4$, $EQ = 2$, and $QP = 3$, determine the length of segment $PC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. Diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$. Let $F$ and $G$ be points on $AB$ and $CD$ such that $AF = 15$, $FB = 13$, $BE = 30$, $ED = 13$, $DG = 7.5$, and $GC = 6.5$. If $P$ is a point satisfying $PF \perp AB$ and $PG \perp CD$, determine the value of $\frac{PE}{PO}$.
Consider a set of $n$ binary strings of length 200. If any two binary strings in the set differ in at least 101 positions, is it possible that $n \ge 101$?

Let $P_1P_2\dots P_n$ be a convex polygon with $n \ge 4$. For each index $i$, define $g(i)$ as the largest angle formed at a vertex $P_j$ such that $\angle P_iP_jP_{i+1}$ is defined and $j \ne i, i+1$ (with $P_{n+1} = P_1$). Determine the minimal total $g(1) + g(2) + \dots + g(n)$ for any such polygon.

Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$ in acute triangle $\triangle ABC$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AM$. The circumcircle of triangle $\triangle ABD$ meets $BC$ again at a point $E$ distinct from $B$. Let $F$ be a point on segment $AE$ such that $FB = FC$. Show that $F$ lies at the midpoint of $AE$.

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezium with $AD \parallel BC$ and $AD > BC$. The side lengths satisfy $AB = CD$. A point $P$ exists in the plane such that the distances from $P$ to $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are $1$, $2$, $3$, and $4$ respectively. Determine the ratio $AD : BC$.

\text{Let square } ABCD \text{ contain a point } P \text{ where } \angle APD + \angle BPC = 180^\circ \text{ and } \angle BPC < 90^\circ. \text{ If } PB = 3 \text{ and } PC = 4, \text{ determine the length of side } BC.
In triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC = 75^\circ$ and $\angle BCA = 45^\circ$. Extend $BC$ to a point $T$ such that $CT = BC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AT$. Determine $\angle BMC$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB > AC$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $I$ be the incenter of the triangle. Drop a perpendicular from $I$ to $BC$, meeting it at $D$. Let $E$ be the second intersection point of the line through $A$ perpendicular to $BC$ with the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$. If $\angle MID = \angle C - \angle B$, show that $DE = DI$.

Let $a, b, c$ be positive integers, with $b$ and $c$ not exceeding $2023$, such that $a - b = 2c$ and $(a^2 + c^2)(b^2 + c^2)$ is divisible by $17^2$. How many ordered triples $(a, b, c)$ satisfy these conditions?

In triangle $ABC$, where $AB < AC$, let $AD$ be the internal angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ meeting $BC$ at $D$. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle passing through $A$ and $D$ that is tangent to $BC$ at $D$. Let $E$ be the second intersection of $\Gamma$ with $AB$, and let $F$ be the second point of intersection of the tangent to the circumcircle of $\triangle BDE$ at $D$ with $\Gamma$. If $P$ is the intersection of $EF$ and $AC$, show that $PD$ is perpendicular to $BC$.
Given an equilateral triangle $ABC$ and a point $P$ inside it such that $AP = 15$ and $BP = 8$, determine the maximum possible value of the total area of triangles $ABP$ and $BCP$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB = 5$, $AD = 17$, and $CD = 6$. Suppose the internal angle bisectors of $\angle DAB$ and $\angle CDA$ meet at the center point of segment $BC$. Determine the area of quadrilateral $ABCD$.
How many solutions exist for $\frac{\ln x}{\ln 3} = 3 \sin(3\pi x)$?

Let $b_{0}$ be an arbitrary real number and define $b_{i+1} = \left\lfloor b_{i} \right\rfloor \cdot (b_{i} - \left\lfloor b_{i} \right\rfloor)$ for all $i \geq 0$. Show that $b_{i} = b_{i+2}$ for sufficiently large $i$.

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ and $AB > CD$. Let points $K$ and $L$ be on $AB$ and $CD$ such that $\frac{AK}{KB} = \frac{DL}{LC}$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on $KL$ such that $\angle APB = \angle BCD$ and $\angle CQD = \angle ABC$. Show that $P$, $Q$, $B$, and $C$ lie on a circle.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle A < 90^\circ$ and $\angle C < \angle A$. A point $D$ lies on side $AC$ such that $BD = BA$. Suppose the incircle of triangle $ABC$ touches $AB$ and $AC$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively. If $J$ is the incenter of triangle $BCD$, prove that the line $KL$ intersects $AJ$ at its midpoint.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Two circles, one passing through $A$ and $D$, and the other passing through $B$ and $C$, are externally tangent at a point $P$ located inside $ABCD$. If
$$
\angle PAB + \angle PDC \leq 90^\circ \quad \text{ and } \quad \angle PBA + \angle PCD \leq 90^\circ,
$$
show that $AB + CD \geq BC + AD$.

Let $p > q > 1$ be relatively prime positive integers. Define the weight of an integer $c$, denoted by $w(c)$, to be the minimal value of $|x| + |y|$ such that there exist integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $p x + q y = c$.
An integer $c$ is said to be a local champion if $w(c) \geq w(c \pm p)$ and $w(c) \geq w(c \pm q)$.
Determine all such local champions and the total number of them.

Let $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ be such that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, the inequality
$$
 f(a+b) \geq f(a) + f(f(b)) - 1
$$
holds. Determine all possible values of $f(2007)$.

Let $n > 1$ be an integer. Find all binary sequences $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n^{2}+n}$ such that the sum of any $n$ consecutive terms in the first $n^{2}-n+1$ blocks is strictly less than the sum of the next $n$ consecutive terms in that block.

Given a unit square partitioned into $n>1$ rectangles with sides parallel to the square’s sides, suppose every line parallel to a side of the square that intersects the square’s interior also intersects the interior of one of the rectangles. Show that at least one rectangle lies entirely in the interior of the square.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be isosceles with $AB = AC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $X$ be a variable point on the shorter arc $AM$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABM$. Let $T$ be a point in the interior of $\angle BMA$ such that $TX = BX$ and $\angle TMX = 90^\circ$. Prove that the difference $\angle MTB - \angle CTM$ is constant with respect to the position of $X$.

Find the minimal positive real number $k$ such that the following condition holds for any convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with points $A_{1}, B_{1}, C_{1}, D_{1}$ on $AB, BC, CD, DA$ respectively. Let $S$ denote the sum of the two smallest areas among $\triangle AA_{1}D_{1}, \triangle BB_{1}A_{1}, \triangle CC_{1}B_{1}, \triangle DD_{1}C_{1}$, and let $S_{1}$ be the area of quadrilateral $A_{1}B_{1}C_{1}D_{1}$. Then the inequality $k S_{1} \geq S$ always holds.

Let $w$, $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that
$$
wx y z = 1 \quad \text{ and } \quad w + x + y + z > \frac{w}{x} + \frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{z} + \frac{z}{w}
$$
Prove that
$$
w + x + y + z < \frac{x}{w} + \frac{y}{x} + \frac{z}{y} + \frac{w}{z}
$$
\text{Let } a, b, c, d > 0. \text{ Show that} \quad \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{(a-b)(a-c)}{a+b+c} \geq 0 \quad \text{and characterize when equality holds.}

Find all functions $f$ from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$, the identity
$$
\ f(a f(a + b)) = f(b f(a)) + a^2
$$
holds.

Let triangle $ABC$ have an incircle touching $AB$ at $Z$ and $AC$ at $Y$. Let $G$ be the intersection point of lines $BY$ and $CZ$. Define points $R$ and $S$ such that $BCYR$ and $BCSZ$ are parallelograms. Show that $GR = GS$.

Suppose $P$ is a convex polygon with a point $O$ such that $P$ is centrally symmetric about $O$. Show that there exists a parallelogram $R$ containing $P$ such that
$$
\frac{\text{Area}(R)}{\text{Area}(P)} \leq \sqrt{2}.
$$

\text{In a round-robin tennis tournament with } n \geq 4 \text{ players, each pair plays once with no ties. A group of four players is termed bad if one is defeated by the other three, and each of the three has one win and one loss among themselves. If no bad groups exist, and } w_i, \ell_i \text{ are the number of wins and losses for player } i, \text{ prove that} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left(w_i - \ell_i\right)^3 \geq 0

Let $\mathcal{P}_{1}, \ldots, \mathcal{P}_{s}$ be arithmetic progressions of integers, satisfying:
(1) every integer lies in at least one of them;
(2) for each $i$, there exists an integer in $\mathcal{P}_{i}$ that is not in any other $\mathcal{P}_{j}$, $j \neq i$.
Let $n$ be the least common multiple of the steps of these progressions, with prime factorization $n = p_{1}^{\alpha_{1}} \cdots p_{k}^{\alpha_{k}}$. Prove that
$$
 s \geq 1 + \sum_{i=1}^{k} \alpha_{i}(p_{i} - 1)
$$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $D$ be the midpoint of $AC$. The internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets the circumcircle of triangle $DBC$ at a point $E$ distinct from $B$ and $C$. The line $BD$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $AEB$ at a point $F$ distinct from $B$. The lines $AF$ and $BE$ intersect at a point $I$, and the lines $CI$ and $BD$ intersect at a point $K$. Prove that $I$ is the incenter of triangle $KAB$.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon with all sides tangent to a circle $\omega$ centered at $O$. Suppose the circumcircle of triangle $ACE$ coincides in center with $\omega$. Let $J$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to $CD$. Suppose that the perpendicular from $B$ to $DF$ intersects the line $EO$ at a point $K$. Let $L$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $K$ to $DE$. Prove that the lengths $DJ$ and $DL$ are equal.

Let $k$ be a positive integer and define $n = 2^{k} + 1$. Show that $n$ is prime if and only if there exists a sequence $a_{1}, \ldots, a_{n-1}$ containing each integer from $1$ to $n-1$ exactly once, and a sequence $g_{1}, \ldots, g_{n-1}$, such that $g_{i}^{a_{i}} \equiv a_{i+1} \pmod{n}$ for all $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,n-1\}$, with $a_{n} = a_{1}$.

Let $ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, and let $C_0$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. Let $X$ lie in the interior of segment $CC_0$, and let $K, L$ be points on segments $AX, BX$ such that $BK = BC$ and $AL = AC$, respectively. Let $M$ be the intersection of $AL$ and $BK$. Prove that $MK = ML$.

Let $S$ be a set of $2000$ distinct real numbers. Show that there are two distinct pairs $(a, b)$ and $(c, d)$ with $a > b$ and $c > d$ such that
$$
\left|\frac{a-b}{c-d}-1\right|<\frac{1}{100000}
$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $A \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. An $A$-partition of $n$ into $k$ parts is a representation of $n$ as $n = a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_k$, where each $a_i \in A$. The number of different parts in the partition is the number of distinct elements in $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k\}$. An $A$-partition is called optimal if no $A$-partition of $n$ has fewer than $k$ parts. Prove that any optimal $A$-partition of $n$ has at most $\sqrt[3]{6n}$ distinct parts.

Let $n \geqslant 2$ be an integer. Consider all circular arrangements of the numbers $0,1, \ldots, n$, identifying arrangements that are rotations of each other. An arrangement is called beautiful if, for any four distinct numbers $0 \leqslant a, b, c, d \leqslant n$ such that $a + c = b + d$, the chords connecting $a$ and $c$ and $b$ and $d$ do not intersect. Let $M$ be the number of beautiful arrangements of $0,1, \ldots, n$. Let $N$ be the number of coprime pairs ($x, y$) of positive integers with $x + y \leqslant n$. Prove that $$ M = N + 1. $$

Let $\triangle ABC$ satisfy $\angle B > \angle C$. Place points $P$ and $Q$ on the line $AC$ such that $\angle PBA = \angle QBA = \angle ACB$, with $A$ lying between $P$ and $C$. If there exists a point $D$ on segment $BQ$ such that $\angle PBD = \angle DPB$, and ray $AD$ meets the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ again at $R$, prove that $QR = QB$.

Let $PQRSTU$ be a convex hexagon such that $PQ = TU$, $QR = UV$, $RS = VP$, and $\angle P - \angle U = \angle R - \angle V = \angle T - \angle Q$. Prove that the lines $PR$, $QS$, and $RT$ are concurrent.

Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. On an $n \times n$ board, place $n$ rooks such that each row and each column contains exactly one rook. Such a placement is termed a permutation configuration. Determine the maximum integer $k$ such that every permutation configuration guarantees the existence of an empty $k \times k$ subgrid.

Suppose $n \geq 3$ lines are drawn in the plane, with no two being parallel and no three intersecting at a single point. These lines partition the plane into various regions, and let $\mathcal{F}$ denote the set of regions with finite area. Show that it is possible to select and colour $\lceil\sqrt{n / 2}\rceil$ lines blue such that no bounded region in $\mathcal{F}$ is entirely enclosed by blue lines.

Let $M$ be a set of $n \geqslant 4$ points in the plane, with no three collinear. Initially, $n$ segments are drawn such that every point is an endpoint of exactly two segments. At each step, if two segments $AB$ and $CD$ intersect in their interiors, they can be replaced with $AC$ and $BD$, provided neither is already present. Show that no more than $n^{3} / 4$ such replacements can occur.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on $BC$ such that $\angle PAB = \angle ACB$ and $\angle QAC = \angle CBA$. Points $M$ and $N$ lie on the extensions of $AP$ and $AQ$ beyond $P$ and $Q$, respectively, so that $PM = AP$ and $QN = AQ$. Show that the lines $BM$ and $CN$ meet on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

Let $\Omega$ and $O$ be the circumcircle and circumcenter of triangle $ABC$, where $\angle ABC < 90^\circ$ and $AB > BC$. Let $M$ be the second intersection of the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ with $\Omega$. Let $\Gamma$ be the circle with diameter $BM$. The bisectors of $\angle AOB$ and $\angle BOC$ intersect $\Gamma$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $R$ lie on $PQ$ such that $BR = MR$. Show that $BR \parallel AC$.

Along a one-dimensional road in Lineland, there are $n \geqslant 1$ towns positioned from left to right. Each town is equipped with a distinct-sized right-facing and left-facing bulldozer. When two bulldozers face each other (one right-facing, one left-facing), the larger one pushes the smaller one off the road. If a bulldozer reaches the back of another bulldozer, it pushes it off regardless of size. Given two towns $A$ and $B$, with $B$ to the right of $A$, we define that $A$ can sweep $B$ if the right bulldozer of $A$ can reach $B$ and remove all intervening bulldozers. Similarly, $B$ can sweep $A$ if its left bulldozer can reach $A$ and clear the path. Prove that there is a unique town that cannot be swept away by any other.

Let $S$ be a finite set of points in the plane. We say $S$ is symmetric if for every pair of points $A, B \in S$ with $A \neq B$, there is a point $C \in S$ such that $AC = BC$. We say $S$ is center-avoiding if for all triples of distinct points $A, B, C \in S$, there is no point $P \in S$ such that $PA = PB = PC$.

a. Prove that for all $n \geq 3$, there exists a symmetric set with $n$ points.

b. Determine all $n \geq 3$ for which a symmetric, center-avoiding set of $n$ points exists.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB > AC$, and let $\Gamma$ be its circumcircle. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $ABC$, $M$ the midpoint of side $BC$, and $F$ the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Suppose points $Q$ and $K$ lie on $\Gamma$ such that $\angle AQH = 90^\circ$ and $\angle KQH = 90^\circ$. Show that the circumcircles of triangles $KQH$ and $KFM$ are tangent.

Determine all integers $n \geqslant 3$ such that for any real numbers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ and $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ with $\left|a_{k}\right| + \left|b_{k}\right| = 1$ for all $1 \leqslant k \leqslant n$, there exists a choice of $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n} \in \{-1, 1\}$ for which
$$
\left|\sum_{k=1}^{n} x_{k} a_{k}\right| + \left|\sum_{k=1}^{n} x_{k} b_{k}\right| \leqslant 1
$$
