Let $k$ be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. In the plane, there are $2k+1$ segments such that any two intersect at a unique interior point and no three intersect at the same point. Jeff assigns a snail to one endpoint of each segment and claps $2k$ times. Each clap causes the snails to advance to the next intersection point along their respective segments. After $2k$ claps, the snails reach the furthest intersection from their starting point.

a) Prove that Jeff can always choose the starting positions of the snails so that no two snails ever share an intersection point during the claps.

b) Prove that if $k$ is a positive integer such that $2k+1$ is replaced with $2k$, then regardless of Jeff's choices, there will be a clap at which at least two snails share an intersection point.

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $(f(a)+b)(f(b)+a)>0$, it follows that $f(a)+b=f(b)+a$. Show that $f(a)+b \leqslant f(b)+a$ for all $a > b$.

Let $n$ be an integer greater than or equal to 3. Given two regular polygons $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ with $n$ sides in the plane, show that the vertices of $\mathcal{A}$ which are contained within or on the boundary of $\mathcal{B}$ form a connected arc of the polygon $\mathcal{A}$.
(That is, prove that such a set of vertices can be separated from the rest of $\mathcal{A}$'s vertices by a straight line.)

Let $n \geqslant 2018$ be an integer, and let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}, b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ be distinct positive integers with $a_i, b_i \in [1, 5n]$ for all $i$. If the values
$$
\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}, \frac{a_{2}}{b_{2}}, \ldots, \frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}
$$
form an arithmetic progression, show that all the fractions are equal.

Let $\mathbb{Z}$ be the set of integers. Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ such that, for all integers $x$ and $y$,
$$
f(2x) + 2f(y) = f(f(x+y)).
$$

Let $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{2019}$ be real numbers such that
$$
x_{1}+x_{2}+\cdots+x_{2019}=0 \quad \text{and} \quad x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+\cdots+x_{2019}^{2}=1 .$$
Let $m=\min \left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{2019}\right)$ and $M=\max \left(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{2019}\right)$. Prove that
$$
mM \leqslant-\frac{1}{2019}$$

Let $n \geqslant 2$ be a positive integer and $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$ be real numbers such that
$$
 x_{1} + x_{2} + \cdots + x_{n} = 0 .
$$
Define the set $S$ as
$$
 S = \left\{ (p, q) \mid 1 \leqslant p < q \leqslant n,\ |x_p - x_q| \geqslant 1 \right\} .
$$
Show that if $S$ is non-empty, then
$$
\sum_{(p, q) \in S} x_p x_q < 0 .
$$

Let $P(x, y, z)$ be a real polynomial in three variables satisfying
$$
P(x, y, z) = P(x, y, x y - z) = P(x, x z - y, z) = P(y z - x, y, z)
$$
Show that $P(x, y, z)$ can be written as $F(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - x y z)$ for some univariate polynomial $F(t)$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider a sequence of $n$ bits $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$, where each $b_i$ is either 0 or 1 (representing tails or heads). Repeatedly perform the following: if there are exactly $k$ ones among the bits and $k > 0$, then flip the $k^{	ext{th}}$ bit; otherwise, terminate. For a sequence $C$, define $\ell(C)$ as the number of operations until all bits are zero. Prove that $\ell(C)$ is finite for all $C$, and compute the average of $\ell(C)$ over all $2^n$ sequences.

Let $n > 1$ be an integer. Suppose $2n$ distinct points in the plane are given, with no three collinear. Label these points $P_{1}, P_{2}, \ldots, P_{2n}$ in some order. Consider the $2n$ smallest positive angles formed consecutively as $\angle P_{1}P_{2}P_{3}, \angle P_{2}P_{3}P_{4}, \ldots, \angle P_{2n}P_{1}P_{2}$. Prove that there exists a labelling of the points such that the angles can be partitioned into two subsets with equal total angle sum.

In a land with $n \geqslant 2$ cities, each pair of cities is connected by a one-way road whose direction is unknown to Alice. Alice can ask for the direction of any road between two cities. She needs to determine whether there exists a city with at most one outgoing road. Prove that Alice can determine this with at most $4n$ queries.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with orthocenter $H$, and let $D$, $E$, and $F$ be the feet of the altitudes from $A$, $B$, and $C$ onto $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$, respectively. Let $\omega_{B}$ and $\omega_{C}$ be the incircles of triangles $BDF$ and $CDE$, tangent to $DF$ and $DE$ at $M$ and $N$. Let line $MN$ intersect $\omega_{B}$ and $\omega_{C}$ again at $P$ and $Q$. Show that $MP = NQ$.

Let $A B C D E$ be a convex pentagon with $CD = DE$ and $\angle EDC \neq 2 \cdot \angle ADB$. A point $P$ lies in the interior of the pentagon such that $AP = AE$ and $BP = BC$. Show that the condition $\operatorname{area}(BCD) + \operatorname{area}(ADE) = \operatorname{area}(ABD) + \operatorname{area}(ABP)$ is equivalent to $P$ being on the diagonal $CE$.

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the set of all lines in the plane and let $f$ be a function that assigns to each line $\ell \in \mathcal{L}$ a point $f(\ell)$ on $\ell$. Suppose that for any point $X$, and for any three distinct lines $\ell_{1}, \ell_{2}, \ell_{3}$ through $X$, the points $f(\ell_{1}), f(\ell_{2}), f(\ell_{3})$, and $X$ are concyclic. Prove that there exists a unique point $P$ such that $f(\ell) = P$ for every line $\ell$ passing through $P$.

Let $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ be positive real numbers such that $p \geqslant q \geqslant r \geqslant s > 0$ and $p + q + r + s = 1$. Prove that
$$
(p + 2q + 3r + 4s) p^{p} q^{q} r^{r} s^{s} < 1
$$

Let $n$ be an integer with $n \geqslant 1$. Consider a grid with $n$ rows and $n$ columns where each entry is $\left\lfloor\frac{ij}{n+1}\right\rfloor$ for row $i$ and column $j$. Find all values of $n$ such that the sum of all $n^{2}$ entries is $\frac{1}{4} n^{2}(n-1)$.

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. Define an integer $m \geqslant n+1$ as $n$-colourful if it is possible to arrange $m$ marbles of $n$ different colours $c_{1}, c_{2}, \ldots, c_{n}$ around a circle such that each block of $n+1$ adjacent marbles contains all $n$ distinct colours. Show that only finitely many positive integers fail to be $n$-colourful and determine the maximum such integer.

Find the maximum number $N$ such that there exists an $N \times 100$ matrix $T$ where each row is a permutation of $\{1,2,\ldots,100\}$, and for every pair of distinct rows $r$ and $s$, there is at least one column $c$ with $|T(r,c) - T(s,c)| \geq 2$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $AC = BC$. A point $P$ lies on the extension of $AB$ past $B$. The circle passing through $A$, $C$, and $D$ intersects $PD$ again at $Q$, and the circle through $A$, $P$, and $Q$ intersects $PC$ again at $R$. Show that $CD$, $AQ$, and $BR$ meet at a common point.

Find all integers $n \geq 3$ such that in any convex polygon with $n$ sides, each of length $1$, there exists an equilateral triangle with side length $1$ whose boundary is entirely contained within the polygon.

Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, and define $P^{(1)}(x) = P(x)$ and $P^{(k+1)}(x) = P\left(P^{(k)}(x)\right)$ for all $k \geq 1$. Determine all positive integers $n$ such that there exists a polynomial $P(x)$ with integer coefficients for which the set $\{P^{(m)}(1), P^{(m)}(2), \ldots, P^{(m)}(n)\}$ has precisely $\left\lceil n / 2^{m} \right\rceil$ distinct values modulo $n$ for all $m \geq 1$.

The Bank of Oslo produces coins from two metals: aluminium ($A$) and copper ($C$). Morgane possesses $n$ of each type and arranges them in a row in some arbitrary order. Given a fixed positive integer $k \leqslant 2n$, she performs the following operation repeatedly: find the maximal group of consecutive coins of the same metal that includes the $k$-th coin from the left and move this group to the leftmost position. For instance, if $n=4$ and $k=4$, the configuration $A A C C C A C A$ evolves as $$ A A C C C A C A \rightarrow C C C A A A C A \rightarrow A A A C C C C A \rightarrow C C C C A A A A \rightarrow \cdots . $$ Determine all pairs $(n, k)$ with $1 \leqslant k \leqslant 2n$ such that for any initial configuration, at some point in the process the number of adjacent $A$-$C$ pairs is at most one.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. Let $D$ be a point on segment $BC$, and consider the line through $D$ perpendicular to $BC$, which intersects $AO$, $AC$, and $AB$ at points $W$, $X$, and $Y$, respectively. Let $Z$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $ABC$ and $AXY$. Prove that if $OD = OW$, then line $DZ$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $AXY$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be given, and let $\ell_{1}$ and $\ell_{2}$ be parallel lines intersecting $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $X_{1}, Y_{1}, Z_{1}$ and $X_{2}, Y_{2}, Z_{2}$ respectively. For each $i$, construct triangle $\Delta_{i}$ by drawing lines through $X_{i}$, $Y_{i}$, and $Z_{i}$ perpendicular to $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $\Delta_{1}$ and $\Delta_{2}$ are tangent.

Let $N$ be a positive integer. Prove that there exist three bijections $\sigma, \tau, \rho: \{1,2,\ldots,N\} \to \{1,2,\ldots,N\}$ such that
$$
\left|\sqrt{\sigma(k)} + \sqrt{\tau(k)} + \sqrt{\rho(k)} - 2\sqrt{N}\right| < 2023
$$
for all $k = 1, 2, \ldots, N$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Arrange $\sum_{i=1}^n i$ circles in a triangular formation with $n$ rows such that the $i^\text{th}$ row has $i$ circles. A ninja-path is defined as a sequence of circles where each step goes to one of the two circles directly beneath. Given that exactly one circle is selected from each row and marked red, determine the maximum $k$ such that there always exists a ninja-path containing at least $k$ red circles.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $AC > BC$. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, with radius $r$. Choose a point $P$ on segment $AC$ such that $CP = BC$, and let $S$ be the projection of $P$ onto line $AB$. Suppose ray $BP$ intersects $\omega$ again at $D$. Define a point $Q$ on the line $SP$ such that $PQ = r$ and the order of points is $S, P, Q$. Let $E$ be the intersection of the line through $A$ perpendicular to $CQ$ and the line through $B$ perpendicular to $DQ$. Show that $E$ lies on $\omega$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$. Let $\Omega$ be the circumcircle of $ABC$ and let $S$ be the midpoint of the arc $CAB$ not containing $B$. The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ intersects $BS$ at $D$ and $\Omega$ again at $E$. If a line through $D$ parallel to $BC$ intersects $BE$ at $L$, and $\omega$ is the circumcircle of triangle $BDL$, then let $\omega$ and $\Omega$ intersect again at $P$. Prove that the tangent to $\omega$ at $P$ and line $BS$ meet on the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$.

Let $M$ be a positive integer. Two players, Alex and Sam, play a game by writing the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, M$ on a board. Alex starts. On a turn, a player selects a pair $(k, m)$ with $k \geqslant 0$ and $m$ on the board, then removes all numbers $t$ on the board such that $2^{k} \mid m - t$. The game ends when the board is empty, and the player who removes the final number loses. Find all $M$ for which Alex can force a win regardless of Sam's strategy.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with $AC < BD < AD$ and $\angle DBA < 90^\circ$. Let $E$ be a point on the line through $D$ parallel to $AB$ such that $E$ and $C$ are on opposite sides of line $AD$ and $DE = AC$. Let $F$ be a point on the line through $A$ parallel to $CD$ such that $F$ and $C$ are on opposite sides of line $AD$ and $AF = BD$. Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of $BC$ and $EF$ meet at a point on the circumcircle of $ABCD$.

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ and $AB < CD$. Let $P = AD \cap BC$. Let $X$ be a point on the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$, different from $C$, such that $PX = PC$. Let $Y$ be a point on the circumcircle of triangle $ABD$, different from $D$, such that $PY = PD$. Let $Q = AX \cap BY$. Prove that $PQ \parallel AB$.

Find all sequences $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots$ of positive integers such that for all positive integers $m$ and $n$ with $m \leq n$, the arithmetic mean $\frac{1}{k} \sum_{i = m}^{n} a_i$ and the geometric mean $\left(\prod_{i = m}^{n} a_i\right)^{\frac{1}{k}}$, where $k = n - m + 1$, are both integers.
Find all integer triples $(x, y, z)$ such that $x+y+z=24$, $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=210$, and $x y z=440$.

Let $s_{1}, s_{2}, s_{3}, s_{4}$ be the positive real roots of the equation $4x^{4} - a x^{3} + b x^{2} - c x + 5 = 0$. Find $s_{1}, s_{2}, s_{3}, s_{4}$, given that $\frac{s_{1}}{2} + \frac{s_{2}}{4} + \frac{s_{3}}{5} + \frac{s_{4}}{8} = 1$.

ext{Let } a, b, c \in \mathbb{R} 	ext{ with } a 
eq 1, b 
eq 1, a 
eq b, 	ext{ and } \dfrac{b c - a^{2}}{1 - a} = \dfrac{a c - b^{2}}{1 - b}. 	ext{ Prove that } \dfrac{b c - a^{2}}{1 - a} = a + b + c.

Let $g(n)$ be a function defined on positive integers with non-negative integer outputs satisfying

(1) $g(m n) = g(m) + g(n)$,

(2) $g(n) = 0$ if $n$ ends in $3$,

(3) $g(10) = 0$.

Determine $g(1985)$.
Determine $f(x)$ such that $f\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right) f(x)^{2} = 64x$ for all $x \ne 0, \pm 1$.
Let $k$ be an odd positive integer, and suppose $(2+\sqrt{3})^{k} = 1 + m + n \sqrt{3}$ with $m, n$ positive integers. Prove that $m$ is a perfect square.
Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $p$, $q$ be positive integers such that $ad - bc = 1$ and $\frac{a}{b} > \frac{p}{q} > \frac{c}{d}$. Prove that $q \geq b + d$ and that equality holds only if $p = a + c$.
Let P be a fixed point in the plane. Among all triangles ABC with fixed distances PA = 3, PB = 5, and PC = 7, prove that the one with maximum perimeter has P as its incenter.

Suppose $k$ satisfies $k^{3} = 2$ and let $x$, $y$, $z$ be rational numbers with $x + y k + z k^{2} \ne 0$. Prove that there exist rational numbers $u$, $v$, $w$ such that $(x + y k + z k^{2})(u + v k + w k^{2}) = 1$.
Let $x, y, z$ be real numbers in the interval $\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Prove that $\frac{\pi}{2} + 2\sin x \cos y + 2\sin y \cos z > \sin(2x) + \sin(2y) + \sin(2z)$.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be the sides of a triangle. Prove that
$$
\frac{x-y}{x+y} + \frac{y-z}{y+z} + \frac{z-x}{z+x} < \frac{1}{16}.
$$

Let $f$ be a function defined on the non-negative integers. For all $n \geq 0$, $f(2^n - 1) = 0$. For all other $m$, $f(m) = f(m+1) + 1$. Prove that for all $n$, $f(n) + n = 2^k - 1$ for some integer $k$, and compute $f(2^{1990})$.
Let $ g $ be a function defined on $ [0,1] $ with $ g(0) = 0 $, $ g\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) = \frac{g(x)}{2} $, and $ g(1 - x) = 1 - g(x) $. Compute $ g\left(\frac{18}{1991}\right) $.

Let $q(a, b)$ be the expression $2 a^{2} - 6 a b + 5 b^{2}$. Define the range of $q$ as the set of integers $k$ such that $k = q(a, b)$ for some integers $a$, $b$. Determine which integers from $\{1,2, \ldots, 100\}$ belong to the range of $q$. Prove that if $h$ and $k$ are in the range of $q$, then so is $h k$.
Let $f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \dfrac{b_{k}}{x + b_{k}}$, with $b_{k}$ being distinct positive real numbers. Determine the total length of the domain for which $f(x) \geq 1$.

\text{Given an equilateral triangle } ABC \text{ with side length } 2, \text{ let } P \text{ be any point on its incircle. Prove that } PA^2 + PB^2 + PC^2 = 5. \text{ Moreover, demonstrate that the triangle formed by the segments } PA, PB, PC \text{ has an area of } \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.
Given a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB \parallel CD$, the distance between the two parallel sides is $h$, and the sum of the lengths of $AB$ and $CD$ is $m$, construct the figure.
Determine all strictly increasing functions $f : \mathbb{N}^+ \to \mathbb{N}^+$ such that for all positive integers $x$ and $y$, $f(y f(x)) = x^2 f(xy)$.

\text{Let } ABC \text{ be an equilateral triangle with incircle } \omega. \text{ Points } D \text{ and } E \text{ lie on } AB \text{ and } AC, \text{ respectively, such that } DE \text{ is tangent to } \omega. \text{ Prove that } \frac{AD}{DB} + \frac{AE}{EC} = 1.

\text{\$ABCD\$ is a cyclic quadrilateral with an incircle centered on side \$AB\$ that is tangent to sides \$BC\$, \$CD\$, and \$DA\$. Prove that \$AB = AD + BC\$. Determine the maximum area of \$ABCD\$ in terms of the lengths \$\|AB\|\$ and \$\|CD\|\$.}

Let the incircle of triangle $ABC$ be tangent to $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at points $D$, $E$, and $F$ respectively. Let $AD$ intersect the incircle again at $X$, with $AX = XD$. Let $BX$ and $CX$ intersect the incircle again at $Y$ and $Z$ respectively. Prove that the lengths $EY$ and $FZ$ are equal.

Let \mathrm{ABC} be a triangle with median \mathrm{AD}, and let \mathrm{M} be the midpoint of \mathrm{AD}. If the ray \mathrm{BM} intersects \mathrm{AC} at point N, prove that the tangent from \mathrm{A} to the circumcircle of triangle \mathrm{NBC} is \mathrm{AB} if and only if \mathrm{BM} / \mathrm{BN} = (\mathrm{BC} / \mathrm{BN})^{2}.

Let $ k = p + 1 $, where $ p $ is a prime. Given $ n = k^2 - k + 1 $, prove that it is possible to color some cells in an $ n \times n $ grid black such that every row and column contains exactly $ k $ black cells, and no rectangle with sides parallel to the grid's sides has all four corner cells black.

Let $ n > 2 $ be an integer. Define the set $ S $ of pairs $ (a, b) $ of positive integers with $ a < b \leq n $, $ \gcd(a, b) = 1 $, and $ a + b > n $. Prove that $ \sum_{(a, b) \in S} \frac{1}{ab} = \frac{1}{2} $.

\text{Given points } P_{1}, P_{2}, \ldots, P_{n} \text{ in the plane, with real numbers } m_{i} \neq 0 \text{ assigned to each point. Suppose that for all } i \neq j, \text{ the square of the distance between } P_{i} \text{ and } P_{j} \text{ equals } m_{i} + m_{j}. \text{ Show that } n \leq 4 \text{ and that if } n = 4, \text{ then } \frac{1}{m_{1}} + \frac{1}{m_{2}} + \frac{1}{m_{3}} + \frac{1}{m_{4}} = 0.

Suppose $ k \geq 1 $ is a real number with the property that for any integers $ m $ and $ n $ such that $ n $ divides $ m $, the integer part of $ mk $ is divisible by the integer part of $ nk $. Prove that $ k $ is an integer.

Let $ n > 1 $ be an integer. Let $ D_n $ be the set of lattice points $ (x, y) $ such that $ x, y $ satisfy $ -n \leq x, y \leq n $. If each point in $ D_n $ is assigned one of three colors, prove that there exist two points of the same color such that the line connecting them contains no other points of $ D_n $. Show that there exists a coloring with four colors such that no line intersects $ D_n $ at exactly two points of the same color.

Let $o(n)$ be the count of $2n$-tuples $(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}, y_{1}, y_{2}, \ldots, y_{n})$ with $x_i, y_j \in \{0,1\}$ and the sum $x_{1} y_{1} + x_{2} y_{2} + \ldots + x_{n} y_{n}$ is odd. Let $e(n)$ count the tuples for which the sum is even. Prove that $\dfrac{o(n)}{e(n)} = \dfrac{2^{n} - 1}{2^{n} + 1}$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$, and let the incircle touch sides $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ at $D$, $E$, and $F$ respectively. Let $AD$ intersect the incircle again at $Q$. Prove that the line $EQ$ passes through the midpoint of $AF$ if and only if triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AC = BC$.

Suppose $n > 1$ countries each have representatives seated around a circular table. If any two individuals from the same country are adjacent in the right-hand direction, then their right-hand neighbors must be from distinct countries. Determine the maximum total number of people that can be seated for each $n$.
Determine all positive integers $n < 1000$ for which $n^2 = \left(\sum_{i=0}^{k} d_i\right)^3$, where $d_i$ are the digits of $n$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be fixed points, and let $C$ lie on the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$. Construct a sequence $C_1, C_2, C_3, \ldots$ such that $C_1 = C$, and for each $n$, if $C_n$ does not lie on line $AB$, then $C_{n+1}$ is the circumcenter of triangle $ABC_n$. The sequence ends if $C_n$ lies on $AB$. Determine all such points $C$ for which the sequence eventually becomes periodic.

Assign distinct integers $1$ through $n$ to the vertices of a regular $n$-gon with $n > 3$. Connect all non-adjacent vertices with diagonals. Prove that when $n$ is odd, it is possible to assign labels $1$ to $n$ to each side and diagonal such that no label matches its endpoints and all edges incident to a vertex have distinct labels.
Find all integer solutions $ (m, a, b) $ with $ m, a, b > 1 $ such that $ m^b + 1 = (m+1)^a $.

Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_k$ be $k > 2$ subsets of a set $S$ with $n$ elements, each of size at least $r$. Prove that there exist indices $i$ and $j$ such that $|A_i \cap A_j| \geq r - \dfrac{n k}{4(k - 1)}$.
Let $b_{1} = 56$ and define $b_{n+1} = b_{n} - \frac{1}{b_{n}}$. Prove that there exists an integer $k$ with $1 < k < 2002$ such that $b_{k} < 0$.

Let $A$, $B$ be sets of $N$ consecutive integers. If $N=2003$, is it possible to match each element of $A$ with one of $B$ to form $N$ pairs $(a,b)$ such that the sum of each pair forms a sequence of $N$ consecutive integers? What if $N=2004$?

Let $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2003}$ be a sequence with $a_0 = 1$ and $0 \leq a_i \leq 2 a_{i-1}$ for all $1 \leq i \leq 2003$. Suppose $T = \pm a_1 \pm a_2 \pm \ldots \pm a_{2002} + a_{2003}$. Prove that the sequence maximising $T$ can be determined without knowing the signs of the terms.
Find integer solutions $(x, y, z)$ satisfying $$x+y+z=1, \quad x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{2}=1.$$

Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $x$ be real numbers with $a b c \neq 0$ and
$$
\frac{x b + (1-x) c}{a} = \frac{x c + (1-x) a}{b} = \frac{x a + (1-x) b}{c}.
$$
Show that $a + b + c = 0$ or $a = b = c$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that $AB = CD$, $(\sqrt{3}+1)BC = DA$, and $\angle CDA - \angle DAB = 30^\circ$. Show that
$$
\angle ABC - \angle BCD = 90^\circ
$$
Let $p, q, r$ be three real numbers such that $1 \geq p \geq q \geq r \geq 0$. Prove that if $\mu$ is a root of the cubic equation $x^{3}+p x^{2}+q x+r=0$ (real or complex), then $|\mu| \leq 1$.

Let $f(n)$ represent the count of distinct triangles with integer side lengths and perimeter $n$ ($n \geq 3$). Prove that:

a. $f(1999) > f(1996)$

b. $f(2000) = f(1997)$.
Show that the equation $$ a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a) $$ has infinitely many solutions in integers $a, b, c$.
Given positive real numbers $x, y, z$ with $xyz = 1$, show that $$x^{y+z} y^{z+x} z^{x+y} \leq 1$$

Let $\mathbb{R}$ be the set of real numbers. Determine all functions $g: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
 g(a+b) = g(a) g(b) g(ab)
$$
holds for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.
Let $a, b$ be positive reals such that $a + b = 2$. Prove that $$a^{3} b^{3} (a^{3} + b^{3}) \leq 2$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and consider an $n \times n$ grid filled with the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, n^2$ in such a way that each row and each column is in increasing order. Let $a_{jk}$ be the number in the $j$-th row and $k$-th column. Define $b_j$ as the number of distinct values that can occur at $a_{jj}$. Prove that
$$
\sum_{j=1}^n b_j \leq \frac{n}{3}(n^2 - 3n + 5)
$$
(Example: When $n = 3$, the number $a_{22}$ can be 4, 5, or 6, so $b_2 = 3$.)

Prove that for any real value $a$, the polynomial
$$
8 x^{4}-16 x^{3}+16 x^{2}-8 x+a=0
$$
possesses at least one complex root that is not real and compute the total of all such complex roots.

Let triangle $PQR$ have side lengths $x, y, z$. Construct a triangle $P_1 Q_1 R_1$ with side lengths $x + \frac{y}{2}$, $y + \frac{z}{2}$, $z + \frac{x}{2}$. Prove that
$$
\left[P_1 Q_1 R_1\right] \geq \frac{9}{4}[PQR].
$$

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with midpoints $K, L, M, N$ of sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$ respectively. Suppose:
(i) $BD$ bisects $KM$ at a point $Q$;
(ii) $Q$ is equidistant from all vertices $A, B, C, D$; and
(iii) the ratio $\frac{LK}{LM} = \frac{CD}{CB}$.
Show that $ABCD$ must be a square.
Let $\alpha$ be a real solution of the equation $x^{5} - x^{3} + x = 2$. Prove that the floor of $\alpha^{6}$ is equal to 3.

Let $S$ be the set of all 6-tuples $(x, y, z, w, u, v)$ of positive integers such that $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}+w^{2}+u^{2}=v^{2}$. Consider the set
$$
T=\{x y z w u v:(x, y, z, w, u, v) \in S\}
$$
Find the greatest common divisor of all the elements in $T$.

Prove that the number of 5-tuples of positive integers $(x, y, z, w, v)$ satisfying the equation
$$
xyzwv = 5(y z w v + x z w v + x y w v + x y z v + x y z w)
$$
is an odd integer.

Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers, not all equal, such that some two of the equations
$$
a x^{2}+2 b x+c=0, \quad b x^{2}+2 c x+a=0, \quad c x^{2}+2 a x+b=0
$$
have a common root, say $\beta$. Prove that
(a) $\beta$ is real and negative; and
(b) the third equation has non-real roots.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f\left(a^{2}+b f(c)\right)=a f(a)+c f(b)
$$
for all $a, b, c$ in $\mathbb{R}$.

Prove that for each positive integer $n$ there exists a unique pair $(a, b)$ of positive integers satisfying
$$
n = a + \frac{1}{2}(a + b - 1)(a + b - 2)
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, and let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Suppose the incircle $\gamma$ of triangle $ABC$ slides along the side $BC$ towards $B$. Prove that when $\gamma$ is tangent to $\Gamma$ from inside, it is also tangent to the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$.

Determine all real-valued functions $f$ such that for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, the identity
$$
 f(x+y) + f(x)f(y) = f(x)(1+y) + f(y)(1+x) + f(xy)
$$
holds true.

Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that the quadratic equation $x^{2} - a x + b = 0$ has real roots $\gamma$ and $\delta$. Show that $\gamma$ and $\delta$ are integers if and only if $[a \gamma] + [a \delta]$ is the square of an integer. (Here $[x]$ is the floor function.)

Let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be a permutation of the integers $1, 2, \dots, n$ arranged in a circular sequence. Determine
$$
\min \sum_{i=1}^{n} |b_i - b_{i+1}| \quad \text{and} \quad \max \sum_{i=1}^{n} |b_i - b_{i+1}|,
$$
where $b_{n+1} = b_1$ and the minimum and maximum are computed over all such permutations.

Let $\sigma = (x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ be a permutation of the set $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, n\}$. Define an inversion as a pair $(x_i, x_j)$ such that $i < j$ and $x_i > x_j$. For example, in the permutation $(3, 6, 2, 5, 1, 4)$, there are 7 inversions. Determine the number of such permutations of length $n$, with $n \geq 3$, that contain exactly two inversions.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $P$ lie on $AD$. Let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to $AC$. If $\frac{AP}{PD} = \frac{BP}{PE} = \lambda$, $\frac{BD}{AD} = m$, and $z = m^2(1+\lambda)$, prove that
$$
 z^2 - (\lambda^3 - \lambda^2 - 2)z + 1 = 0
$$
Deduce that $\lambda \geq 2$ and equality holds if and only if $ABC$ is equilateral.
\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be positive real numbers. Show that} \quad (a+b+c)^{2}(ab+bc+ca)^{2} \leq 3\left(b^{2}+bc+c^{2}\right)\left(c^{2}+ca+a^{2}\right)\left(a^{2}+ab+b^{2}\right)
Show that there exist infinitely many pairs $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a < b$ such that $\frac{(a + b)(a + b + 1)}{ab}$ is an integer.
Find all triples $(q, a, b)$ such that $q^{a} = b^{4} + 4$, where $q$ is a prime and $a, b$ are positive integers.

\text{Let } ABC \text{ be a triangle and let } P \text{ be an interior point such that } \angle BPC = 90^{\circ} \text{ and } \angle BAP = \angle BCP. \text{ Let } M, N \text{ be the midpoints of } AC, BC \text{ respectively. If } BP = 2PM, \text{ prove that points } A, P, N \text{ lie on a straight line.}
Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. If $3^n + 4^n \equiv 0 \pmod{n}$, prove that $7 \mid n$.

Determine all integers $n \ge 2$ and all primes $p, q, r$ such that for any set of $n$ distinct positive integers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$, if for all $1 \le j < k \le n$, $p \mid (a_j - a_k)$, $q \mid (a_j - a_k)$, or $r \mid (a_j - a_k)$, then it must be the case that one of $p, q, r$ divides every difference $a_j - a_k$ for $1 \le j < k \le n$.

Let $\{b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence defined by $b_n = 1 - \left(\left\lfloor \sqrt{n} \right\rfloor^2 = n\right)$, where $\lfloor \cdot \rfloor$ is the floor function. Let $y = 0.b_1 b_2 b_3 \ldots$ be the real number with the $n$-th decimal digit equal to $b_n$. Determine whether $y$ is rational or irrational.

In triangle $ABC$ with $AB > AC$, let $AM$ be the median from $A$ to $BC$, and $AK$ be the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$. A point $L$ lies on $AM$ such that $\angle KLC = \angle ACB$. Show that $CL$ is perpendicular to $AK$.
\text{Let } ABC \text{ be an acute triangle with orthocentre } H. \text{ Let } h_{\max} \text{ be the greatest height of the triangle. Show that } \$$ AH + BH + CH \leq 2 h_{\max} \$$
Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers such that $x^{3}+y^{3}=z^{3}$. Prove that $$ x^{2}+y^{2}-z^{2}>6(z-x)(z-y) $$
\sum_{k=0}^{n} \left[ \binom{3n+2-k}{k} 2^k - \binom{3n+1-k}{k-1} 2^{k-1} \right] = 2^{3n},\quad\text{where the second term is 0 for } k = 0.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be integers with $b$ even. Suppose the cubic polynomial $x^3 + a x^2 + b x + c$ has roots $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ satisfying $\alpha^2 = \beta + \gamma$. Prove $\alpha$ is an integer and $\beta \neq \gamma$.
Determine all integers $k > 3$ such that $(k-2)^2$ does not divide $(k-4)!$.

How many 6-tuples $\left(x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}, x_{5}, x_{6}\right)$ are there such that each of $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}, x_{5}, x_{6}$ is from the set $\{1,2,3,4\}$ and the six expressions
$$
x_{i}^{2} - x_{i}x_{i+1} + x_{i+1}^{2}
$$
for $i=1,2,3,4,5,6$ (where $x_{7} = x_{1}$) are all the same?

Let $\{a_{n}\}_{n \geq 0}$ be a sequence defined by $a_{0}=0$, $a_{1}=1$, and $a_{n}=2 a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}$ for all $n \geq 2$.

a. Prove that for all $m > 0$ and $0 \leq j \leq m$, the quantity $a_{m+j} + (-1)^{j} a_{m-j}$ is divisible by $2 a_{m}$.

b. Show that if $n$ is divisible by $2^{k}$, then $a_{n}$ is also divisible by $2^{k}$.

Define a positive integer $n$ as loyal if there are positive integers $x < y < z$ such that $x \mid y$, $y \mid z$, and $n = x + y + z$.

(i) Prove that only finitely many positive integers are not loyal.

(ii) Determine the total of all positive integers that are not loyal.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Let $D$ be a point on $BC$ such that $BC = 3DC$. Let $P$ be a point on $AD$ such that $\angle BAC = \angle BPD$. Show that $\angle BAC = 2\angle DPC$.
Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with side $AB = \sqrt{2+\sqrt{2}}$, and suppose the central angle subtended by $AB$ is $\frac{3\pi}{4}$. Determine the largest possible area of $ABCD$.

Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ denote the set of all positive real numbers. Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^+$, it holds that
$$
 f(a) + f(b) \le \frac{f(a+b)}{2}, \quad \frac{f(a)}{a} + \frac{f(b)}{b} \ge \frac{f(a+b)}{a+b}.
$$

Let $\{g_{n}(x)\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of functions defined by
$$
g_{0}(x)=1, \quad g_{1}(x)=x, \quad g_{n+1}(x) = \frac{(g_{n}(x))^{2}-1}{g_{n-1}(x)} \text{ for } n \geq 1
$$
Show that each $g_{n}(x)$ is a polynomial with integer coefficients.

Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(x + y + xy) = f(x) + f(y) + f(xy)$ for all real numbers $x, y$. Prove that $f$ satisfies $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.

Let $P(z) = \sum_{k=m}^{n} c_k z^k$ be a polynomial with complex coefficients such that $c_m \neq 0$, $c_n \neq 0$ and $n > m$. Prove that $$\max_{|z|=1}\{|P(z)|\} \ge \sqrt{\sum_{k=m}^{n} |c_k|^2 + 2|c_m c_n|}.$$

Let $f: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be a function satisfying $f(0) \neq 0$, $f(1)=0$ and

(i) $f(x)f(y) + f(xy) = f(x) + f(y)$;

(ii) $(f(x-y)-f(0)) f(x) f(y) = 0$,

for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$, simultaneously.

a. Determine the set of all possible values of the function $f$.

b. If $f(10) \neq 0$ and $f(2)=0$, find all integers $n$ such that $f(n) \neq 0$.
Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $a$ and $b$, with $b > 1$ and $a > b\sqrt{3} - 1$, such that $ab + 1$ is divisible by $a + b$ and $ab - 1$ is divisible by $a - b$.

A positive integer $n$ admits a unique decomposition into a non-decreasing sequence of odd positive integers $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_k)$ such that $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_k = n$ and for every integer $m$ in $[1, n]$, $m$ has a unique representation as a subsum of the $a_i$. The sequence $(1, 1, 3, 3)$ is an example for $n = 8$. How many such sequences exist for $n = 9999$?

Let $ h $ be an integer such that $ h \ge 3 $, and define $ X = \{ n \in \mathbb{Z}^+ \mid n \ge 2h \} $. Suppose $ S $ is a nonempty subset of $ X $ satisfying: 
* For all $ a, b \ge h $, if $ a + b \in S $, then $ ab \in S $;
* For all $ a, b \ge h $, if $ ab \in S $, then $ a + b \in S $. 
Prove that $ S = X $.

Two circles $\Gamma_{1}$ and $\Gamma_{2}$ touch externally at point $R$. A line $l_{1}$ is tangent to $\Gamma_{2}$ at $P$ and passes through the center $O_{1}$ of $\Gamma_{1}$. Another line $l_{2}$ is tangent to $\Gamma_{2}$ at $Q$ and passes through the center $O_{2}$ of $\Gamma_{2}$. Let $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ intersect at a point $K$ such that $KP = KQ$. Show that triangle $PQR$ is equilateral.
Let $p, q, r, s$ be positive integers with $p \geq q \geq r \geq s$. Show that the polynomial $x^{4}-p x^{3}-q x^{2}-r x-s$ cannot have an integer root.

Let $p, q, r, s, t, u$ be positive real numbers such that $p + q + r = s + t + u$ and $p q r = s t u$. Additionally, assume $p \leq s < t < u \leq r$ and $p < q < r$. Show that $p = s$, $q = t$ and $r = u$.
In triangle $ABC$, suppose point $D$ lies on $BC$ such that $AB + BD = AC + CD$. If the centroids of triangles $ABD$ and $ACD$, along with points $B$ and $C$, are concyclic, show that $AB = AC$.

Let $x$, $y$ be positive integers with $xy > 2$. If $\gcd(x, y) + \mathrm{lcm}(x, y)$ is divisible by $x + y$, show that the resulting quotient is no greater than $\frac{x + y}{4}$. Determine the conditions under which the quotient is exactly $\frac{x + y}{4}$.

Let $n$ be a natural number with $n > 1$. Consider the decimal representation of $1 / n$ in which finite decimals are expressed with repeating 9s. Determine the number of digits before the start of the repeating segment.
Determine all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that $$ f\left(y f(x) + x^{2} \right) = x f(x + y) $$ holds for all real numbers $ x $ and $ y $.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ meeting at $P$. Let $PE$, $PF$, $PG$, and $PH$ be the perpendiculars from $P$ to the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$, respectively. Prove that $ABCD$ is tangential (i.e., has an incircle) if and only if $$\frac{1}{PE} + \frac{1}{PG} = \frac{1}{PF} + \frac{1}{PH}$$
Let $\triangle ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. If the orthocenter of the triangle lies on its incircle, determine the value of $AB/BC$.

Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Define a function $f: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ by $f(2m) = m$ and $f(2m + 1) = 2m + 2$. Let $f^r(n) = f(f^{r-1}(n))$ for $r > 1$. 
(i) Prove that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists $r$ such that $f^r(n) = 1$.
(ii) For each $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $d_r$ be the number of $n$ such that $f^r(n) = 1$. Show that $d_{r+2} = d_{r+1} + d_r$ for $r \ge 1$.
Given that $2016$ distinct points on a circle are painted red and all other points are blue, show that for every integer $n \ge 3$, there exists a regular $n$-gon with all vertices in the blue set.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a right-angled triangle at $B$. A point $D$ lies on $AC$ such that the in-radii of triangles $ABD$ and $CBD$ are equal, both equal to $r'$. If $r$ is the in-radius of triangle $ABC$, prove that $$\frac{1}{r'} = \frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{BD}.$$

Let $a_1, a_2, \dots$ be a non-constant arithmetic progression. Suppose $p > 1$ and $q > 1$ are relatively prime integers such that $a_1^2$, $a_{p+1}^2$, and $a_{q+1}^2$ lie on the same arithmetic progression. Prove that every term in the progression is an integer.
Let $n$ be a non-negative integer such that all the integer roots of the cubic equation $x^3 + \alpha x + 4 - 2 \cdot 2016^n = 0$ exist. Determine all possible values of $\alpha$.

Let a polynomial $p(x)$ with real coefficients be defined as a square if it is non-constant and there exists a polynomial $q(x)$ with real coefficients such that $p(x) = q(x)^2$. Suppose that $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are non-constant polynomials over $\mathbb{R}$ with $f(x) \ne q(x)^2$ and $g(x) \ne r(x)^2$ for any polynomials $q(x), r(x)$, yet $f(g(x))$ is a square. Prove that $g(f(x))$ cannot be a square.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with incenter $I$. A line is drawn perpendicular to $BI$ at $I$, intersecting side $BC$ at $D$ and side $BA$ at $E$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the incenters of triangles $BIA$ and $BIC$, respectively. If points $D, E, P, Q$ lie on a circle, show that $AB = CB$.

Let $n$ and $M$ be positive integers with $M > n^{n-1}$. Show that one can find $n$ distinct primes $q_{1}, q_{2}, q_{3}, \ldots, q_{n}$ satisfying the condition $q_{k} \mid M + k$ for all $k$ in $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer and let $1 < x_{1} \leq x_{2} \leq x_{3} \leq \cdots \leq x_{n}$ be $n$ real numbers such that $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3} + \cdots + x_{n} = 2n$. Prove that
$$
x_{1} x_{2} \cdots x_{n-1} + x_{1} x_{2} \cdots x_{n-2} + \cdots + x_{1} x_{2} + x_{1} + 2 \leq x_{1} x_{2} \cdots x_{n}
$$

Given a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $\angle ABD = 30^\circ$, $\angle BCA = 75^\circ$, $\angle ACD = 25^\circ$ and $CD = CB$. Let $E$ be the second point of intersection of the line $CB$ extended with the circumcircle of triangle $DAC$. Show that $CE = BD$.

Let $\mathbb{R}[x]$ denote the set of all real-coefficient polynomials. Define $\operatorname{deg} P$ as the degree of a nonzero polynomial $P$. Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R}[x] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}[x]$ such that:
- $f(0) = 0$,
- for all $P \in \mathbb{R}[x] \setminus \{0\}$, $\operatorname{deg} f(P) \leq \operatorname{deg} P + 1$, and
- for all $P, Q \in \mathbb{R}[x]$, the real roots of $P - f(Q)$ are exactly the real roots of $Q - f(P)$.

Suppose $r > 0$ and the interior of a disc $D(r)$ is colored with two colors. 
1. If $r > \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}$, prove that there exist two points $A, B$ inside $D(r)$ with $AB = \pi$ and the same color.
2. Is the result from (1) still valid if $r > \frac{\pi}{2}$?

Let $r > 0$ be a real number. Suppose that all points in the open disk $D(r)$ are assigned one of two colors, red or blue.

1. If $r > \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}$, prove that there exist two points $A$ and $B$ inside the disk such that the Euclidean distance $AB = \pi$ and both points have the same color.

2. Does the result in (1) remain valid if $r > \frac{\pi}{2}$?

Alice starts with an integer $ N > 1 $ on a blackboard. Every minute, she replaces the number $ x $ with $ 2x + 1 $ if $ x $ is not a perfect cube, or with $ \sqrt[3]{x} $ if it is. Prove that eventually, the number on the blackboard exceeds $ 10^{100} $.

Let $N \ge 3$ be an integer. Consider an $N \times N$ grid of nodes connected by edges such that adjacent nodes are connected. A drone is programmed to travel a closed rectangular path, starting and ending at the same node. If every edge is traversed by at least one drone, what is the smallest number of drones needed to achieve this?

Let $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_n$ be $n$ distinct points in the plane. For each pair $(P_i, P_j)$, define $f(P_i, P_j) = \lfloor \log_2 \|P_i - P_j\| \rfloor$. Prove that the number of distinct values of $f$ is strictly less than $2n$.

In an acute scalene triangle $ABC$, the incircle touches $BC$ at $D$, and $I$ is the incentre. Let $Z$ be the point diametrically opposite to $A$ on the circumcircle of $ABC$. Point $L$ lies on the internal bisector of $\angle BZC$ such that $LI = AL$. Let $M$ be the arc midpoint of $BZC$, and let $V$ be the midpoint of segment $ID$. Prove that $\angle IML = \angle DVM$.
Let $f(k)$ represent the sum of the decimal digits of a positive integer $k$. Is there a positive integer $M$ such that $f(2^n) \le f(2^{n+1})$ holds for all $n > M$?
Show that for every integer $k > 2$, there exist $k$ distinct positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$ such that $$ \sum_{1 \le i < j \le k} \frac{1}{x_i x_j} = 1. $$

Suppose $P(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ is a polynomial of degree $d \ge 2$. Show that there cannot exist an infinite sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of rational numbers satisfying $P(a_n) = a_{n-1} + n$ for all $n \ge 1$.

Let two circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ intersect at points $P$ and $K$. A common tangent $XY$ is drawn near $P$, with $X$ lying on $\omega_1$ and $Y$ on $\omega_2$. The line $XP$ intersects $\omega_2$ again at $C$, and the line $YP$ intersects $\omega_1$ again at $B$. The lines $BX$ and $CY$ intersect at point $A$. Let $Q$ be the second point of intersection of the circumcircles of $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle AXY$. Show that
$$
\angle QXA = \angle QKP
$$
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_n$ be natural numbers such that for all $i \ne j$, $a_j - a_i$ divides $a_i$. Prove that for all $i < j$, $\frac{a_j}{j} \le \frac{a_i}{i}$.

Let $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{1389}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers satisfying $2a_i \ge a_{i-1} + a_{i+1}$ for all $1 \le i \le 1388$. Determine the largest constant $c$ such that $$ \sum_{k=0}^{1389} k a_k^2 \ge c \sum_{k=0}^{1389} a_k^2 $$ for all such sequences.
Determine all integers $n \ge 2$ for which the condition $\text{parity}(i + j) = \text{parity}\left(\binom{n}{i} + \binom{n}{j}\right)$ holds for all $i, j$ with $0 \le i, j \le n$.

Let $Q$ be the collection of all contiguous intervals of natural numbers. For any subset $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \dots < a_k\}$ of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, define $g(A)$ as the length of the largest interval in $A$, and $f(A)$ as the largest gap between consecutive elements in $A$. Set $G(n) = \sum_{A \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, n\}} g(A)$ and $F(n) = \sum_{A \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, n\}} f(A)$. Show there exists $m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $n > m$, $F(n) > G(n)$.

Let a polynomial $P(x, y, z)$ be called cyclic if $P(x, y, z) = P(y, z, x)$. Show that there exist four cyclic polynomials $P_1, P_2, P_3, P_4$ such that any cyclic polynomial $P$ can be expressed as $$P(x, y, z) = Q(P_1(x, y, z), P_2(x, y, z), P_3(x, y, z), P_4(x, y, z))$$ for some four-variable polynomial $Q$.
Determine all pairs of coprime positive integers $a$ and $b$ such that the decimal $b.a$ equals $\frac{a}{b}$. For example, if $a = 92$ and $b = 13$, then $b.a = 13.92$.

Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$. A point $X$ lies on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ not containing $A$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the projections of $X$ onto $BI$ and $CI$, respectively, and let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $EF$. Suppose that $MB = MC$. If $D$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $I$ to side $BC$, prove that $\angle BAD = \angle CAX$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have circumcircle $\omega$ and circumcenter $O$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of arc $BC$ of $\omega$ not containing $A$. Draw lines through $O$ parallel to $MB$ and $MC$; let these lines intersect $AB$ and $AC$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively. Let $N$ be the second intersection of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$ with $\omega$. Prove that $NK = NL$.

Let $P(x) = Q(y)$ be an **interesting equation** with integer coefficients and degree $\geq 1$, and infinitely many natural number solutions. We define $F(x) = G(y)$ as a **resulting equation** from $P(x) = Q(y)$ if there exists a rational-coefficient polynomial $R$ such that $F(x) = R(P(x))$ and $G(y) = R(Q(y))$.

a) Suppose that $S$ is an infinite subset of $\mathbb{N}^2$. If all elements of $S$ satisfy some interesting equation, show that there exists an interesting equation $P_0(x) = Q_0(y)$ such that all such equations satisfied by $S$ are resulting from $P_0(x) = Q_0(y)$.

b) Let the **degree** of an interesting equation be the maximum of the degrees of $P$ and $Q$. An equation is **primitive** if it cannot be derived from a lower-degree interesting equation. If $P(x) = Q(y)$ is primitive and both $P$ and $Q$ are monic, prove that $\deg P$ and $\deg Q$ are coprime.

Let $P_1P_2P_3P_4P_5$ be a convex pentagon in the Cartesian plane with all vertices having rational coordinates. For each $1 \le i \le 5$, let $Q_i$ be the point of intersection of the lines $P_{i+1}P_{i+2}$ and $P_{i+3}P_{i+4}$, where indices are taken modulo 5. Prove that at most three of the lines $P_iQ_i$, for $1 \le i \le 5$, can meet at a common point.

Let $I_b$ be the $B$-excenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ in the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ not containing $A$. Suppose the line $MI_b$ meets the circumcircle again at point $T$. Prove that $TI_b^2 = TB \times TC$.
Let $ABCD$ be a square with points $N$ on $AB$ and $P$ on $AD$ such that $PN = NC$. Let $Q$ be a point on $AN$ with $\angle QPN = \angle NCB$. Show that $\angle BCQ = \frac{1}{2} \angle PQA$.

Let $p(x) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ be a polynomial of odd degree $m > 1$, and define a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{Z}$ such that $p(f(x)) = f(p(x))$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

a) Show that the image of $f$ is finite.

b) If $f$ is non-constant, show that the equation $p(x) = x$ has at least two distinct real roots.

c) Prove that for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n > 1$, there exists a function $f$ with an image of size $n$ and a polynomial $p(x)$ satisfying the given condition.

Let $x = \frac{1}{ab}$, $y = \frac{1}{bc}$, $z = \frac{1}{cd}$, $w = \frac{1}{da}$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z + w = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{xyzw} + 16 \geq 8\sqrt{(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{z})\left(x + z\right)} + 8\sqrt{(\frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{w})\left(y + w\right)}.
$$

a) Let $ m $ be a natural number. Define $ (a_n) $ as the sequence where $ a_n $ is the remainder of $ n $ modulo $ m $. Show that for every base $ k > 1 $, the sequence $ (a_n) $ is $ k $-Computable.

b) If $ (a_n) $ is $ k $-Computable, prove that the shifted sequence $ (b_n) $ with $ b_n = a_{n+1} $ and the doubled index sequence $ (c_n) $ with $ c_n = a_{2n} $ are also $ k $-Computable.

c) Define $ a_n = 1 $ if $ n $ is a perfect square and $ a_n = 0 $ otherwise. Determine whether this sequence is 3-Computable.

d) A modified definition of $ k $-Computable sequences considers input digits provided from left to right. These sequences are termed $ k $-Left Computable. Prove that the original and modified definitions are equivalent.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with altitudes $AD$, $BF$, and $CE$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on line $EF$ such that $EP = DF$ (with $E$ between $P$ and $F$) and $QF = DE$ (with $F$ between $E$ and $Q$). Let the perpendicular bisector of $DQ$ meet $AB$ at $X$ and the perpendicular bisector of $DP$ meet $AC$ at $Y$. Prove that the midpoint of side $BC$ lies on line $XY$.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ and $w$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z + w = 2$. Prove that
$$
\frac{(x+z)^2}{xw+yz} + \frac{(y+w)^2}{xz+yw} + 4 \ge 4 \left( \frac{x+y+1}{z+w+1} + \frac{z+w+1}{x+y+1} \right).
$$

Let $(h_1, h_2, \dots, h_{n+1})$ be a $(n+1)$-tuple of $n$-variable polynomials with real coefficients. Define it as **good** if the following holds: whenever $f_1, f_2, \dots, f_n : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $h_i(f_1(x), f_2(x), \dots, f_n(x))$ being a polynomial in $x$ for each $1 \le i \le n+1$, then all $f_j(x)$ are themselves polynomials.

a) Show that for each positive integer $n$, one can construct a **good** $(n+1)$-tuple where each $h_i$ has degree strictly greater than one.

b) Demonstrate that for no $n > 1$ is there a **good** $(n+1)$-tuple in which all $h_i$ are symmetric in their variables.

\text{In triangle } ABC, \text{ let } \omega_1 \text{ be the circumcircle and let } \angle C = 2\angle B. \text{ A tangent to } \omega_1 \text{ at } A \text{ meets } BC \text{ at } E. \text{ Let } \omega_2 \text{ be a circle through } B \text{ and tangent to } AC \text{ at } C. \text{ This circle intersects } AB \text{ again at } F. \text{ A line through } E \text{ is tangent to } \omega_2 \text{ at } K, \text{ with } BC \text{ between } A \text{ and } K. \text{ Let } M \text{ be the arc midpoint of } BC \text{ on } \omega_1 \text{ (not containing } A). \text{ Prove that } M, F, A, K \text{ lie on a circle.}

Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}^+$ such that the following hold:
* For all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}^+$, $x + y$ divides $f(x) + f(y)$.
* For any integer $x \ge 1395$, $f(x) \le \frac{x^3}{2}$.

Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $AB = AC$. A point $Q$ lies on segment $BC$ and a point $P$ lies on $\omega$ such that $AP = AQ$. If line $AP$ intersects $BC$ at point $R$, show that the tangents from $B$ and $C$ to the incircle of triangle $AQR$, other than the one along $BC$, meet on $\omega$.

Let $\omega_1$ be a circle centered at $O$, and $\omega_2$ be another circle intersecting $\omega_1$ at $A$ and $B$, with $O$ lying on $\omega_2$. Let $S$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $O$ to $AB$. The line $OS$ intersects $\omega_2$ again at $P$. The angle bisector of $\angle ASP$ intersects $\omega_1$ at $L$ such that $A$ and $L$ lie on the same side of $OP$. Let $K$ be a point on $\omega_2$ with $PK = PS$ and $A, K$ on the same side of $OP$. Prove that $SL = KL$.
Find all functions $g : \mathbb{R}^+ \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^+$ such that for all positive real numbers $a$, $b$ $$ \frac{a + g(b)}{a g(b)} = g\left(\frac{1}{b} + g\left(\frac{1}{a}\right)\right) $$

Let $ ABCD $ be an isosceles trapezoid with $ AB \parallel CD $. A point $ P $ lies inside $ ABCD $ such that $ \angle APB > \angle ADC $ and $ \angle DPC > \angle ABC $. Show that the sum of the lengths of the bases $ AB $ and $ CD $ is greater than the sum of the lengths of the legs $ AD $ and $ BC $.

Let $\omega$ be a circle inside triangle $ABC$ tangent to sides $AB$ and $AC$ at $E$ and $F$, respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let the tangents from $M$ to $\omega$ intersect $\omega$ at points $P$ and $Q$, with $P$ and $B$ on the same side of $AM$. Define $X = PM \cap BF$ and $Y = QM \cap CE$. If $BC = 2PM$, prove that the segment $XY$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Let $a$, $b$ be distinct real numbers such that $a^4 - b^4 = a - b$. Prove that
$$
\frac{a - b}{a^6 - b^6} \le \frac{4}{3}(a + b)
$$

Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that satisfy the following conditions:
(a) $f(y + f(x)) - f(x + f(y)) = y - x$, $\forall x, y \in \mathbb{R}$
(b) The set $I = \left\{\frac{f(x)-f(y)}{x-y} \mid x, y \in \mathbb{R}, x \neq y\right\}$ is connected as an interval in $\mathbb{R}$.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ and $AD = BC$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $X$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircle of triangle $APB$ with segment $BC$, and let $Y$ be a point on line $AX$ such that $DY \parallel BC$, with $C$ and $Y$ on opposite sides of $AD$. Show that $\angle YDA = 2 \times \angle YCA$.

Two intersecting circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ have common tangents $AB$ and $CD$, with $A, C$ on $\omega_1$ and $B, D$ on $\omega_2$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. The tangents from $M$ to $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ (excluding $AB$) meet $CD$ at $Y$ and $X$, respectively. If $I$ is the incenter of triangle $MXY$, show that $IC = ID$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be acute with orthocenter $H$, and let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle $BHC$ with center $O'$. Define $\Gamma$ as the circle through the midpoints of $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$. Take an arbitrary point $X$ on the arc $BHC$ of $\omega$, and let line $AX$ meet $\Gamma$ again at point $Y$ such that $X$ lies between $A$ and $Y$. Let $P$ be a point on $\Gamma$ satisfying $PX = PY$. Prove that $\angle O'PX = 90^\circ$.

Let $P(x)$ be a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients satisfying $P(0) = 0$. For every positive real number $M$, show there exists a positive integer $d$ such that if $Q(x)$ is any monic polynomial with degree $\deg Q(x) \geq d$, then the set of integers $k$ satisfying
$$
|P(Q(k))| \leq M
$$
has cardinality at most $\deg Q(x)$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$, let the altitudes from $B$ and $C$ intersect at $H$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $ABC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$. Let $P$ lie on $EF$ such that $HP$ is perpendicular to $HO$, and let $Q$ be a point on $HA$ such that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $HM$. Prove that the segment $QA$ is thrice the segment $QH$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $AB = AC$ and incenter $I$. A circle $\omega$ passes through $C$ and $I$, and is tangent to the angle bisector $AI$. The circle $\omega$ meets $AC$ at $Q$ and the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at $D$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$ and $N$ be the midpoint of $CQ$. Show that the lines $AD$, $MN$, and $BC$ intersect at a common point.

Let $k > 1$ be an integer. Show that there exists a real number $r$ such that for all $1 < m < 1398$:
$$
\{r^m\} < \{r^{m-1}\} \iff m \equiv 0 \pmod{k}.
$$

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$ and $\angle A > 60^\circ$. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$. A point $P$ is on the circumcircle of $\triangle BOC$ such that $BP$ is parallel to $AC$, and a point $K$ is chosen on $AP$ such that $BK = BC$. Show that line $CK$ divides the arc $\widearc{BC}$ (not containing $O$) on the circumcircle of $\triangle BOC$ into two equal parts.
Let $n > 2$ be a natural number. Prove that the equation $\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^2 = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^3$ has no solution in positive integers $x_i > 1$.

Let $n > 0$ be an integer. We say $n$ is interesting if, for every permutation $\tau$ of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, there exist polynomials $Q_1, Q_2, \dots, Q_n$ and a positive real number $\delta$ such that:
$$
\text{i)}\ Q_1(0) = Q_2(0) = \dots = Q_n(0),
$$
$$
\text{ii)}\ Q_1(x) > Q_2(x) > \dots > Q_n(x) \text{ for } -\delta < x < 0,
$$
$$
\text{iii)}\ Q_{\tau(1)}(x) > Q_{\tau(2)}(x) > \dots > Q_{\tau(n)}(x) \text{ for } 0 < x < \delta.
$$
Determine all such interesting numbers.

Let $g : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function satisfying the condition that for any non-empty subsets $A, B \subseteq [0, 1]$ such that $A \cup B = [0, 1]$ and $A \cap B = \emptyset$, it holds that either $\exists x \in A : g(x) \in B$ or $\exists x \in B : g(x) \in A$. Suppose further that $g(x) > x$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$. Show that there exist infinitely many $x$ in $[0, 1]$ with $g(x) = 1$.

Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be non-zero distinct real numbers. Suppose there exist functions $F$, $G : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
\alpha F\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) + \beta F(xy) = \gamma F(x) + G(y)
$$
for all positive real $x$ and for $y > Y$, where $Y$ is a fixed positive constant.
Show that there exists a function $H : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$
F(xy) + F\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = 2F(x) + H(y)
$$
for all $x > 0$ and $y > Y$.

Define a set $ S \subseteq \mathbb{N} $ as *good* if for any distinct $ a, b, c \in S $, every positive divisor of $ \frac{a^c - b^c}{a - b} $ is also in $ S $. Prove that for all integers $ n > 1 $, there exists a good set $ S $ that does not contain $ n $.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with circumcenter $O$. Let $P$ be the intersection of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Define $M$ and $N$ as midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$, respectively. Let $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$ be the circumcircles of triangles $ADP$, $BCP$, and $OMN$, respectively. Let $E$ be the second intersection of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_3$, and $F$ the second intersection of $\omega_2$ and $\omega_3$. Prove that $OE = OF$.

Let $n \ge 6$ be an integer and let $P_1, P_2, \dots, P_n$ be points in the plane with no three colinear. A "connected infrastructure" is defined as a connected graph with vertex set $\{P_1, \dots, P_n\}$, straight-line edges, and no intersecting edges. Show that there exist three such infrastructures $G_1, G_2, G_3$ such that the edge sets of $G_1, G_2, G_3$ are pairwise disjoint.

Let $n$ be a natural number with $n \ge 3$. Determine the largest natural number $k$ such that there exist real numbers $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n \in [0, 1)$ for which every integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le k$ can be expressed as the sum of some subset of the $x_i$'s.

Given an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $AB = BC$, let $P$ be a point on the altitude from $B$. The circumcircle of triangle $BAP$ intersects $AC$ again at $M$. Let $N$ be the point symmetric to $M$ with respect to the midpoint of $AC$. If $NP$ intersects the circumcircle of $BAP$ again at $X$ and $AB$ intersects the circumcircle of $NAP$ again at $Y$, then let $Z$ be the point where the tangent at $A$ to the circumcircle of $NAP$ meets $BP$. Prove that $CZ$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $XYP$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have incenter $I$ and let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ (not containing $A$) of the circumcircle of $ABC$. Let $X$ lie on the external bisector of $\angle BAC$, and suppose that line $BX$ intersects the circumcircle of triangle $BIC$ again at $T$. Let $Y$ be a point on the circumcircle of $ABC$ such that $MY = MA$. Prove that $AY$ is parallel to $TC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with midpoints $M$ and $N$ on $AB$ and $AC$. Let the second intersections of $BN$ and $CM$ with the circumcircle of $ABC$ be $N'$ and $M'$, respectively. Suppose points $X$ and $Y$ lie on the line $BC$ extended such that $B$ lies between $X$ and $C$, and $C$ lies between $B$ and $Y$. If

$$
\angle M'XB = \angle MAC, \angle N'YC = \angle NBA
$$

show that $AX = AY$.

Let $x, y, z$ be natural numbers such that $y > x > 1$ and $\gcd(z, xy) = 1$. Prove that there exists a natural number $n$ such that
$$
z \mid \binom{y^n}{x^n}
$$

In triangle $ABC$ with $\angle A > 90^\circ$, let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $B$ and $C$ to the opposite sides. Tangents at $B$ and $C$ to the circumcircle of $ABC$ meet line $EF$ at points $K$ and $L$, respectively. Suppose $\angle CLB = 135^\circ$. Let $R$ be a point on $BK$ such that $KR = KL$, and let $S$ be a point on the extension of $BK$ beyond $K$ with $\angle BLS = 135^\circ$. Prove that the circle with diameter $RS$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n \ge 4$. Consider all permutations $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ of the integers $1, 2, \dots, n$. For each such permutation, compute the sum
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} i a_i
$$
and record its value. How many unique results will be obtained in total?

Find all sequences $(b_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of positive integers such that for every $n \ge 3$ we have:
$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n-2} \frac{1}{b_k b_{k+2}} = 1 - \frac{1}{\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} b_k^2}
$$

\text{Suppose } n > 10 \text{ lines are drawn in the plane such that no two are parallel and no three meet at a point. At least } \frac{n^2}{8} + 1 \text{ of the bounded regions are colored black. A triangle is *good* if it contains exactly one black region. Show that the number of good triangles is at least } \frac{n}{2}.

Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $a, b, c$ opposite to $A, B, C$, respectively. The internal angle bisectors from $A, B, C$ intersect the opposite sides at $D, E, F$, and let the lengths of $AD, BE, CF$ be $d, e, f$, respectively. Show that
$$
def = \frac{4abc(a+b+c)\Delta}{(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)},
$$
where $\Delta$ is the area of triangle $ABC$.

Let $k$ and $m$ be nonnegative integers such that $k \le m$.

a. Prove that
$$
\frac{m+1-2k}{m+1-k} \binom{m}{k}
$$
is an integer.

b. Prove that
$$
\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor} \frac{m+1-2k}{m+1-k} \binom{m}{k} < 2^{m-2}
$$
for all $m \ge 9$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $f_k(n)$ for $k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ as the number of sequences $x_1, \dots, x_n$ with $x_i \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$ such that the sum of the sequence satisfies
$$
\sum_{i=1}^n x_i \equiv k \mod 4.
$$

a. Show that $f_1(n) = f_3(n)$ for all positive integers $n$.

b. Show that
$$
f_0(n) = \frac{3^n + 2 + (-1)^n}{4}.
$$

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Suppose $D$ lies on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ that contains $A$. Show
$$
|AB| + |AC| \ge |DB| + |DC|
$$
with equality if and only if $D = A$. Hence, deduce that among all triangles inscribed in a fixed circle, the equilateral triangle has the largest perimeter.

Let $\triangle ABC$ satisfy $|AB| < |AC|$. Let $D$ and $E$ be the points where the internal angle bisectors from $B$ and $C$ meet $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Suppose that $I$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$. Prove that $|IE| = |ID|$ is equivalent to $\angle BAC = 60^\circ$.
Let $ABCD$ be a square with a point $P$ inside it such that $PA = 3$, $PB = 7$, and $PD = 5$. Determine the area of the square.

Let triangle $ABC$ lie in the plane. For $\lambda \ge 0$, define a point $D(\lambda)$ on segment $BC$ such that $\frac{BD(\lambda)}{DC(\lambda)} = \frac{c^\lambda}{b^\lambda}$. Show that
$$
|AD(\lambda)| \le |AD(2 - \lambda)| \quad \text{holds if and only if} \quad \lambda \ge 1.
$$

In an equilateral triangle $ABC$, a line is drawn from $A$ intersecting $BC$ at $D$ and the circumcircle at $P$. Prove that
$$
\frac{1}{|PD|} = \frac{1}{|PB|} + \frac{1}{|PC|}
$$

In the country of Harpland, coins are of three colors: green, white, and orange, and each has a positive integer shilling value. These coins are arranged in an equilateral triangle with side length $n$, satisfying the following conditions: 1. adjacent coins are never of the same color; 2. the sum of coin values along any line parallel to a side is a multiple of three. Show that the sum of the values of the green coins is also divisible by three.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $P$ the midpoint of $BC$. Points $M$ and $N$ lie on segments $AB$ and $AC$ respectively, and the line $MN$ intersects the segment $AP$ at point $D$. If $|AD| = |DM| = 2|DN|$, prove that $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $|AC| = |BC|$.

In triangle $ABC$, let $AD$ and $BE$ be the internal angle bisectors of $\angle A$ and $\angle B$, respectively, with $D$ on $BC$ and $E$ on $AC$. Let $M$ be on $BC$ such that $CM = AE$, and let $N$ be on $AC$ such that $CN = BD$. Prove that $D, E, M, N$ lie on a circle if and only if triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = AC$.
Determine all cubic polynomials $f(x) = x^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$, with real coefficients $b, c, d$, such that $f(x^2 - 2) = -f(-x)f(x)$.

Two non-intersecting circles are touched by a common external tangent at points $T$ and $T'$. The transverse tangents intersect the segment $TT'$ at points $A$ and $B$. Show that
$$
|AT| = |BT'|
$$

The function $\mu(a, b)$ for two real numbers $a$ and $b$ is defined by
$$
\mu(a, b) = \begin{cases} a, & \text{if } a \ge b, \\ b, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$
Let $x_0 > 0$, $x_1 > 0$ be any positive real numbers. A sequence $x_n$ is defined recursively by
$$
x_{n+1} = \frac{4 \mu(x_n, 4)}{x_{n-1}}, \quad \text{for } n \ge 1.
$$
Compute $x_{2010}$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be given. The circle centered at $A$ and tangent to side $BC$ meets the circle centered at $C$ and tangent to side $AB$ at points $M$ and $N$. Prove that $M$, $N$, and $B$ lie on a straight line precisely when $AB = BC$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have area $1$. Let $P$ be the midpoint of side $BC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be points on $AB$ and $AC$ such that $AM : MB = 2 : 1$ and $CN : AN = 2 : 1$. If $AP$ intersects $MN$ at $D$, determine the area of triangle $ADN$.

Let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\mathbb{R}$, and suppose its graph is symmetric with respect to the vertical lines $x = 1/4$ and $x = 3/4$. Show that $f(x) = f(x + 1)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Provide a non-constant, nonnegative function satisfying these symmetries.

Let the sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ be defined by $a_0 = 1$, $a_1 = 3$, and $a_{n+1} = a_n + a_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$. Determine all integers $n \ge 1$ such that the greatest common divisor of $n a_{n+1} + a_n$ and $n a_n + a_{n-1}$ is greater than 1.
\text{Let } x, y, z > 0 \text{ satisfy } xy + yz + zx + 2xyz = 1. \text{ Show that there exist } a, b, c > 0 \text{ with } x = \frac{a}{b+c}, y = \frac{b}{c+a}, z = \frac{c}{a+b}.

Let $x = a$, $y = b$, $z = c$, and $w = d$ be positive real numbers. Show that
$$
\frac{x^2}{y+z+w} + \frac{y^2}{x+z+w} + \frac{z^2}{x+y+w} \ge \frac{4x + 4y + 4z - 3w}{9}.
$$

Let triangle $ABC$ have side lengths $a = |BC|$, $b = |CA|$, $c = |AB|$, and let $m_a$, $m_b$, $m_c$ be the lengths of the medians from vertices $A$, $B$, $C$ to the midpoints of the opposite sides.

a. Prove that $2m_a < b + c$. From this, infer that $m_a + m_b + m_c < a + b + c$.

b. Construct a triangle where $m_a > \sqrt{bc}$, and another where $m_a \le \sqrt{bc}$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Points $B'$ and $C'$ lie on the line through $BC$, extended beyond $B$ and $C$ respectively, with $B$ between $B'$ and $C$ and $C$ between $B$ and $C'$. Additionally, $B'BA$ and $ACC'$ are isosceles. Let $X$ be a point on $BC$ such that $X$ lies on the side of $B$ opposite $B'$. Show that $|AX| = |BX|$ if and only if $\frac{1}{|AB|} = \frac{1}{|B'X|} + \frac{1}{|BC'|}$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $|AB| = |AC|$. Points $D, E$, and $F$ lie on $BC, CA$, and $AB$, respectively, such that $\angle FDE = \angle ABC$ and $FE \nparallel BC$. Prove that the circumcircle of $\triangle DEF$ is tangent to $BC$ if and only if $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$.

\text{a. Let } f(x) = x^2 + 8. \text{ Prove that } f(x\sqrt{2}) \text{ is the product } P(x)Q(x) \text{ of two quadratic polynomials with coefficients in } \mathbb{Z}.\\\text{b. Let } g(x) = x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + x + 1. \text{ Prove that } g(5x^2) \text{ is the product } R(x)S(x) \text{ of two polynomials of degree four with coefficients in } \mathbb{Z}.\\\text{c. Let } h(x) = (x+1)^{13} - x^{13} - 1. \text{ Prove that } h(x) \text{ is the product } T(x)U(x) \text{ of two polynomials of degree six with coefficients in } \mathbb{Z}.

For which real values of $\lambda$ do there exist positive real numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ such that
$$
\frac{1}{a} + a = 2(1 + \lambda),
$$
$$
\frac{1}{c} + c = 2(1 + \lambda),
$$
$$
\frac{1}{a} + b = 2(1 - \lambda),
$$
$$
\frac{1}{b} + c = 2(1 - \lambda)?
$$
Find the values of $a$, $b$, and $c$ for each valid $\lambda$.

Let $x_1, x_2, x_3, \dots, y_1, y_2, y_3, \dots$ and $z_1, z_2, z_3, \dots$ be three sequences such that each term is either $+1$ or $-1$. Prove that the inequality $$ 3 \sum_{i=1}^{2014} x_i y_i + 3 \sum_{i=1}^{2014} y_i z_i \le \sum_{i=1}^{2014} x_i^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{2014} y_i^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{2014} z_i^2 + 3 \sum_{i=1}^{2014} x_i z_i $$ is true.

Let $ABCD$ be a square inscribed in a circle centered at $O$. Suppose $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. The line through $C$ and $E$ intersects the circle again at $F$. The lines $FB$ and $AD$ intersect at $H$. Show that $|HD| = 2|AH|$.

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and $r$ satisfy $r^3 = 2$. Prove that there do not exist rational numbers $b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{n-1}$, not all of them equal to zero, such that
$$
b_0 + b_1 r + b_2 r^2 + \dots + b_{n-1} r^{n-1} = 0.
$$

Let $x_1 = 1$, $y_1 = 0$, $z_1 = 1$ and define for all $n \ge 1$\begin{align*}x_{n+1} = x_n + 2y_n, \quad y_{n+1} = y_n + 2z_n, \quad z_{n+1} = x_n + z_n.\end{align*}Find integers $P$, $Q$, $R$ such that $x_{n+3} = Px_{n+2} + Qx_{n+1} + Rx_n$ for all $n \ge 1$.

Let triangle $ABC$ have side $BC$ as its longest side. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on segments $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, satisfying $|AD| = |AE|$. Points $F$ and $G$ are located on segment $BC$ with $|BD| = |BG|$ and $|CF| = |CE|$. Prove that the points $D$, $E$, $F$, and $G$ lie on a single circle.
Show that $||1-4t^2|-3|t|| \le \frac{3}{2}$ for all real numbers $t$ in the interval $[-1, 1]$.

Let $a, b, c$ be non-negative real numbers with $a + b + c \le 1$. Prove that
$$
6abc \le a(1-a) + b(1-b) + c(1-c),
$$
and characterize when equality occurs.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle BAC < 90^\circ$. Drop perpendiculars from $C$ to $AB$ and from $B$ to $AC$, and let these lines intersect the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ again at $D$ and $E$, respectively. If the segment $DE$ is congruent to $BC$, determine the measure of angle $\angle BAC$.

Determine all integer solutions $(x, y)$ to the equation $x^2 + y^2 = 65$. Use these solutions to verify the inequality
$$
\frac{4 + 6\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{65}} < \pi < \frac{4}{11}(3 + \sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{5}).
$$

Let $\{a_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be a sequence of real numbers such that for every integer $n$,
$$
a_{n+3} = \frac{a_n + a_{n+1} + a_{n+2}}{3}.
$$
Prove that if $\{a_n\}$ is bounded (i.e., there exists $R > 0$ such that $|a_n| \le R$ for all $n$), then the sequence is constant.

Let $(a_n)_{n=0}^\infty$ be defined by $a_0 = 2$ and
$$
a_n = \frac{2a_{n-1} + 1}{a_{n-1} + 2}, \text{ for } n \geq 1.$$
Show that for all positive integers $n$,
$$1 < a_n < 1 + \frac{2}{3^n}.$$

Let $z$ be a complex number such that $z^k = 1$ for some positive integer $k$. Define $S_n$ as the set of such $z$ of the form $\frac{a+bi}{\sqrt{n}}$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$ and $a, b$ are positive integers. (i) Show that the number of distinct elements in $S_n$ is strictly less than $\sqrt{n}$. (ii) Demonstrate that $S_5 = \emptyset$.
Find the equations of the lines that are tangent to both circles defined by $x^2 + y^2 = 2r$ and $(x - 0)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 1$.

Consider an equilateral triangle subdivided into smaller equilateral triangles with side length $1$, forming a grid of triangles for side length $n \ge 1$. Assign each vertex of the grid one of two colors (red or blue) such that no triangle of any size has all three vertices of the same color. Let $f(n)$ be the total number of such colorings. Determine $f(n)$ for all $n \ge 1$.
Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers such that $x \ge 0$ and $y^2 - x(x+1) \ge 0$. Show that $(y-1)^2 - x(x-1) \ge 0$.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Extend $CA$ to a point $D$ such that $A$ lies between $C$ and $D$, and extend $AB$ to a point $E$ such that $B$ lies between $A$ and $E$, with the condition that $|MD| = |ME|$. Let $F$ be the point where $MD$ intersects $AB$. Show that $\angle BFM = \angle BME$.

Determine all quadratic functions $f(x) = a x^2 + b x + c$, where $a \neq 0$, satisfying
$$
f(f(1)) = f(f(0)) = f(f(-1)).
$$

Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{2020}$ be non-negative real numbers satisfying
$$
a_i + a_{i+1} + a_{i+2} \le 2 \quad \text{for } i = 1, 2, \dots, 2018.
$$
Prove that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{2018} a_i a_{i+2} \le 1009.
$$

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be the side lengths of an isosceles triangle with area $\Delta$. Prove that
$$
\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 - 4\Delta} + \sqrt{x^2 + z^2 - 4\Delta} \ge \sqrt{y^2 + z^2 - 4\Delta}.
$$
Determine when equality holds.

A cyclic trapezium $ABCD$ has $AB$ parallel to $DC$. Let the extensions of $DA$ and $CB$ meet at point $P$, and let the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$. Prove that the product of the distances $|OE|$ and $|OP|$ equals the square of the radius $R$ of the circle.

Let $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy the condition
$$
f(x + y) = f(f(x)) + f(f(y))
$$
for all integers $x, y$. Determine all possible values of $f(2020)$.

Let $d_1 = 1 < d_2 < d_3 < \dots < d_k = N$ be the list of all positive divisors of a positive integer $N$. Determine all $N$ such that $$ N = d_3d_4d_7 \quad \text{and} \quad d_3d_4 < d_7. $$ Verify that $N = 2020$ satisfies these conditions.

Let $N$, $k$ be positive integers with $k \le N$. Consider an $(N, k)$-Mountain Tetris mini-game on an $N \times N$ grid. A path from $(0, 0)$ to $(N, N)$ is called *ascending* if it is made of horizontal and vertical segments and never goes down or back. Each game starts with a mountain having an ascending path with exactly $k$ horizontal and $k$ vertical segments. A $1 \times 1$-square rock falls from a randomly chosen column at the top of the grid. The player can shift the rock right by one unit in each *move*. The game is won if the player makes the minimum number of moves to ensure the rock lands on the mountain such that the new shape still forms an ascending path. Prove that the average number of moves required across all such games is $$\frac{N-k}{k+1}.$$

Let $x, y, z$ be the side lengths of a triangle. Prove that
$$
x^2 + y^2 + z^2 \leq x \max(y, z) + y \max(z, x) + z \max(x, y)
$$
and show that equality holds precisely when $x = y = z$.
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB + CD = AD + BC$. Show that $ABCD$ is tangential, i.e., it admits an incircle tangent to all four sides.

Let $n$ be an integer with at least three digits. Define $T(n)$ as the number formed by moving the first two digits of $n$ to the end. For instance, $T(12345) = 34512$ and $T(100) = 10$. Determine all such $n$ for which the equation $T(n) = 9n$ holds true.

Let $P$ be a point on the hypotenuse $AB$ of a right triangle $\triangle ABC$ with right angle at $C$. From $P$, draw lines parallel to the legs $AC$ and $BC$, intersecting $BC$ at $D$ and $AC$ at $E$. Show that $|BP| \cdot |AP| = |BD| \cdot |CD| + |AE| \cdot |CE|$.

Let $f : [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ satisfy the functional equation:
$$
f(f(x)) = \frac{3x}{x+3}, \text{ for all } x \ge 0.
$$
Additionally, $f(x) = \frac{x+1}{2}$ for $2 \le x \le 3$.

a. Determine $f(2021)$.
b. Determine $f\left(\frac{1}{2021}\right)$.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be the sides of triangle $ABC$, and let $S$ be its area. If $s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}$, prove that
$$
\frac{a + b + c}{2} < \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - 4S} + \sqrt{b^2 + c^2 - 4S} + \sqrt{c^2 + a^2 - 4S}.
$$

Let triangle $ABC$ have the internal angle bisector of $\angle ACB$ intersecting $AB$ at point $D$, and the external angle bisector intersecting $AB$ at point $E$. If $CD$ is a median of triangle $AEC$, and $B$ lies between $A$ and $D$, prove that $AC = 3BC$.

Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer and let $(a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots, a_n)$ be a permutation of $\{1, 2, 3, \dots, n\}$. A value $a_t$ is called a *turning point* if $2 \le t \le n-1$ and
$$
(a_t - a_{t-1})(a_t - a_{t+1}) > 0.
$$
For fixed $n$, define $q(n)$ as the number of such permutations with precisely one turning point.
Determine all $n \ge 3$ for which $q(n)$ is a perfect square.
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying $$ f(f(x) + y) = x + f(y) $$ for all integers $x, y$.
Determine all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that $5a! = b! + 4c!$.
Let $ N $ be a positive integer, and let $ R(N) $ represent the number formed by reversing the digits of $ N $. Find all such $ N $ where $ N - R(N) = 9 $.

Show that for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$
 x^4 + y^4 + 18 - 12xy \ge 0.
$$
When is the expression equal to zero?

Let $ k $ be a positive integer and define a sequence $ a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots $ recursively by
$$
\begin{align*}
 a_0 &= 0 \\
 a_1 &= 1 \\
 a_{n+1} &= ka_n + a_{n-1} \quad \text{for all } n \ge 1.
\end{align*}
$$

a. If $ k = 1 $, show that $ a_{n-1}a_{n+1} $ is not a perfect square for $ n \ge 2 $.

b. For all $ k \ge 1 $, show that $ a_{n-1}a_{n+1} $ is not a perfect square for $ n \ge 2 $.
Show that $\sum_{m=1}^{M} \frac{1}{m(m+1)} \sum_{k=1}^{m+1} \frac{1}{k} < 2$.

Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of positive integers. Suppose a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfies for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$: (i) $f(n + 1) > f(n)$; (ii) $f(f(f(n))) = 4n$. Determine $f(2022)$.

Let $S = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and define $g : S \to \mathbb{R}$ by
$$
g(x, y) = y\sqrt{1-x^2} + x\sqrt{1-y^2}.
$$
Show that $g(S) = [0, 1]$. Determine whether $g$ is injective on $S$.

Let square $ABCD$ be given, with $\Gamma$ as the circle having $CD$ as its diameter. A tangent from $B$ to $\Gamma$ touches the circle at $E$ and intersects $AD$ at $K$. Prove that the length of segment $AD$ is four times the length of segment $KD$.

Let $AOB$ be a right triangle with $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$. A sequence of points $X_1, X_2, X_3, \dots, X_{2022}$ is defined such that:
* $X_1$ is on ray $\vec{OA}$ with $|OX_1| = 1$,
* $X_2$ is on ray $\vec{OB}$ with $|X_1X_2| = 2$,
* For $n \geq 3$, each $X_n$ alternates between $\vec{OA}$ and $\vec{OB}$, with $|X_{n-1}X_n| = n$.
Determine $|X_{2020}X_{2022}|$.

Aisling and Brendan play a turn-based game starting with the number $x = 2023$. Aisling moves first. On each turn, a player can either increment $x$ by 1 or divide $x$ by one of its prime factors $p$. The player who writes the number $x = 1$ wins. Determine which player has a winning strategy.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z = 3$. Show that
$$
\frac{x+y}{z+2} + \frac{y+z}{x+2} + \frac{z+x}{y+2} \ge 2
$$
and find the condition for equality.

Let $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$, $T$ be points on a circle with $|PQ| = |RS|$ and $|QR| = |ST|$. The chords $PS$ and $QT$ meet at $U$. Let $N$ be the midpoint of $RS$. Prove that the circle centered at $N$ with radius $NT$ also passes through the midpoint of $PU$.

In triangle $ABC$, where $\angle BAC < 90^\circ$, let $D$ be on the side of line $AB$ opposite $C$ such that triangle $ADB$ is isosceles with $|AD| = |BD|$ and right-angled at $D$. Similarly, let $E$ be on the side of line $AC$ opposite $B$ such that triangle $AEC$ is isosceles with $|AE| = |CE|$ and right-angled at $E$. If $X$ is the point such that quadrilateral $ADXE$ is a parallelogram, show that $|BX| = |CX|$.
Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $b = c$. Prove that $a^2 < 4bc$. Provide an example of a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $a$ for which the inequality does not hold.

Let $a, b, c, d$ be positive integers such that
$$
(i) a + b + c + d = 2023
$$
$$
(ii) ab \equiv cd \pmod{2023}
$$
$$
(iii) a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2 \equiv 0 \pmod{2023}.
$$
If $a, b, c, d$ are all divisible by 7, show that they are all divisible by 17.

Let $a, b, c, d$ be real numbers such that $-1 \leq a, b, c, d \leq 1$. Show that
$$
|ad + bc + ca - db| \leq 2
$$
and identify when equality holds.

Let $ Q $ be a cyclic quadrilateral with vertices $ A, B, C, D $. Show that the maximum diagonal of $ Q $ is at most $ \sqrt{2} $ times the maximum side length, with equality if and only if $ Q $ is a square.

Let $N(x, y) = x^2 - xy + y^2$ for any real numbers $x, y$.

a. Prove that $N(a, b)N(x, y) = N(ax - by, ay + bx - by)$.

b. Demonstrate that the equation $N(x, y) = 2023 - 490z^2$ has at least 16 distinct non-negative integer solutions $(x, y, z)$.

For $n \ge 3$, define a *special $n$-triangle* as a triangle with $n$ unique numbers on each side, all distinct, such that the total sum on each side is equal. For example, the triangle
$$
\begin{array}{c c c}
& 41 & \\
23 & 19 & \\
43 & 17 & 47
\end{array}
$$
is a special 3-triangle since all side sums are equal. A special $n$-triangle contains $3(n-1)$ elements in total. An infinite set $A$ is *special* if, for all $n \ge 3$, the $3(n-1)$ smallest elements of $A$ can form a special $n$-triangle. Prove that the set of all positive integers not divisible by 2023 is a special set.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezium inscribed in a circle with centre $O$, where $AB \parallel DC$ and $|AB| < |DC|$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $P$ such that $\angle APC = 90^\circ$. If $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $DC$ respectively, show that $|OF| = |PE|$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $BD \perp AB$. Let $P$ lie on segment $BC$ such that $|PD| = |BE|$, where $E$ is the intersection of $BD$ and $AP$. Let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to $BD$. Show that
$$
\frac{|AB|}{|PF|} = \sqrt{2}.
$$

Let $b_0, b_1, b_2, \dots$ be an arithmetic progression of positive integers. A hexagon is called equiangular if all its internal angles are congruent.
