For each $j \ge 0$, determine the number of non-congruent equiangular hexagons whose sides are the six consecutive terms $b_j, b_{j+1}, b_{j+2}, b_{j+3}, b_{j+4}, b_{j+5}$ arranged in some order.

Find all positive integers $n$ and $m$ such that
$$
\binom{n}{3} + n = 2^m.
$$

A system consists of $n$ switches, each capable of being in one of three positions, numbered 1 through 3, with $n > 1$. Initially, all switches are in position 1, and the goal is to bring all to position 2. A specific sequence of $n + 1$ single-switch position changes achieves this. Let $c_n$ denote the number of such $n + 1$-step sequences, excluding the specific one shown, where sequences are distinct only if they differ in order or content. Prove that $c_n$ has no divisor $k$ with $1 < k < n+2$, and $n+2$ divides $c_n$ if and only if $n+2$ is prime.

Let $\triangle ABC$ satisfy $|AB| < |AC| < |BC|$, and let $I$ be its incenter. The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ meets $BC$ and $AC$ at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Let $R$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and define $N$ on $DE$ such that $|RN| = |RE|$. If $Q$ is the midpoint of $ND$, and $P$ is the intersection of $AN$ and $RQ$, show that $I, N, P, Q$ are concyclic.
Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be real numbers with $x + y + z = 1$ and $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1$. Show that $x^3 + y^3 + z^3 \le 1$.

In un test matematico, $N<40$ studenti partecipano. Il punteggio minimo per il superamento del test è 65. I dati aggregati sono: media generale 66, media dei superati 71 e media dei non superati 56. A causa di un errore, tutti i punteggi vengono incrementati di 5, risultando in una media di 75 per i superati e 59 per i non superati.
a) Determinare tutti i valori possibili di $N$.
b) Determinare tutti i valori possibili di $N$ nel caso in cui, dopo l'aumento, la media dei superati fosse 79 e quella dei non superati 47.

\text{Definiamo due polinomi a coefficienti interi } p \text{ e } q \text{ simili se hanno lo stesso grado e lo stesso insieme di coefficienti, ma in ordine diverso.}\\\text{a. Mostrare che se } p \text{ e } q \text{ sono simili, allora } p(2007)-q(2007) \text{ è divisibile per } 2.\\\text{b. Esistono interi } k>2 \text{ tali che, per ogni coppia di polinomi simili } p \text{ e } q, p(2007)-q(2007) \text{ è divisibile per } k?

Sia $ABC$ un triangolo con baricentro $G$. Sia $D$ un punto su $AG$ distinto da $A$ tale che $GD = AG$, e $E$ un punto su $GB$ distinto da $B$ tale che $GE = GB$. Sia $M$ il punto medio di $AB$. Dimostrare che $BMCD$ è ciclico se e solo se $BA = BE$.

Determinare i valori di $n \geq 3$ per cui esistono $n$ numeri interi positivi $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ tali che ogni coppia $a_i, a_j$ abbia un divisore comune maggiore di 1, ma ogni terna $a_i, a_j, a_k$ abbia $\gcd(a_i, a_j, a_k) = 1$. Supponendo che ogni $a_i < 5000$, trovare il valore massimo di $n$.

Per ogni intero $n \geq 2$, determinare:
a. il più grande numero reale $c_{n}$ tale che
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{1 + x_i} \geq c_{n}
$$
per ogni scelta di numeri reali positivi $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$ tali che $\prod_{i=1}^{n} x_i = 1$;
b. il più grande numero reale $d_{n}$ tale che
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{1}{1 + 2 x_i} \geq d_{n}
$$
per ogni scelta di numeri reali positivi $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}$ tali che $\prod_{i=1}^{n} x_i = 1$.

Sia $ABCD$ un quadrato di lato unitario. Si considerino due punti $M$ e $N$ sui lati $AB$ e $AD$ rispettivamente, tali che $AM = AN = x$, con $0 < x < 1$. Determinare il valore massimo dell'area del quadrilatero $CDNM$.

(A) $\frac{1}{2}$
(B) $\frac{9}{16}$
(C) $\frac{19}{32}$
(D) $\frac{5}{8}$
(E) $\frac{2}{3}$

Sia $p$ un numero primo. Trovare tutte le coppie ordinate $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ tali che:
$$
\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{p}
$$

Sia $X$ l'insieme dei numeri naturali in base dieci che non sono fatti di una singola cifra ripetuta. Per ogni $n \in X$, consideriamo $A_n$ l'insieme di tutti i numeri generati permutando le cifre di $n$ in tutti i modi possibili. Sia $d_n$ il massimo comune divisore di tutti gli elementi di $A_n$. Ad esempio, se $n=1120$, allora $A_{1120}$ include $\{112, 121, 211, 1012, 1021, 1102, 1120, 1201, 1210, 2011, 2101, 2110\}$ e $d_{1120} = 1$. Determinare il valore massimo che $d_n$ può assumere.

Sia $x$ un numero reale positivo e denotiamo con $\lfloor x \rfloor$ la parte intera di $x$, ovvero il più grande intero $m$ tale che $m \leq x$. Determinare il valore della somma $\sum_{k=1}^{1000000} \lfloor \sqrt{k} \rfloor$.

[Suggerimento: Si può utilizzare la formula $\sum_{i=1}^k i^2 = \frac{k(k+1)(2k+1)}{6}$, senza doverla dimostrare.]

Sia $ABCD$ un trapezio con base maggiore $AB$ e diagonali $AC$ e $BD$ perpendicolari. Sia $O$ il centro del cerchio circoscritto a $\triangle ABC$, e sia $E$ l'intersezione di $OB$ con $CD$. Dimostrare che $$\overline{BC}^2 = \overline{CD} \cdot \overline{CE}$$

Sia $f: \mathbb{Z}^+ \to \mathbb{Z}^+$ una funzione. Diciamo che:
- $f$ è crescente se $n < m$ implica $f(n) < f(m)$,
- $f$ è moltiplicativa se $\gcd(n, m) = 1$ implica $f(nm) = f(n)f(m)$,
- $f$ è completamente moltiplicativa se $f(nm) = f(n)f(m)$ per tutti $n, m$.

a. Mostrare che se $f$ è crescente, allora $f(n) \geq n$ per ogni $n$.

b. Mostrare che se $f$ è crescente, completamente moltiplicativa e $f(2) = 2$, allora $f(n) = n$ per ogni $n$.

c. Rimane vera la conclusione (b) se si toglie la parola "completamente"?
Sia $R$ un rettangolo di dimensioni $a$ e $b$ con $a > b$. Determinare l'area del triangolo formato dall'intersezione dei due triangoli che si generano piegando $R$ lungo una sua diagonale.
Sia $R$ un rettangolo di dimensioni $a$ e $b$ con $a > b$. Determinare l'area del triangolo formato dall'intersezione dei due triangoli che si generano piegando $R$ lungo una sua diagonale.

Siano $\mathcal{C}$, $\mathcal{C}_1$, $\mathcal{C}_2$, tre circonferenze con raggi $R$, $a$, $b$ tali che $0 < a < b < R$. $\mathcal{C}_1$ e $\mathcal{C}_2$ sono tangenti internamente a $\mathcal{C}$ nei punti $A$ e $B$, e si intersecano in due punti diversi. Mostrare che il segmento $AB$ contiene uno dei punti comuni tra $\mathcal{C}_1$ e $\mathcal{C}_2$ se e solo se $a + b = R$.

\text{a. Trovare tutte le soluzioni intere positive }(x, k)\text{ dell'equazione }x^{3}+1=3^{k}.
\text{b. Mostrare che se }n\in\mathbb{N}, n>1\text{ e }n\ne 3\text{, allora non esistono soluzioni intere positive }(x, k)\text{ dell'equazione }x^{n}+1=3^{k}.

\text{a. Trovare tutte le coppie }(x, k)\text{ di interi positivi tali che }x^{3}+1=3^{k}.\text{ b. Mostrare che se }n\text{ è un intero maggiore di 1 e }n\neq 3\text{ allora non esistono coppie }(x, k)\text{ di interi positivi che soddisfano }x^{n}+1=3^{k}.

Quale tra le seguenti proprietà è soddisfatta nell'insieme $\mathbb{Q}$?
(A) $ orall x \in \mathbb{Q}, \exists y \in \mathbb{Q} 	ext{ t.c. }  orall z \in \mathbb{Q}, x + y + z = x$
(B) $ orall x \in \mathbb{Q}, \exists y \in \mathbb{Q} 	ext{ t.c. }  orall z \in \mathbb{Q}, x + y + z = z$
(C) $ orall x \in \mathbb{Q}, \exists y \in \mathbb{Q} 	ext{ t.c. }  orall z \in \mathbb{Q}, x y z = x$
(D) $ orall x \in \mathbb{Q}, \exists y \in \mathbb{Q} 	ext{ t.c. }  orall z \in \mathbb{Q}, x y z = z$

Quanti sono i numeri interi positivi $x$ per cui $x^{x} = 2^{x} + x^{2} + 10$?\text{(A) Nessuna}\text{(B) una}\text{(C) due}\text{(D) più di due, ma un numero finito}\text{(E) infinite}.

Sia $\lfloor x \rfloor$ la parte intera di $x$, definita come il massimo intero minore o uguale a $x$. Determinare il numero di soluzioni reali positive $x > 0$ dell'equazione $2^{5x} = 2^{6\lfloor x \rfloor}$.
\text{Determinare tutti i valori interi relativi di } (a, b) \text{ tali che } a^3 + b^3 = 91

Sia $A$ l'area del sottoinsieme del piano formato dai punti $(x, y)$ tali che $x^{2}+y^{2} \leq 100$ e $\sqrt{17} y \leq -\pi x$. Allora:
(A) $A<100$
(B) $100 \leq A<150$
(C) $150 \leq A<200$
(D) $200 \leq A<250$
(E) $A \geq 250$

Una piramide di vertice $V$ e base un quadrilatero $ABCD$ è inscritta in una sfera. Si sa che $AD = 2BC$, e le rette $AB$ e $CD$, prolungate, si incontrano in un punto $E$ che giace dalla parte di $BC$. Determinare il rapporto tra il volume della piramide di base triangolare $AED$ e vertice $V$ e la piramide originale.

Siano $P = x + 7y$, $Q = 2x + 5y$, $R = 4x + 2y$, con $x, y > 0$. Quindi:

(B) $R < Q < P$
(C) $Q < P < R$

(A) 9

(B) $1 < b < a$

Sia $ABC$ un triangolo con incerchio $\gamma$, tangente al lato $AB$ nel punto $T$. Sia $D$ il punto diametralmente opposto a $T$ su $\gamma$, e $S$ il punto in cui la retta $CD$ interseca $AB$. Mostrare che $AT = SB$.

Sia $ABC$ un triangolo con incerchio $\gamma$, tangente al lato $AB$ nel punto $T$. Sia $D$ il punto diametralmente opposto a $T$ su $\gamma$, e $S$ il punto in cui la retta $CD$ interseca $AB$. Mostrare che $AT = SB$.

Dato che $x=\frac{y}{2}$ e $y=\frac{z}{2}$, a cosa è uguale $x+y+z$?

(A) $5x$

Sia $Q(X) = p X^{2} + q X + r$ un polinomio di secondo grado a coefficienti reali (con $p \neq 0$). Se $Q(1000) = 1000$ e $Q(1001) = 1001$, allora $Q(1002)$ non può essere uguale a: (A) 1000 (B) 1001 (C) 1002 (D) 1003 (E) 1004.

Siano $a$ e $b$ due numeri reali tali che $0 < a < 1$ e $0 < b < 1$. Quale delle seguenti relazioni è necessariamente soddisfatta?

(B) $\frac{a}{b} < 1$

Sia $f(n)$ la somma delle cifre di $n$ in base 10. Trova il più piccolo numero intero $N$ tale che $f(f(N)) \geq 10$.
\text{(i) Trovare tutti i numeri naturali }(a, b)\text{ tali che }b^{2} - 2^{a} = 1.\\\text{(ii) Trovare tutti i numeri naturali }(a, b)\text{ tali che }2^{a} - b^{2} = 1.
Sia $a_{0}, a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots$ una successione con $a_{0} = 2$ e $a_{n+1} = 5 + a_{n}^{2}$ per ogni $n \geq 0$. Provare che $a_{n}$ non è mai un numero primo diverso da 2.

\text{a) Dimostrare che se due altezze di un triangolo hanno la stessa lunghezza, allora il triangolo è isoscele.}\\\text{b) Dimostrare che se due mediane di un triangolo hanno la stessa lunghezza, allora il triangolo è isoscele.}\\\text{c) Dato un triangolo }ABC\text{, si prendano su }AB\text{ e }AC\text{ due punti }M\text{ e }N\text{ tali che }\frac{AM}{AB} = \frac{AN}{AC}\text{ e }BN = CM\text{; dimostrare che }ABC\text{ è isoscele}

Siano dati tre interi positivi $p, q, r$. Siano definiti $m = pq$, $n = pr$, $o = qr$. Quale delle seguenti affermazioni è corretta?

(A) Se $m, n, o$ sono quadrati perfetti, allora $p, q, r$ sono quadrati perfetti
(B) Se $m, n, o$ sono divisibili per 2, allora $p, q, r$ sono divisibili per 2

(D) Se $m, n, o$ sono divisibili per 10, allora $p, q, r$ sono divisibili per 10
(E) Nessuna delle precedenti affermazioni è corretta.

Sia $\mathcal{R}$ la regione finita del piano compresa tra l'asse $x$ e il grafico della curva $y = \frac{10 - 2x^2}{5}$. Se si scelgono tre punti in $\mathcal{R}$, quale delle seguenti affermazioni è sempre verificata?

(A) almeno due dei punti hanno una distanza reciproca $\geq \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$
(B) almeno due dei punti hanno una distanza reciproca $\leq 3$
(C) la somma delle distanze reciproche è $\leq \frac{9}{2} \sqrt{5}$
(D) la somma dei quadrati delle distanze reciproche è $\leq 38$

Quanti sono i numeri $10a + b$ con $1 \leq a \leq 9$ e $0 \leq b \leq 9$ tali che $(10a + b)^2 = 1100a + 10b + c$, con $c = b - 1$?

Un edificio quadrato è composto da $n^2$ stanze uguali disposte in una griglia $n 	imes n$, con $n > 1$. Ogni stanza condivide un muro con le sue vicine e ciascuna coppia di stanze adiacenti è connessa da una porta. Un ispettore deve effettuare un giro in cui si muove da stanza a stanza, spendendo esattamente un minuto in ogni stanza prima di spostarsi. È permesso visitare le stanze più volte, ma alla fine del giro ogni stanza deve essere stata visitata esattamente $k$ volte. Determinare per quali valori interi positivi $n$ e $k$ è possibile completare un tale giro.

Un edificio quadrato è composto da $n^2$ stanze uguali disposte in una griglia $n 	imes n$, con $n > 1$. Ogni stanza condivide un muro con le sue stanze adiacenti (tranne quelle ai bordi). Il guardiano inizia in una stanza, trascorre 1 minuto lì, quindi si sposta in una stanza adiacente, spendendo un minuto per stanza visitata. Il movimento può ripassare per stanze già visitate, ma alla fine del giro ogni stanza deve essere stata visitata per un totale di $k$ minuti. Determinare per quali interi positivi $n$ e $k$ tale giro è realizzabile.

Quanti sono i polinomi $p(x)$ a coefficienti reali, con $\deg(p) \in [1, 2020]$, per cui esiste un numero reale $\beta$ tale che $p(x)^2 - \beta p(x) = p(x^2)$ per ogni $x \in \mathbb{R}$?

Sia $T$ l'insieme degli interi $\geq 2$. Una funzione $g: T \rightarrow T$ si dice primordiale se soddisfa:

Sia $ABCD$ un rettangolo e siano $M$ e $N$ punti sui lati $AB$ e $BC$, rispettivamente. Supponiamo che $MC = CD$, $MD = MN$ e che $C, D, M, N$ siano conciclici. Determinare il rapporto $AB / BC$.

Sia $N$ il numero di sestuple ordinate di interi $(x, y, z, w, u, v)$ tali che $x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}+w^{3}+u^{3}+v^{3}=168$ e $-202120212021^{9}<xyzwuv<202120212021^{9}$, dove $xyzwuv$ è il prodotto dei sei interi. Quale dei seguenti è il resto di $N$ nella divisione per 6?

\text{Date due frazioni } \frac{p}{q} \text{ e } \frac{r}{s}, \text{ definiamo l'operazione } \oplus \text{ come } \frac{p}{q} \oplus \frac{r}{s} = \frac{p + r}{q + s}, \text{ dove } \frac{p}{q}, \frac{r}{s} \text{ sono irriducibili e il risultato è anch'esso ridotto ai minimi termini.}\\\text{Dato } n \geq 3, \text{ inizialmente sulla lavagna sono scritte le frazioni } \frac{1}{1}, \frac{1}{2}, \ldots, \frac{1}{n}. \text{ Ad ogni passo cancelliamo due frazioni e sostituiamo con } \frac{p + r}{q + s}. \text{ Determinare, in funzione di } n, \text{ il valore massimo e minimo che può assumere l'ultima frazione rimasta.}

Siano $a, b, c$ interi, ciascuno compreso fra $1$ e $2021$ (estremi inclusi), che soddisfano l'equazione $$ \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} = \sqrt{a + c \sqrt{b}}. $$ Determinare il numero di valori distinti che $c$ può assumere.

Sia $\{a_{n}\}$ una successione definita da un insieme iniziale di $p$ interi positivi distinti che si ripetono ciclicamente, con $a_{n+p} = a_n$ per ogni $n$. Non si conosce il valore degli elementi, ma si può scegliere in modo dinamico e adattivo una sequenza di $n$ query per determinare $p$.

\text{Un numero $a b c$ di tre cifre distinte e non nulle si dice petaloso se esiste un intero $n \geq 1$ per cui il numero $c b a$ seguito da $n$ zeri è divisibile per $a b c$. Il valore minimo di $n$ per cui tale divisibilità è verificata è chiamato fiore di $a b c$.}\\\text{Esempio. Il numero 132 è petaloso perché $23100 / 132 = 175$ è intero, ma $2310 / 132 = 17,5$ non lo è; quindi il fiore di 132 è 2.}\\\text{a. Sia $Q$ l'insieme dei punti $(x, y)$ con $x, y > 0$. Ogni punto di $Q$ è colorato in uno dei due colori: rosso o blu. Let $n \geq 1$ be a positive integer. For any rearrangement $(b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n})$ of the numbers $(1,2, \ldots, n)$, define the cumulative sums $S_k = b_1 + b_2 + \cdots + b_k$ for $k = 1, 2, \ldots, n$. A rearrangement is called quadratique if at least one $S_k$ is a perfect square. Determine the largest integer $n < 2003$ such that all such rearrangements are quadratique.

Let $S = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2003\}$ and let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2003}$ be a permutation of $S$. Define $b_k = k a_k$ for each $k = 1, 2, \ldots, 2003$, and let $B = \max\{b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{2003}\}$.

a) If $a_k = 2004 - k$ for all $k$, determine the value of $B$.

b) Show that $B \geq 1002^{2}$.
Let $k$ be a positive integer with $k = n + 1$ such that $2003(k - 1) + 1$ is a perfect square. Prove that $k$ is the sum of 2003 positive perfect squares.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 3 x y z$. Prove that
$$
\frac{x}{y^{2} z^{2}} + \frac{y}{z^{2} x^{2}} + \frac{z}{x^{2} y^{2}} \geq \frac{9}{x + y + z}
$$

Let triangle $ABC$ be such that $AB = BC$. Let $F$ be the point where the internal bisector from $A$ intersects side $BC$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $B$ to side $AC$. If $AF = 2 BD$, determine the measure of $\angle ABC$.

Fie $S(n)$ suma cifrelor numărului natural $n$ în baza 10. Demonstrați că, pentru orice $k \in \mathbb{N}$, există un număr $m \in \mathbb{N}$ astfel încât ecuația $x + S(x) = m$ admite cel puțin $k$ soluții în $\mathbb{N}$.

Fie un romb $ABCD$ cu latura $1$. Pe laturile $BC$ și $CD$ se consideră punctele $M$ și $N$, astfel încât $MC + CN + NM = 2$ și $\angle MAN = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAD$. Determinați măsurile unghiurilor rombului.

Fie un poligon convex cu $n$ vârfuri, $n \geq 4$. Fiecare triunghi dintr-o descompunere a poligonului în triunghiuri având vârfuri numai printre cele ale poligonului și fără intersecții de puncte interioare este colorat astfel: negru dacă are două laturi comune cu poligonul, roșu dacă are exact o latură comună și alb dacă nu are nicio latură comună. Demonstrați că există exact 2 triunghiuri negre în plus față de cele albe.
\text{Prove that for all real } x, y \quad \frac{x+y}{x^{2}-x y+y^{2}} \leq \frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}

Consider a $p \times q$ grid where all cells are initially labeled with "-". Two operations are allowed:
(i) flip all entries in a row (i.e., change all "-" to "+" and vice versa);
(ii) flip all entries in a column (i.e., change all "-" to "+" and vice versa).

a. Show that when $p = q = 100$, it is impossible to achieve 2004 "+" signs.

b. Given $p = 100$, determine the smallest $q > 100$ such that 2004 "+" signs are achievable.

Let $k_{1}$ and $k_{2}$ be intersecting circles at points $A$ and $B$. A circle centered at $A$, denoted $k_{3}$, intersects $k_{1}$ at $M$ and $P$ and $k_{2}$ at $N$ and $Q$, with $N$ and $Q$ lying on opposite sides of $MP$, and it is given that $AB > AM$. Prove that $\angle MBQ = \angle NBP$.
Let $x, y, z, w, v$ be real numbers such that $x+y+z+w+v=0$. Let $P=xy+yz+zw+wv+vx$ and $Q=xz+zv+v y + yw + w x$. Show that $$2005 P + Q \leq 0 \text{ or } P + 2005 Q \leq 0$$

Find all positive integers $x, y$ satisfying the equation
$$
9x^{2}+9y^{2}+6xy+13=2005
$$

Find all integer solutions $(a, b)$ to the equation
$$
8 a^{3}+8 a^{2} b+8 a b^{2}+8 b^{3}=15\left(a^{2}+b^{2}+a b+1\right)
$$.

Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezoid with $AB = BC = AD$, $AB \parallel DC$, and $AB > DC$. Let $E$ be the intersection point of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$, and let $N$ be the reflection of $B$ over the line $AC$. Show that the points $A$, $N$, $D$, and $E$ lie on a circle.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$ and $\angle B > \frac{1}{2} \angle A$. Points $D$ and $Z$ lie on the extension of the altitude $AM$ such that $\angle CBD = \angle A$ and $\angle ZBA = 90^\circ$. If $E$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $M$ to the altitude $BF$, and $K$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $Z$ to $AE$, show that $\angle KDZ = \angle KBD = \angle KZB$.
In parallelogram $ABCD$, let $P$ lie on $CD$ and $Q$ lie on $AB$. Define $M = AP \cap DQ$, $N = BP \cap CQ$, and set $K = MN \cap AD$ and $L = MN \cap BC$. Prove that $DK = BL$.

\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ and } m_a, m_b, m_c \text{ be respectively the lengths of the sides and the medians of an acute-angled triangle } ABC. \text{ Prove that} \quad \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{m_a^2}{b^2 + c^2 - a^2} \geq \frac{9}{4}

Let $a, b, c$ be non-negative numbers such that $a + 2b + 3c = \frac{11}{12}$. Prove that
$$
63ab + 10a + 2bc + 3b + 4c + 72abc \leq \frac{17}{18}
$$
When does equality hold?

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ and $AB > CD$. Suppose that $\angle A + \angle B = 90^\circ$. Prove that the segment connecting the midpoints of $AB$ and $CD$ has length $\frac{1}{2}(AB - CD)$.
\text{Show that } \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a^{2}-b c}{2 a^{2}+b c} \leq 0 \text{ for all } a, b, c > 0.
\begin{gathered}x \sqrt{y z(x + m y)(x + n z)} + y \sqrt{x z(y + m x)(y + n z)} + z \sqrt{x y(z + m x)(z + n y)} \\ \leq \frac{3(m+n)}{8}(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)\end{gathered}

In triangle $ABC$, with $\angle BAC = 70^\circ$ and $\angle ABC = 80^\circ$, let $M$ lie inside such that $\angle ACM = 10^\circ$ and $\angle CBM = 20^\circ$. Prove that the length of $AB$ equals the length of $MC$.

Let the incircle of triangle $\triangle ABC$ be tangent to side $BC$ at $M$, side $CA$ at $N$, and side $AB$ at $P$. Suppose a point $D$ lies on segment $[NP]$ such that $\frac{DP}{DN} = \frac{BD}{CD}$. Prove that the line $DM$ is perpendicular to the segment $PN$.
Show that there are no positive integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $x^{2006} - 4 y^{2006} - 2006 = 4 y^{2007} + 2007 y$.
Let $n > 1$ be an integer and $p$ a prime with $n \mid (p-1)$ and $p \mid (n^{6} - 1)$. Show that one of $p+n$ or $p-n$ must be a perfect square.

Let $p$, $q$ be two co-prime positive integers. A number is said to be expressible if it can be represented as $p x + q y$ for non-negative integers $x$, $y$. Define the function $g: \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ as $g(n) = n - \mathrm{rem}(n, p) - \mathrm{rem}(n, q)$. Prove that an integer $n$ is expressible if and only if the sequence $n, g(n), g(g(n)), \ldots$ never becomes negative.

Given $0 < x, y, z, w < 1$, prove that
$$
1 + x y + y z + z w + w x + x z + y w > x + y + z + w
$$

Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x y z = 1$. Prove the inequality
$$
\left(x y + y z + \frac{1}{z x}\right)\left(y z + z x + \frac{1}{x y}\right)\left(z x + x y + \frac{1}{y z}\right) \geq (1 + 2 x)(1 + 2 y)(1 + 2 z)
$$

Let $n \geq 4$ be an integer and consider a list of real numbers $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, \ldots, x_{n}$. A filtering process removes all elements whose indices are not of the form $4k+3$, resulting in the subsequence $x_{3}, x_{7}, x_{11}, \ldots$. Apply this process 5 times on the list $1,2,3,\ldots,1024$. Prove that a single number remains at the end and determine its value.

On a $5 \times 5$ grid, $n$ tokens are placed on separate unit squares. A child is tasked to convert as many tokens as possible to black using the following rule: remove a white token, color it black, and place it on an unoccupied square such that no adjacent square (sharing a side) has a white token. If the child can turn all tokens black, the initial configuration is called valid.
a) Show that a valid configuration exists when $n=20$.
b) Show that no valid configuration exists when $n=21$.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AC = BC$. A point $D$ is placed on $AB$, and a semicircle with diameter $BD$ is drawn with center $O$, which is tangent to $AC$ at point $P$ and intersects $BC$ at point $Q$. The line segment $OP$ intersects the chord $DQ$ at point $E$ such that $\frac{PE}{DE} = \frac{3}{5}$. Determine the value of $\frac{AB}{BC}$.

Let $a$ and $b$ be the side lengths of a parallelogram, with diagonals $x$ and $y$. If the product of the side lengths is half the product of the diagonals, i.e., $a b = \frac{x y}{2}$, prove that
$$
a = \frac{x}{\sqrt{2}},\ b = \frac{y}{\sqrt{2}} \quad \text{or} \quad a = \frac{y}{\sqrt{2}},\ b = \frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}
$$

Let $n \geq 2$ be a fixed positive integer. An integer is defined to be $n$-free if it is not divisible by the $n$-th power of any prime. Let $M$ be an infinite set of rational numbers with the property that the product of any $n$ elements from $M$ is an $n$-free integer. Show that all elements of $M$ must be integers.

Let $d(a)$ represent the sum of the digits of a positive integer $a$. Consider a sequence of positive integers $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{n}, \ldots$ where $x_{n+1} = x_{n} + d(x_{n})$ for all positive integers $n$. Determine the maximum possible $n$ such that $x_{n} = 2008$.
Find the smallest prime $ p > 3 $ such that for all $ n \in \mathbb{N} $, the congruence $ 2^{n} + 3^{n} \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p} $ holds.
\prod_{\text{cyc}}\left(x^{2}+y+1\right)\left(x^{2}+z+1\right) \geq (x+y+z)^{6}

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with diagonals intersecting at $O$, and suppose that $AC > BD$. A circle centered at $O$ with radius $OA$ intersects the extensions of $AD$ and $AB$ at $G$ and $L$, respectively. If $Z$ is the intersection of $GL$ and $BD$, show that $\angle ZCA = 90^\circ$.

Let $ABCD$ be a right trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ and $\angle ABC = 75^\circ$. Suppose the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$ intersects $BC$ at point $H$. If $BH = DC$ and $AD + AH = 8$, determine the area of trapezoid $ABCD$.

Prove there exist infinitely many positive integers $ c $ such that the equations
$$
\left(a^{2}-c\right)\left(b^{2}-c\right)=k^{2}-c
$$
and
$$
\left(a^{2}+c\right)\left(b^{2}-c\right)=k^{2}-c
$$
have solutions in positive integers $ a, b, k $.

Find all four-digit numbers $\overline{p q r s}$ satisfying
$$
p(p+q+r+s)\left(p^{2}+q^{2}+r^{2}+s^{2}\right)\left(p^{6}+2 q^{6}+3 r^{6}+4 s^{6}\right)=\overline{p q r s}
$$
Find all real number pairs $(a, b)$ satisfying $|a| + |b| = 1340$ and $a^{3} + b^{3} + 2010ab = 670^{3}$.
Let $x, y, z$ be positive real numbers such that $xyz(x+y+z) = 3$. Prove the inequality $$(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) \geq 8$$ and find the conditions for equality.
Let $a, b, c$ be positive real numbers such that $a \leq 2$, $b \leq 3$, and $a + b + c = 11$. Show that $\sqrt{a b c} \leq 6$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be right-angled at $C$. Let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C$ to $AB$. A circle $\omega$ is tangent to segment $FB$ at $P$, to the segment $CF$ at $Q$, and to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $R$. Prove that points $A$, $Q$, and $R$ lie on a straight line and that $AP = AC$.
\frac{a+2b}{c+2a+3b} + \frac{b+2c}{a+2b+3c} + \frac{c+2a}{b+2c+3a} \leq \frac{3}{2}
\text{Let } a, b > 0. \text{ Show that} \quad \sqrt{\frac{a^{2} + ab + b^{2}}{3}} + \sqrt{ab} \leq a + b.
Let $a, b$ be positive real numbers satisfying $a^{3}+b^{3} \leq a^{2}+b^{2}$. Determine the maximum value of $ab$.
Find positive integers $x, y$ such that $x^{2} y^{2} + 208 = 4\left(\mathrm{lcm}[x, y] + \gcd(x, y)\right)^{2}$.
Let $x_{i} > 1$, for all $i \in \{1,2,3, \ldots, 2011\}$. Prove the inequality $$\sum_{i=1}^{2011} \frac{x_{i}^{2}}{x_{i+1}-1} \geq 4 \cdot 2011$$ where $x_{2012} = x_{1}$. When does equality hold?
\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be positive real numbers with } abc = 1. \text{ Prove the inequality: } \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{2 a^{2} + \frac{1}{a}}{b + \frac{1}{a} + 1} \geq 3
Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$ be real numbers such that $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \min \left(a_{i}, a_{i+1}\right) = \min \left(a_{1}, a_{n}\right)$. Show that $\sum_{i=2}^{n-1} a_{i} \geq 0$.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $AB = AC$. Extend $CA$ beyond $A$ to a point $D$ such that $AD < AC$. Let the perpendicular bisector of segment $[BD]$ intersect the internal and external bisectors of $\angle BAC$ at points $E$ and $Z$, respectively. Prove that the four points $A, E, D, Z$ lie on a circle.

Let $D$ be a point on side $[BC]$ of triangle $ABC$. Let $O_{1}$ and $O_{2}$ be the circumcenters of triangles $ADC$ and $BAD$, respectively. If $O_{1}O_{2}$ is parallel to $AB$, and the orthocenter $H$ of triangle $ADC$ satisfies $AH = O_{1}O_{2}$, determine the angles of triangle $ABC$ given that $2m(\angle C) = 3m(\angle B)$.

Consider square $ABCD$ with an equilateral triangle $\triangle ABE$ constructed on side $AB$. A point $M$ lies inside $\triangle ABE$ satisfying $MB = \sqrt{2}$, $MC = \sqrt{6}$, $MD = \sqrt{5}$, and $ME = \sqrt{3}$. Determine the area of square $ABCD$.
Find all positive integer solutions to the equation $2011^{y} + 1005^{x} = 1006^{z}$.
Determine all positive integers $n$ for which there exist positive integers $x$ and $y$ satisfying $y^{2} + x y + 3 x = n(x^{2} + x y + 3 y)$.
Determine all pairs of prime positive integers $p, q$ satisfying the equation $2 p^{3} - q^{2} = 2(p + q)^{2}$.

Suppose $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = AC$. A circle centered at $K$ with radius $KC$ is tangent to $AC$ at point $C$ and intersects the segment $BC$ at a point $H$ lying between $B$ and $C$. Show that the line $HK$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

Let $x = a - 2b + c$, $y = b - 2c + a$, $z = c - 2a + b$, and define $A = 2x^4 + 2y^4 + 2z^4$, $B = d(d+1)(d+2)(d+3) + 1$. Show that $(\sqrt{A} + 1)^2 + B$ is not a perfect square for any integers $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$.

Let $ABCD$ be a square of side length $1$, with points $P, Q, R, S$ on sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ respectively such that $PR \cdot QS = \frac{5}{4}$. Is it possible to divide the set $\{PQ, QR, RS, SP\}$ into two pairs whose sums are both positive integers?
\text{Find all integer solutions } (m, n, p) \text{ such that } n^{2p} - n^2 - p = m^2 + 1 \text{ with } p \text{ being a prime number}.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $xyz = 1$. Show that
$$
\frac{1}{x^{3}+y z}+\frac{1}{y^{3}+z x}+\frac{1}{z^{3}+x y} \leq \frac{(x y+y z+z x)^{2}}{6}
$$

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x + y + z = x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}$. Show that $$\frac{x^{2}}{x^{2} + x y} + \frac{y^{2}}{y^{2} + y z} + \frac{z^{2}}{z^{2} + z x} \geq \frac{x + y + z}{2}$$

Find all natural numbers $a, b, c$ such that
$$
\left(1+\frac{a}{b+c}\right)^{2}+\left(1+\frac{b}{c+a}\right)^{2}+\left(1+\frac{c}{a+b}\right)^{2}=\frac{27}{4}
$$

Determine the maximum positive integer $n$ such that the inequality
$$
\frac{x+y+z}{x y z+1}+\sqrt[n]{x y z} \leq \frac{5}{2}
$$
holds for all $x, y, z \in [0,1]$. Here $\sqrt[1]{x y z} = x y z$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$, with $O$ and $H$ as its circumcenter and orthocenter, respectively. Let $A'$ be the point on $\Gamma$ such that $AA'$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Given that $A'H = AH$, determine $\angle BAC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with $AB = 2013$ and $AD = 1000$. A billiard ball is fired from point $A$ along the angle bisector of $\angle BAD$. Given that reflections obey the law of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), does the ball ever reach corner $B$?

Suppose the weights of all $\binom{n}{2}$ pairs of $n$ distinct fruits are recorded in random order. Is it possible to uniquely identify the weights of the fruits if

a. $n=4$

b. $n=5$

c. $n=6$?
Determine all integer solutions $(a, b, c)$ such that $20^{a} + 13^{b} = 2013^{c}$.
\text{Determine all positive integer solutions } (x, y, z) \text{ to the equation} \quad \frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{y}{x z} + \frac{1}{z^{2}} = \frac{1}{2013}

Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x y z = \frac{1}{8}$. Prove the inequality
$$
x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} + x^{2} y^{2} + y^{2} z^{2} + z^{2} x^{2} \geq \frac{15}{16}
$$
When does equality hold?
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be non-negative real numbers with $a + b + c = a b c$. Show that $$ 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2) \geq 3(a + b + c) $$ and find the conditions for equality.

\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that} \quad \left(\left(3 x^{2}+1\right)^{2}+2\left(1+\frac{3}{y}\right)^{2}\right)\left(\left(3 y^{2}+1\right)^{2}+2\left(1+\frac{3}{z}\right)^{2}\right)\left(\left(3 z^{2}+1\right)^{2}+2\left(1+\frac{3}{x}\right)^{2}\right) \geq 48^{3} \quad \text{When does equality hold?}

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive real numbers such that $x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 48$. Prove $$ x^{2} \sqrt{2 y^{3} + 16} + y^{2} \sqrt{2 z^{3} + 16} + z^{2} \sqrt{2 x^{3} + 16} \leq 24^{2} $$ When does equality hold?

In a network of $n$ nodes, every pair of nodes is connected by a two-way edge. There are $r > 2014$ directed paths of length at most 2 between distinct nodes. Determine the smallest $n$ and the corresponding smallest $r$.
In triangle $ABC$, it is given that $\angle B = \angle C = 40^\circ$. If $D$ lies on $AC$ such that $\angle ABD = \angle DBC$, prove that $BD + DA = BC$.
Assign a unique digit from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ to each letter of the word OHRID such that the following holds: $$\frac{(O+H+R+I+D)^2}{(O-H-R+I+D)} = O^{H^{R^{I_{D}}}}.$$

Determine all integer pairs $(a, b)$ satisfying
$$
a^{2}=b^{2}\left(a + b^{4} + 2b^{2}\right)
$$
\text{Determine all nonnegative integers } a, b, c \text{ for which } 2013^{a} + 2014^{b} = 2015^{c}

Vukasin, Dimitrije, Dusan, Stefan, and Filip asked their professor to guess three consecutive positive integers, given the following true statements:

Vukasin: "The digit sum of one is prime. The digit sum of another is an even perfect number. The digit sum of the last is equal to the number of its positive divisors."

Dimitrije: "Each number contains at most two 1s in its decimal form."

Dusan: "Adding 11 to one of them gives a perfect square."

Stefan: "Each of the three has exactly one prime factor less than 10."

Filip: "All three numbers are square-free."

The professor correctly identified the numbers. What are they?

\text{Let } a, b, c \text{ be real numbers, satisfying the relations} \quad \left\{\begin{array}{l} a \geq 20 \\ b \geq 40 \\ c \geq 1675 \\ a+b+c=2015 \end{array}\right. \text{Find the greatest value of the product } Q = a \cdot b \cdot c.
\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \frac{x}{y} + \sqrt{\frac{y}{z}} + \sqrt[3]{\frac{z}{x}} > 2
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=3$. Prove that $$\frac{a^{2}+bc}{a^{2}+bc+1} + \frac{b^{2}+ca}{b^{2}+ca+1} + \frac{c^{2}+ab}{c^{2}+ab+1} \leq 2$$

An $n \times n$ grid ($n \geq 3$) is filled with integers from $0$ to $n$ (inclusive), with one integer per cell, such that the sum of numbers in every $2 \times 2$ subgrid is unique. Determine all values of $n$ for which such a configuration is possible.

Let $n$ be a positive integer with $n \geq 1$. A square grid of side length $n$ is formed by dividing the square into unit squares. Determine how many parallelograms can be formed using the grid vertices, such that each side of the parallelogram has length at most $2$, and the area of the parallelogram is exactly $2$.

Let a $5 \times 5$ grid represent a chessboard and suppose we have $\{L\}$-shaped tiles, each consisting of three connected unit squares in the form of a corner. Two players, $A$ and $B$, take turns marking squares, starting with $A$, until exactly $k$ squares are marked. The marking is done one square per turn.

Player $A$ wins if the unmarked squares can be completely tiled with $\{L\}$-shaped tiles, leaving at most 2 unmarked squares uncovered, and no marked square is used in the tiling. If this is not possible, player $\boldsymbol{B}$ wins. Determine the smallest $\boldsymbol{k}$ for which $\boldsymbol{B}$ can guarantee a win.
\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers such that } xyz = 8. \text{ Prove that } \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{xy+4}{x+2} \geq 6

Let $a, b, c$ be non-negative real numbers such that $a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=a+b+c$. Prove that:
$$
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a+1}{\sqrt{a^{5}+a+1}} \geq 3
$$
Determine when equality occurs.

Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be positive real numbers such that $a + b + c = \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}$.

a) Prove the inequality
$$
a + b + c \geq \sqrt{\frac{ab + 1}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{bc + 1}{2}} + \sqrt{\frac{ca + 1}{2}}
$$

b) When does the equality hold?
For a convex $n$-gon in the plane, where $n \geq 3$, find the smallest number $m$ such that every triangulation of the polygon uses at least $m$ triangles.

Let $(c)$ be a circle with center $O$, and let $[AB]$ be a chord of $(c)$. A point $K$ lies on the segment $(AB)$ with $AK < BK$. There are two circles passing through $K$ and internally tangent to $(c)$ at $A$ and $B$, respectively; they intersect again at $L$. Let $P$ be one of the points where the line $KL$ intersects $(c)$, and let $M$ be the intersection of $AB$ and $LO$. Prove that the line $MP$ is tangent to the circle $(c)$.
Find all four-digit numbers $\overline{w x y z}$ where $$(w+x)(w+y)(w+z)(x+y)(x+z)(y+z)=\overline{w x y z}$$

Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be positive numbers. Prove that
$$
\frac{a^2}{\sqrt{\sqrt[4]{b^2}+\sqrt[4]{c^2}}}+\frac{b^2}{\sqrt{\sqrt[4]{c^2}+\sqrt[4]{a^2}}}+\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{\sqrt[4]{a^2}+\sqrt[4]{b^2}}} \geq \frac{\sqrt[4]{(a + b + c)^7}}{\sqrt{2 \sqrt{27}}}
$$
Determine the largest integer $k$ for which the inequality $$ m^{3}+n^{3} \geq (m+n)^{2}+k $$ holds for all positive integers $m, n$ satisfying $m^{3}+n^{3} > (m+n)^{2}$.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive numbers such that $xy + yz + zx = 3$. Prove that
$$
\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{3}+5}} + \frac{y}{\sqrt{y^{3}+5}} + \frac{z}{\sqrt{z^{3}+5}} \leq \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}
$$

Let $A$ be a set of positive integers satisfying the following:
(i) Every element of $A$ is at most $2018$.
(ii) Any three elements in $A$ contain two such that their absolute difference is at least the sum of their square roots.
What is the largest possible size of $A$?

Let $H$ be the orthocentre of an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AC < BC$, inscribed in a circle $\Gamma$. Let $D$ be the second intersection point of $\Gamma$ with a circle centred at $C$ and radius $CB$, such that $D$ lies on the arc $AB$ not containing $C$. Let $K$ be the intersection of $CD$ with a circle centred at $C$ and radius $CA$. Draw a line through $K$ parallel to $BD$, intersecting $AB$ at $L$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$, and $N$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ onto $CL$. Prove that $MN$ bisects the segment $CH$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with side-lengths $a$, $b$, $c$, and circumradius $R$. Let $I$ denote its incenter. Suppose $A_{1}$, $A_{2}$, and $A_{3}$ are the areas of triangles $ABI$, $BCI$, and $CAI$, respectively. Prove that
$$
\frac{R^4}{A_{1}^{2}} + \frac{R^4}{A_{2}^{2}} + \frac{R^4}{A_{3}^{2}} \geq 16
$$

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle with $AB = b$ and $BC = 2a$, where $b > 2a$. Let $E$ be the midpoint of side $AD$. On a line through $E$ parallel to $AB$, a point $G$ is selected so that the area of triangle $GCE$ is given by
$$
[\triangle GCE] = \frac{1}{2}\left(ab + \frac{a^3}{b}\right)
$$
Let $H$ be the perpendicular projection of $E$ onto $GD$, and choose a point $I$ on the diagonal $AC$ such that $\triangle ACE \sim \triangle AEI$. The intersection of lines $BH$ and $IE$ is denoted $K$, and the intersection of $CA$ and $EH$ is denoted $J$. Prove that $KJ$ is perpendicular to $AB$.

Let $XY$ be a chord of a circle $\Omega$ with center $O$, where $XY$ is not a diameter. Let $P, Q$ be two points on segment $XY$ such that $Q$ lies between $P$ and $X$. Let $\ell$ be the perpendicular line from $P$ to the diameter through $Q$. Let $M$ be the intersection of $\ell$ with $\Omega$ closer to $P$. Prove that
$$
MP \cdot XY \geq 2 \cdot QX \cdot PY
$$

Determine all integer solutions $(x, y)$ such that
$$
(x^{5} - y^{5}) = 16 x y
$$
Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers such that $x^{3} + y^{3} - 6xy = -11$. Show that $-\frac{7}{3} < x + y < -2$.

Let $x, y, z, w$ be positive real numbers such that $x y z w = 1$. Prove the inequality
$$
\frac{1}{x^{3}+y+z+w}+\frac{1}{x+y^{3}+z+w}+\frac{1}{x+y+z^{3}+w}+\frac{1}{x+y+z+w^{3}} \leqslant \frac{x+y+z+w}{4}
$$
\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers. Prove that } \left(x^{2}+x z+z^{2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{x+y+z}+\frac{1}{x+z}\right)+y^{2}\left(\frac{1}{y+z}+\frac{1}{x+y}\right) > x+y+z
Find all prime numbers $p$ and nonnegative integers $a > b$ such that $a^{4} - b^{4} = p(a^{3} - b^{3})$.

Find all integers $a, b$ such that
$$
 a^{3}(b+1)+b^{3}(a+1)=19
$$

Find all positive integers $a, b, c$ such that
$$
(3^{2} \cdot 5)^{a} - (2 \cdot 3)^{b} = 2019^{c}
$$
Find all triples $(x, y, z)$ of nonnegative integers that satisfy $$x! + 5^{y} = 7^{z}$$
Determine all square numbers $n$ for which every positive divisor $a$ of $n$ satisfying $a \geqslant 15$ leads to $a + 15$ being a power of a prime.

Determine all positive real numbers $(x, y, z)$ such that the expression
$$
N=\frac{(x+y)(y+z)(x+y+z)}{x y z}
$$
attains its minimum value.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, and let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Let $Z$ be a point on the line $AB$ such that $AB = BZ$, and $Z \neq A$. Let $(c)$ be the circumcircle of triangle $\triangle AEZ$. Let $D$ be the second intersection of line $ZC$ with $(c)$, and let $F$ be the point diametrically opposite $D$ on $(c)$. Let $P$ be the intersection of lines $FE$ and $CZ$. If the tangent to $(c)$ at $Z$ intersects $PA$ at $T$, prove that $T, E, B, Z$ lie on a circle.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$, and let $E$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Let $Z$ be a point on the line $AB$ such that $AB = BZ$, and $Z \neq A$. Let $(c)$ be the circumcircle of triangle $\triangle AEZ$. Let $D$ be the second intersection of line $ZC$ with $(c)$, and let $F$ be the point diametrically opposite $D$ on $(c)$. Let $P$ be the intersection of lines $FE$ and $CZ$. If the tangent to $(c)$ at $Z$ intersects $PA$ at $T$, prove that $T, E, B, Z$ lie on a circle.

Alice and Bob play a game with the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, where $n \geqslant 2$. Bob begins, and each player in turn picks a number not yet selected, provided it is adjacent (i.e., differs by 1) to a previously chosen number. The game concludes when all numbers are picked. Alice wins if her total is a composite number; otherwise, Bob wins. Determine which player has a winning strategy.

Let triangle $ABC$ be acute, with orthocenter $H$, and let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$ such that $AH = HD$. Let $\ell$ be a line through $H$ tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BHC$. Let $S$ and $T$ be the points where $\ell$ meets $AB$ and $AC$, and let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $BH$ and $CH$, respectively. Prove that the lines $SM$ and $TN$ are parallel.

Determine all positive integer quadruples $(x, y, m, n)$, with $x$ and $y$ prime and $m>1$, satisfying the equation
$$
 x^{m} = 1 + 5 y^{n}
$$

Show that for all non-negative real numbers $a, b, c$, not all zero, the inequality
$$
\frac{2a^{2}-a+b+c}{a+b^{2}+c^{2}}+\frac{2b^{2}+a-b+c}{a^{2}+b+c^{2}}+\frac{2c^{2}+a+b-c}{a^{2}+b^{2}+c} \geqslant 3
$$
holds. Find all triples $(a, b, c)$ for which equality occurs.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcenter $O$. Let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $OD$. Suppose $O_b$ and $O_c$ are the centers of the circles passing through $A, O, C$ and $A, O, B$, respectively. If $AD = AO$, show that $A$, $O_b$, $M$, and $O_c$ lie on a common circle.

Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the identity
$$
\quad f(x)^2 + 2y f(x) + f(y) = f(y + f(x))
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

Find all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ such that all the following equations hold.
$$
 a^2 - 3b - c = -8
$$
$$
 b^2 - 5c - a = -12
$$
$$
 c^2 - a - b = 6
$$

Find a degree $3$ polynomial $f(x, y, z)$ with real coefficients such that:
• $f(x, y, z) + x$ is divisible by $z + y$
• $f(x, y, z) + y$ is divisible by $x + z$
• $f(x, y, z) + z$ is divisible by $y + x$
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at a point $P$. Given $AC = 2$, $BD = 3$, and $\angle APB = 60^\circ$, find the minimal perimeter $AB + BC + CD + DA$.

Let a $3 \times 3$ grid of unit squares be given, numbered as follows:

| ① | ② | ③ |
|----|----|----|
| ⑧ |    | ④ |
| ⑦ | ⑥ | ⑤ |

Choose points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ from the interiors of squares $1$, $3$, $5$, and $7$, respectively. Define $X$ as the total area of overlap between the quadrilateral $ABCD$ and squares $1$, $3$, $5$, and $7$, and $Y$ as the total area of overlap between $ABCD$ and squares $2$, $4$, $6$, and $8$. Show that $X < Y$.

In triangle $ABC$, a circle $O$ passes through $B$ and $C$ and intersects $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$ (excluding the endpoints), such that $AD + AE = BC$. Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, and suppose the lines $BI$ and $CI$ intersect circle $O$ again at $P$ and $Q$ respectively. Prove that the points $A$, $I$, $P$, and $Q$ are concyclic.

Let $H$ be the orthocenter of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$. Define $P$ as the intersection point of the median $AM$ with the line through $H$ that is perpendicular to $AM$. Show that the product $AM \cdot PM$ is equal to the square of $BM$.

Let $f$ be a function from the positive integers to the positive integers such that for all positive integers $x, y$, the inequality
$$
(x + y)f(x) \leq x^2 + f(xy) + 110
$$
holds. Find the smallest and largest possible value of $f(23) + f(2011)$.

Given a sector $ OAB $ of a circle centered at $ O $, with point $ Q $ lying on chord $ AB $, let $ P $ be the intersection point of the arc $ AB $ with the line $ OQ $. If $ AQ = 5 $, $ BQ = 6 $, and $ OQ = PQ $, find the radius of the circle.

Let $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$ be right isosceles triangles such that $\angle ACB = \angle PQR = 90^\circ$, $AB = 5$, and $PR = 3$. The points $A, P, Q$ lie on a straight line in that order; the same holds for $B, Q, R$ and $R, C, P$. Compute the area of triangle $ABQ$.

Let square $ABCD$ have side length $a$. Points $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ lie on $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$, respectively, such that $PR \parallel BC$ and $SQ \parallel AB$. Let $Z$ be the intersection of $PR$ and $SQ$. If $BP = 7$, $BQ = 6$, and $DZ = 5$, find the value of $a$.

Let cube $ABCD$-$EFGH$ with side length $2012$ be intersected by a plane forming a hexagon $IJKLMN$, with $I$, $J$, $K$, $L$, $M$, $N$ lying on $AE$, $EF$, $FG$, $GC$, $CD$, $DA$, respectively. Given that $AI - GL = 8$, $CM - EJ = 6$, and $FK - DN = 4$, compute the difference between the total area of triangles $IKM$ and $JLN$ and the area of the hexagon $IJKLMN$.

Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f(f(a+b)f(a-b)) = a^2 - b f(b)
$$
for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be given with side lengths $AB = 3$, $BC = 4$, and $CA = 3$. Outside the triangle, squares $PQBA$, $RSCB$, and $TUAC$ are constructed on the sides $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$, respectively. Find the area of the hexagon $PQRSTU$ formed by the outer vertices of these squares.
In quadrilateral $ABCD$, a point $E$ lies on side $DA$ such that $AB \parallel EC$. Given that $AB = 3$, $BC = 3$, $CD = 5$, and $DE = 3$, with $EA = 2$, compute the length of segment $EC$.
How many quadruples $(x, y, z, w)$ of 1-digit positive integers are there which satisfy $x + yzw = xy + zw$?

Let $n$ be a positive integer. A lattice point in $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a point $(a, b, c)$ where $a, b, c$ are integers. A lattice segment is a unit-length segment connecting two adjacent lattice points in the region $0 \le x, y, z \le n$. Each lattice segment must be assigned a direction, either from one endpoint to the other. A lattice square is a square whose four edges are lattice segments. Two lattice squares are considered congruent if one can be rotated and translated to exactly match the other, with the additional condition that the directions of the edges also match. How many ways are there to assign directions to all lattice segments such that all lattice squares are congruent?

Let $b_1, b_2, \dots$ be an infinite sequence of distinct non-zero real numbers such that $\frac{b_{i+1}}{b_i} + \frac{b_{i+1}}{b_i}$ is constant for each $i \ge 1$ and lies in the interval $(0, 2)$. Find the smallest $c$ (in terms of $b_1, b_2, b_3$) such that for all positive integers $x < y$, $$\frac{b_x b_{x+1} + b_{x+1} b_{x+2} + \dots + b_{y-1} b_y}{b_x b_y} \le c$$ is true.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all integers $a, b$,
$$
f(a) + f(b) = f(ab) + f(a + b + ab).
$$

Two circles, $C_2$ and $C_1$, are internally tangent at point $A$, with $O$ as the center of $C_2$. A tangent to $C_1$ at point $P$ passes through $O$. The segment $OP$ intersects $C_2$ at point $Q$, and the tangent to $C_1$ at $A$ intersects $OP$ at point $R$. Given that the radius of $C_2$ is $9$ and $PQ = QR$, find the length $OP$.

Let $S$ be a set of functions $f: [6] \times [6] \to [6]$, where $[6] = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. How many such functions $f$ satisfy the following conditions:

* For every $i \in [6]$, $f(i, i) = i$.
* For all $i, j, k, \ell \in [6]$, $f(f(i, j), f(k, \ell)) = f(i, \ell)$.

Let points $A$, $B$, and $C$ be located on the circle $\Gamma$. Let $P$ denote the intersection of the tangents at $B$ and $C$. It is given that $AB \parallel CP$, $AB = 3$, and $BP = 4$. Determine the length of $BC$.

Let $ABCDE$ be a regular pentagon. If $F$ is the intersection point of $BE$ and $AC$, and a line through $F$ intersects $AB$ at $G$ and $CD$ at $H$ with $BG = 4$ and $CH = 5$, compute the value of $AG$. Use the standard notation for segment lengths.

Let $a, b, c, d$ be integers such that $1 \le a, b, c, d \le 1000$. For all such quadruples, define $S = \max(ab + cd, ac + bd, ad + bc)$ and sum all such $S$ to get $M$. Similarly, define $s = \min(ab + cd, ac + bd, ad + bc)$ and sum all such $s$ to get $m$. Compute the number of positive divisors of $M - m$.

Let $P$ be a point inside triangle $ABC$ with $AB = AC$. Let $D, E, F$ be the projections of $P$ onto $BC, CA, AB$, respectively. If $BD = 9$, $DC = 5$, and the lengths of the perpendiculars from $P$ to $CA$ and $AB$ are $2$ and $5$, respectively, find $AB$.
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $P$ be a point such that $AP \perp AD$ and $BP \perp CD$. If $AB = 7$, $AP = 3$, $BP = 6$, $AD = 5$, and $CD = 10$, compute the area of triangle $ABC$.
Find all positive integer solutions $ (a, b) $ such that $ 3^a - 2^{3b} = 2ab + 1 $.

Let triangle $ABC$ be isosceles with right angle at $A$ and $AB = AC = 7$. Points $D$, $E$, and $F$ lie on $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$ respectively such that $\angle EDF = 90^\circ$, $DE = 5$, and $DF = 3$. Determine the length of segment $BD$.

Let $S$ be a collection of functions mapping $\{1, 2, \dots, 2023\}$ to itself. Suppose $S$ satisfies:
* For any $f \in S$ and all $x, y$ with $1 \le x < y \le 2023$, it holds that $f(x) \ge f(y)$.
* For any $f, g \in S$ and all $x \in \{1, 2, \dots, 2023\}$, $f(g(x)) = g(f(g(x)))$.
Determine the maximum size of $S$.

Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Determine all real number tuples $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ such that the sequence $a_1 - 2a_2, a_2 - 2a_3, \dots, a_{n-1} - 2a_n, a_n - 2a_1$ is a rearrangement of the sequence $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$.

Let us define a point in the $xy$-plane as a lattice point if both its coordinates are integers from $1$ to $2000$. A polyline $ABCD$ is called a Z-shaped polyline if it satisfies the following:
* All points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ are lattice points.
* $x_1 < x_2$ and $y_1 = y_2$.
* $x_2 > x_3$ and $y_2 - x_2 = y_3 - x_3$.
* $x_3 < x_4$ and $y_3 = y_4$.
Find the minimal positive integer $n$ such that there exist $n$ Z-shaped polylines covering all lattice points in the $2000 \times 2000$ grid.

Let triangle $ABC$ be equilateral with side length $10$. A circle through point $A$ is tangent to side $BC$ at point $X$ (not at the endpoints) and intersects sides $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $E$ (distinct from $A$). If $BX > CX$ and $AD + AE = 13$, compute the length of $BX$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$, $O$ be its circumcenter, and $M$ be the midpoint of arc $BC$ of triangle $ABC$'s circumcircle not containing $A$. Let $D$ lie on the ray $AB$ beyond $B$ such that $BD = BM$, and let $E$ lie on segment $AC$ (excluding endpoints) such that $CE = CM$. Suppose the circumcircles of triangles $ABE$ and $ACD$ intersect again at point $X$. Prove that the perpendicular bisector of segment $DE$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $AOX$.

Find the smallest integer $n \ge 10$ such that
$$
\prod_{k=1}^{10} \left\lfloor \frac{n}{k} \right\rfloor = \binom{n}{10}
$$

Let $\mathbb{N}_0$ be the set of nonnegative integers and $\mathbb{Z}$ be the set of integers. Determine how many sequences $(f(0), f(1), \dots, f(2024))$ satisfy
$$
f(m+n)^2 = f(m|f(n)|) + f(n^2)
$$
for all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}_0$.

In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $AB = 7$, $BC = 18$, and the angle bisector of $\angle CDA$ meet $BC$ at $E$. A point $F$ lies on $DE$ such that $\angle AED = \angle FCD$. Given $BE = 5$ and $EF = 3$, compute $DF$.

Sea $ABC$ un triángulo acutángulo con $M$ el punto medio de $AB$ y $P$ la proyección perpendicular de $A$ sobre $BC$. Demuestra que si $AB = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(AC + BC)$, entonces el círculo circunscrito a $BMP$ es tangente a $AC$.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the identity
$$
 f(2 y + x f(y)) = x f(y) + f(x y) + f(f(y))
$$
for all real $x$ and $y$.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. A vertex $V_i$ ($1 \leq i \leq n$) of a convex polygon $V_1 V_2 \ldots V_n$ is called Bohemian if reflecting $V_i$ across the midpoint of the segment $V_{i-1}V_{i+1}$ (with $V_0 = V_n$ and $V_{n+1} = V_1$) results in a point that is inside or on the boundary of the polygon $V_1 V_2 \ldots V_n$. Determine the minimum number of Bohemian vertices that a convex $n$-gon can have, depending on $n$.

Let triangle $ABC$ with $AC > BC$ have circumcircle $\omega$. A point $P$ lies on $\omega$ such that $AP = AC$ and $P$ is on the minor arc $BC$. Let $Q$ be the intersection of $AP$ and $BC$, and let $R$ be on $\omega$ with $QA = QR$ and $R$ on the minor arc $AC$. If $S$ is the intersection of $BC$ with the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, prove that $P, Q, R, S$ lie on a circle.

Let $\left(b_{n}\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. Suppose that for all sets of four indices $(p, q, r, s)$ satisfying $1 \leqslant p<q \leqslant r<s$ and $p+s = q+r$, the condition $b_{p} + b_{s} > b_{q} + b_{r}$ holds. Find the minimal possible value of $b_{2008}$.
Given an $n \times n$ grid with $n > 1$, how many ways can we choose $2n - 2$ cell centers such that no two are aligned along any line parallel to the main diagonals of the square?

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AC = BC$. The incircle of $\triangle ABC$ touches side $AB$ at point $D$ and side $BC$ at point $E$. A line through $A$, distinct from $AE$, intersects the incircle at points $F$ and $G$. If lines $EF$ and $EG$ intersect $AB$ at points $K$ and $L$, respectively, show that $DK = DL$.

Let $n \geqslant 2$ be an integer. Suppose $n$ positive integers are given. In each move, pick two numbers, say $a$ and $b$, and replace them with $a + b$ and $a + b$. Characterize all $n$ such that it is always possible to make all $n$ numbers equal after finitely many such operations.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral, and let $E$ be a point on diagonal $AC$ such that $AE = AD$ and $CE = CB$. Let $M$ be the center of the circumcircle $k$ of triangle $BDE$, and suppose $k$ intersects $AC$ at $E$ and $F$. Prove that the lines $FM$, $AD$, and $BC$ are concurrent.

For each integer $n \geq 2$, find the maximum value of $C_n$ such that for all positive real numbers $x_1, \ldots, x_n$, the inequality
$$
\frac{x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2}{n} - \left(\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_n}{n}\right)^2 \geq C_n \cdot (x_1 - x_n)^2
$$
holds.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider a regular $n$-gon with a fortress at each vertex. Each fortress simultaneously fires at one of the two adjacent fortresses, hitting it. Define $P(n)$ as the number of distinct sets of hit fortresses, where multiple hits on the same fortress are not distinguished. Show that for any integer $k \geq 3$, $P(k)$ and $P(k+1)$ are coprime.

Initially, only the integer $44$ is written on a board. For any integer $a$ on the board, it can be replaced with four distinct integers $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, a_{4}$ such that $a_{1} + a_{2} + a_{3} + a_{4} = 4a$. In each step, all integers on the board are replaced in this way. After $30$ steps, there are $n = 4^{30}$ integers $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{n}$ on the board. Prove that
$$
\frac{b_{1}^{2} + b_{2}^{2} + \cdots + b_{n}^{2}}{n} \geq 2011
$$

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. John assigns the numbers $1,2,\ldots,n$ to the sides of a regular $n$-gon arbitrarily. Mary then triangulates the polygon with non-crossing diagonals, each labeled 1. For each triangle formed, she writes the product of its three side labels and sums these $n-2$ values to form $S$. Determine the value of $S$ if Mary aims to minimize $S$ and John aims to maximize $S$, with both playing optimally.
Suppose $a$ and $b$, with $a > b$, are positive integers satisfying $a b (a^{2} - b^{2})$ divisible by $a^{3} - b^{3}$. Show that $(a - b)^{3} > 3 a b$.

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that the equality
$$
(x+y)^2 f(x+y) = y^2 f(x) + x^2 f(y) + xy - x^2 - y^2
$$
holds for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$, where $\mathbb{R}$ is the set of real numbers.

\text{Let } x, y, z > 0 \text{ satisfy } \frac{x}{1+x} + \frac{y}{1+y} + \frac{z}{1+z} = 2. \text{ Prove that } \frac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{y} + \sqrt{z}}{2} \geq \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}.

Let $ n $ be an integer with $ n \geqslant 3 $, and define the grid $ \mathcal{G} = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \mid 1 \leqslant x, y \leqslant n\} $. Determine the largest size of a subset $ A \subseteq \mathcal{G} $ such that no three distinct points in $ A $ form a right triangle.

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. Consider a competition with $n$ languages and $3n$ participants, where each participant is fluent in precisely three of these languages. Prove that it is possible to select at least $\left\lceil\frac{2n}{9}\right\rceil$ languages such that no participant is fluent in more than two of them.

Let $P Q R S T$ be a convex pentagon with all sides congruent. Suppose the diagonals $PR$ and $TS$ intersect at a point $X$ such that $\angle RX T = 60^\circ$. Show that $P Q R S T$ has a pair of parallel sides.

\text{Let } x, y, z \text{ be positive real numbers such that } x + y + z = \frac{1}{x^{2}} + \frac{1}{y^{2}} + \frac{1}{z^{2}}. \text{ Prove that } 2(x + y + z) \geq \sqrt[3]{7x^{2}y + 1} + \sqrt[3]{7y^{2}z + 1} + \sqrt[3]{7z^{2}x + 1}. \text{ Find all triples } (x, y, z) \text{ for which equality holds.}

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AC = BC$. Let $N$ be a point inside the triangle satisfying $\angle ANB = 90^\circ + \frac{1}{2} \angle ACB$. Let $D$ be the intersection of the line $BN$ and the line through $C$ that is parallel to $AN$. Let $P$ be the intersection of the internal angle bisectors of $\angle CAN$ and $\angle ABN$. Prove that the lines $DP$ and $AN$ are perpendicular.
\text{Given positive integers } a \text{ and } b, \text{ show that there are positive integers } x \text{ and } y \text{ satisfying } \frac{(x + y)(x + y - 1)}{2} = a x + b y

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
f(2y + x f(x)) = f(x^2) + f(y) + x + y - 1
$$
holds for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

Suppose $n \geq 2$ numbered objects are arranged in a line from position $1$ to position $n$. A process is performed where each adjacent pair of objects is swapped exactly once in the course of the process. How many distinct final arrangements of the objects are possible?

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Construct a triangle $PQR$ such that the sides $PQ$, $QR$, and $RP$ are half the lengths of $AB$, $BC$, and $CA$, respectively, and the lines $PQ$, $QR$, and $RP$ pass through $A$, $B$, and $C$. (All six points $A, B, C, P, Q$, and $R$ are distinct.)

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. A non-intersecting diagonal in a simple $n$-gon is a diagonal that lies entirely within the polygon and does not cross any other diagonal except at a vertex. Let $D(P)$ be the total number of non-intersecting diagonals in a simple $n$-gon $P$, and let $D(n)$ be the minimal value of $D(P)$ over all simple $n$-gons $P$. Prove that all diagonals in $P$ are non-intersecting if and only if $D(P)=D(n)$.
\text{Let } a, b, c > 0 \text{ with } abc = 1. \text{ Show that: } \quad \sum_{\text{cyc}} \frac{a}{2b + c^{2}} \leqslant \frac{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{3}

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\} \to \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$ satisfying
$$
 f\left(x^{2} y f(x)\right) = x^{2} f(x)+f(y)-f(1)
$$
for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$.

Let $N$ be a positive integer. Each of the $N^2$ unit squares in an $N \times N$ grid is divided by a diagonal, either from the top-left to the bottom-right or the bottom-left to the top-right. These diagonals partition the board into $K$ regions. Determine the minimum and maximum possible values of $K$ for each $N$.

Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$ with $AB > AC$, and let $AI$ intersect $BC$ at $D$. Suppose that $P$ lies on segment $BC$ and satisfies $PI = PD$. Let $J$ be the reflection of $I$ over the perpendicular bisector of $BC$, and let $Q$ be the second intersection point of the circumcircles of triangles $ABC$ and $APD$. Prove that $\angle BAQ = \angle CAJ$.

Let $n \geqslant 2$ be an integer and $y_{1}, y_{2}, \ldots, y_{n}$ be real numbers such that
(a) $y_{j} > 0$ for $j=1,2,\ldots,n$ and
(b) $\frac{1}{y_{1}} + \frac{1}{y_{2}} + \cdots + \frac{1}{y_{n}} = n$.
Prove the inequality
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{n} y_{j} \geqslant \sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{1}{\frac{1}{y_{j}} + y_{j}^{2}}
$$
and determine when equality holds.

Let $n \geqslant 3$ and let $S$ be a multiset of positive integers. A valid operation is to select $a, b, c \in S$ such that $a, b, c$ can form a non-degenerate non-equilateral triangle, and replace them with $a+b-c$, $b+c-a$, and $c+a-b$. Prove that this operation cannot be performed infinitely many times.

Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of real numbers. Determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$
\quad f(x) f(a + x) = x f(f(a)) + x f(2x) + f\left(x^{2}\right)
$$
holds for all real numbers $x$ and $a$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be acute with $AB \neq AC$, and let $O$ denote its circumcenter. The line $AO$ meets the circumcircle $\omega$ again at $D$ and the side $BC$ at $E$. The circumcircle of triangle $CDE$ intersects side $CA$ again at $P$. The line $PE$ intersects side $AB$ at $Q$. A line through $O$ parallel to $PE$ meets the altitude from $A$ in point $F$. Show that $FP = FQ$.

Consider the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}+k=xyz$, with $x, y, z$ being positive integers.
Show:
(a) No solutions exist for $k=2017$.
(b) If $k=2016$, then $x$ is a multiple of $3$ for all solutions $(x, y, z)$.
(c) The equation has an infinite number of solutions for $k=2016$.

Determine all functions $ f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ such that
$$
 f\left(f(x) f(y) + x^{2}\right)=x f(x+y)
$$
holds for all real numbers $ x $ and $ y $.

Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Consider a regular $n$-gon with $n$ distinct vertex labels, $n$ distinct side labels, and one label for the interior, all chosen from $2n+1$ distinct consecutive integers. The labelling is called memorable if:

1. For each side, its label equals the average of the labels of the two adjacent vertices.
2. The interior label equals the average of all the vertex labels.

Find all values of $n$ for which such a memorable labelling exists.

\text{Find the minimal real constant } C \text{ for which} \quad \left|a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}+1\right| \leqslant C\left|a^{5}+b^{5}+c^{5}+1\right| \quad \text{is true for all real numbers } a, b, c \text{ such that } a+b+c=-1.

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. A sequence $Q_{1}, Q_{2}, \ldots, Q_{n}$ of distinct points in the plane is called good if the polyline $Q_{1} Q_{2} \ldots Q_{n}$ is non-self-intersecting, no three points are collinear, and for every $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n-2$, the triangle $Q_{i} Q_{i+1} Q_{i+2}$ is oriented in a counterclockwise direction. Determine the maximum integer $k$ such that there exists a set $\{A_{1}, A_{2}, \ldots, A_{n}\}$ of $n$ distinct points in the plane for which exactly $k$ permutations $\sigma$ of the indices $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ yield a good sequence $A_{\sigma(1)}, A_{\sigma(2)}, \ldots, A_{\sigma(n)}$.

Let $\triangle ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB > AC$ and circumcircle $\Gamma$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$. Let $D$ be the point where ray $AC$ intersects ray $BM$. Let $E \neq C$ be the second intersection of the internal angle bisector of $\angle C$ with the circumcircle of $\triangle BDC$. Assume $E$ lies inside $\triangle ABC$, and let $N$ be the second intersection of line $DE$ with $\Gamma$, such that $E$ is the midpoint of $DN$.

Prove that $N$ is the midpoint of the segment connecting the excentres $I_B$ and $I_C$ of $\triangle ABC$ opposite $B$ and $C$, respectively.

Find all integers $n \geqslant 2$ for which there exists a rearrangement $a_{0}, a_{1}, \ldots, a_{n-1}$ of $0,1,\ldots,n-1$ such that the partial sums $S_k = \sum_{i=0}^{k} a_i$ for $k = 0,1,\ldots,n-1$ satisfy $S_k \not\equiv S_j \pmod{n}$ for all $0 \leq k < j < n$.

Let $n$ be an integer with $n \geqslant 3$, and consider the prime factorization of $n!$ as $n! = p_{1}^{\alpha_{1}} p_{2}^{\alpha_{2}} \ldots p_{k}^{\alpha_{k}}$, where $p_{1} < p_{2} < \cdots < p_{k}$ are primes. Find all such $n$ for which the sequence $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2}, \ldots, \alpha_{k}$ forms a geometric progression.

\textbf{a.} Show that for any positive integer $ m $, there is an integer $ n \geq m $ satisfying
$$
\prod_{k=1}^{m} \left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor = \binom{n}{m}
$$
\textbf{b.} Let $ p(m) $ be the minimal $ n \geq m $ for which the above equality holds. Demonstrate that $ p(2018) = p(2019) $.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and $u_{1}, u_{2}, \ldots, u_{n}$ be positive integers with $u_{i} \leq 2^{k}$ for all $i$, where $k \geq 3$. Suppose a non-negative integer $t$ can be expressed as
$$
 t = a_{1} u_{1} + a_{2} u_{2} + \cdots + a_{n} u_{n}
$$
for some non-negative integers $a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots, a_{n}$. Show that there exists such a representation where at most $2k - 1$ of the $a_{i}$ are non-zero.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Points $B'$, $C'$ lie on the rays $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $B'$, $C'$, and $D$ are collinear, and $B$, $C$, $B'$, and $C'$ lie on a circle centered at $O$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$ and $H$ the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$. Show that the quadrilateral $DHMO$ is a parallelogram.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ meet $AC$ at $L$ and the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $W \neq B$. Let $K$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $L$ to $AW$. Let $P$ be the second intersection point of $CK$ with the circumcircle of triangle $BLC$. Let $T$ be the intersection of lines $BP$ and $AW$. Prove that $AW = WT$.

An integer $n$ is called Silesian if there exist positive integers $x, y$ and $z$ such that
$$
n = \frac{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}{xy + yz + zx}
$$

a. Prove that there are infinitely many Silesian integers.

b. Prove that not every positive integer is Silesian.

Find the minimum and maximum values of the expression

$$
\left(\sum_{cyc}\frac{1}{x^{2}+1}\right)\left(\sum_{cyc}\frac{x^{2}}{x^{2}+1}\right)
$$
where $x$, $y$, and $z$ are non-negative real numbers such that $xy+yz+zx=1$.

Let $\beta$ be a real number. Find all real-coefficient polynomials $Q$ such that
$$
Q(2x + \beta) \leq (x^{19} + x^{20}) Q(x)
$$
for all real $x$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute-angled triangle with $AB < AC$. Suppose the perpendicular bisector of $BC$ intersects $AC$ at $D$. Let $P$ be a point on the shorter arc $AC$ of the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ such that $DP \parallel BC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Show that $\angle APD = \angle MPB$.

Let triangle $ABC$ be right-angled at $B$ with circumcircle $c$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of the arc $AB$ not containing $C$. Suppose $P$ lies on segment $AB$ with $CP = CD$, and let $X$ and $Y$ be distinct points on $c$ such that $AX = AY = PD$. Show that $X$, $Y$, and $P$ lie on a straight line.

Let $N$ be a positive integer such that the sum of the squares of all positive divisors of $N$ is equal to the product $N(N+3)$. Prove that $N$ can be expressed as the product of two Fibonacci numbers, $F_i$ and $F_j$, where $\left(F_n\right)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is defined by $F_1 = F_2 = 1$ and $F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2}$ for $n \geq 3$.

Find all real values of $A$ for which every sequence $\{x_{n}\}$ of non-zero real numbers defined recursively by
$$
 x_{n+1}=A-\frac{1}{x_{n}}
$$
for all integers $n \geq 1$, contains at most finitely many negative elements.

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers. Some squares of an $m \times n$ board are marked. A sequence $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{2 r}$ of $2 r \geqslant 4$ distinct marked squares is called a diagonal cycle if for each $k \in\{1, \ldots, 2 r\}$, the squares $b_{k}$ and $b_{k+1}$ lie on a diagonal, but $b_{k}$ and $b_{k+2}$ do not. (Indices are taken modulo $2 r$.) What is the largest number of marked squares on the board such that no such cycle exists?

Let $n \geqslant 3$ be an integer. Zagi starts at a vertex of a regular $n$-gon and makes a sequence of $n-1$ moves, where the $i$-th move consists of moving $i$ steps in the clockwise direction. Show that if after the first $\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ moves Zagi has visited $\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil+1$ distinct vertices, then the total journey will cover all $n$ vertices.

Let triangle $ABC$ have $M$ as the midpoint of $BC$. Let $X$ lie on the ray $AB$ such that $\angle CMA = 2\angle CXA$, and let $Y$ lie on the ray $AC$ such that $\angle AMB = 2\angle AYB$. Let the circumcircle of triangle $AXY$ intersect line $BC$ at points $P$ and $Q$, in the order $P, B, C, Q$. Prove that $PB = QC$.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with acute $\angle DAB$. Define point $E$ on the line $BC$ (not at $B$) such that $AE = AB$, and point $F$ on the line $CD$ (not at $D$) such that $AF = AD$. Let the circumcircle of triangle $CEF$ intersect $AE$ again at $P$ and $AF$ again at $Q$. If $X$ is the reflection of $P$ over line $DE$ and $Y$ the reflection of $Q$ over line $BF$, show that points $A$, $X$, and $Y$ are collinear.

Suppose we have a pair $(x, y)$ of real numbers. Define sequences $(x_{n})$ and $(y_{n})$ by the recurrence relations
$$
x_{n+1} = x_{n} + y_{n} \quad \text{ and } \quad y_{n+1} = x_{n} \cdot y_{n}
$$
for all $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$. Determine all pairs $(x, y)$ for which $x_{2022} = x$ and $y_{2022} = y$.

Let $k$ be a positive integer and $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{k}$ be nonnegative real numbers. Initially, all numbers in a sequence of length $n \geq k$ are zero. In each operation, Nicole selects $k$ consecutive entries and adds $b_{1}$ to the first, $b_{2}$ to the second, and so on up to $b_{k}$. After some number of such operations, all entries in the sequence become equal. Prove that all nonzero values among $b_{1}, b_{2}, \ldots, b_{k}$ are equal.

Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of all real numbers. For each pair $(\beta, \alpha)$ of nonnegative real numbers with $\beta+\alpha \geq 2$, determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$
\quad f(y) f(x) \leq f(x y)+\beta y+\alpha x
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of all real numbers. For each pair $(\beta, \alpha)$ of nonnegative real numbers with $\beta+\alpha \geq 2$, determine all functions $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying
$$
\quad f(y) f(x) \leq f(x y)+\beta y+\alpha x
$$
for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

Determine all integers $n \geq 3$ such that $n$ chords can be drawn in a circle with all $2n$ endpoints distinct, and each chord intersects exactly $k$ other chords, where:
(a) $k = n - 2$,
(b) $k = n - 3$.

Let $x$, $y$, $z$ and $w$ be positive real numbers such that $x y z w = 1$. Prove that
$$
\frac{xy + 1}{x + 1} + \frac{yz + 1}{y + 1} + \frac{zw + 1}{z + 1} + \frac{wx + 1}{w + 1} \geq 4
$$
and find all quadruples $(x, y, z, w)$ for which equality holds.

Let $c \geq 4$ be an even integer. In a football league, each team has a home uniform with two distinct colours and an away uniform with a single colour, not used in the home uniform. At most $c$ distinct colours are used across all uniforms. If two teams share the same home uniform colours, their away uniform colours must differ. A pair of uniforms is clashing if they share a common colour. For each team $X$, there is no team $Y$ such that the home uniform of $X$ is clashing with both uniforms of $Y$. Find the maximum number of teams possible in the league.

Let $c \geq 4$ be an even integer. In a football league, each team has a home uniform with two distinct colours and an away uniform with a single colour, not used in the home uniform. At most $c$ distinct colours are used across all uniforms. If two teams share the same home uniform colours, their away uniform colours must differ. A pair of uniforms is clashing if they share a common colour. For each team $X$, there is no team $Y$ such that the home uniform of $X$ is clashing with both uniforms of $Y$. Find the maximum number of teams possible in the league.

Let triangle $ABC$ be acute with $AB < AC$. Let $J$ be the center of the $A$-excircle of triangle $ABC$, and let $D$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $J$ to $BC$. The internal angle bisectors of $\angle BDJ$ and $\angle JDC$ meet $BJ$ and $JC$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. The segments $XY$ and $JD$ intersect at point $P$. Let $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Prove that the internal bisector of $\angle QAP$ is perpendicular to $XY$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be positive integers. Define a sequence of positive integers $(x_{n})_{n \geq 1}$ by the recurrence relation
$$
x_{n+1} = A \cdot d_{n} + B
$$
where $d_{n} = \operatorname{gcd}(x_{n}, x_{n-1})$ for all $n \geq 2$. Prove that the sequence contains only finitely many distinct terms.

Define the sequences $x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots$ and $y_{0}, y_{1}, y_{2}, \ldots$ with $x_{0} = 0$, $y_{0} = 0$ and recurrence relations
$$
x_{k+1} = y_{k}, \quad y_{k+1} = \frac{x_{k}(y_{k}+1) + 1}{y_{k}+1}
$$
for all $k \geq 0$. Prove that $x_{2024} + y_{2024} \geq 88$.

Let triangle $ABC$ satisfy $\angle BAC = 60^\circ$. Let $D$ be a point on the extension of $AC$ beyond $A$ such that $AB = AD$. Let $E$ and $F$ be two distinct points on the circumcircle of triangle $DBC$ with $AE = AF = BC$. Prove that the line $EF$ goes through the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$.

Let concatenation of positive integers be defined as joining their base ten representations sequentially and reading the result as a single base ten number. Determine all positive integers $k$ such that there exists an integer $N_{k}$ with the following property: for all $n \geq N_{k}$, there exists a permutation of $1, 2, \ldots, n$ whose concatenated result is divisible by $k$.

Let $ k $ be a positive integer and $ a_{1}, a_{2}, \ldots $ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that for each $ i \geq 1 $, the product $ a_{i} a_{i+1} $ divides $ k - a_{i}^{2} $. Show that the sequence eventually becomes constant.
Demonstrați că $8 \cdot \cos^{2} x \cdot (1 - \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}) < 1$, pentru orice $x \in \left[\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

Fie ecuația pătratică $a x^{2} + b x + c = 0$, cu $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$, $a \neq 0$ și $x_1, x_2$ rădăcinile. Să se demonstreze că dacă $c < a < b - c$, atunci cel mult o rădăcină aparține intervalului $(-1, 1)$.

Fie $P$ un punct din interiorul triunghiului $ABC$, cu proprietatea că $\angle CAP = \angle CBP$. Notăm cu $D$ mijlocul segmentului $AB$, iar $M$ și $N$ picioarele perpendicularelor duse din $P$ pe laturile $BC$ și $AC$. Să se arate că $DM = DN$.
Fie $x, y, z$ numere reale pozitive, $x \leq y, x \leq z$, astfel încât $$ \frac{x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}}{x(y+z)}=\frac{3}{2}. $$ Să se arate că $x=y=z$.
Să se demonstreze că există o infinitate de numere întregi pozitive $a$, $b$, $p$, cu $p$ număr prim, care verifică egalitatea $$a^{2} + b^{3} = 2^{p}$$
Fie $x, y, z, w$ numere reale, $x < y < z < w$. Să se demonstreze că $(x + y + z + w)^2 > 8(xz + yw)$.
Să se găsească toate perechile de numere naturale $(m, n)$ pentru care are loc relația $(m! - 1)^2 = n! + 1$.
\text{Demonstrați că nu există } x \in \mathbb{R} \text{ astfel încât } \lfloor x \rfloor + \lfloor 3x \rfloor + \lfloor 9x \rfloor + \lfloor 27x \rfloor + \lfloor 81x \rfloor = 19480.

Fie cubul $ABCD A_{1} B_{1} C_{1} D_{1}$. Punctul $K$ este situat pe muchia $B B_{1}$ astfel încât $\frac{BK}{KB_{1}} = m$. Se construiește planul $\alpha$ care trece prin $K$ și $C_{1}$ și este paralel cu dreapta $BD_{1}$.
a. Fie $P$ punctul în care planul $\alpha$ intersectează muchia $A_{1} B_{1}$. Determinați raportul $\frac{A_{1} P}{P B_{1}}$.
b. Planul $\alpha$ împarte cubul în două corpuri. Calculați raportul volumelor acestor corpuri.
\text{Determinați soluțiile raționale ale ecuației } \sqrt{a \sqrt{5}} - \sqrt{b \sqrt{5}} = \sqrt{3 \sqrt{5} - 5}
Fie $a > 0$ şi $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ cu $|x| < \frac{1}{a}$, $|y| < \frac{1}{a}$. Să se demonstreze că $\left|\frac{x + y}{1 + a^{2} x y}\right| < \frac{1}{a}$.

Demonstrați că, dacă $x, y, z \in [0,1]$, atunci
$$
\frac{3 x^{2}-2 x}{1+y^{3}+z^{3}}+\frac{3 y^{2}-2 y}{1+x^{3}+z^{3}}+\frac{3 z^{2}-2 z}{1+x^{3}+y^{3}} \leqslant 1
$$

Fie $ABC$ un triunghi isoscel cu $AC = BC$. Notăm cu $M$ mijlocul segmentului $AB$, cu $N$ piciorul perpendicularei coborâte din $M$ pe $AC$, și cu $P$ punctul care împarte segmentul $MN$ în raportul $1:1$. Demonstrați că dreptele $BN$ și $CP$ sunt perpendiculare.
Fie $x$, $y$ şi $z$ lungimile laturilor unui triunghi arbitar cu $x + y + z = 1$. Demonstrați că $$ \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} > \frac{9}{\sqrt{1-x} + \sqrt{1-y} + \sqrt{1-z}}. $$
Determinați valorile extreme ale funcției $g:\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\sin x+\cos x+\tan x+\cot x$.
O sferă de rază $R$ este plasată într-un recipient având secțiunea transversală descrisă de curba $y = x^{4}$. Care este valoarea maximă a lui $R$ pentru care sfera atinge originea $(0, 0)$?
Fie $A$ o matrice pătratică de dimensiune $n$, cu toate elementele egal cu $-2019$ sau $2019$. Găsiți cea mai mare valoare posibilă a determinantului $\det(A)$, în cazurile: a) $n=3$; b) $n=4$.
Determinați valoarea minimă a $|z|$ pentru care $$ |z - (-12)| + |z - (5i)| = 13 $$
Fie $I_{n}=n \int_{0}^{1} \frac{\cos x}{1+e^{n x}} d x$, unde $n \in \mathbb{N}^{*}$. Determinați: $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} I_{n}$.
Determinați numerele reale $a, b, c$ care verifică $a-2b+c=2$ și $a+b-2c=5$, astfel încât expresia $F=ab+bc+ac$ să atingă minimul; să se calculeze acest minim.

\text{Să se demonstreze că pentru orice } a, b \in \mathbb{R}, \text{ are loc inegalitatea} \quad \sqrt{(a-3)^{2}+b^{2}} + \sqrt{a^{2}+(b-4)^{2}} \geq 5 \quad \text{şi să se determine cazul egalității.}

Determinați toate perechile $(a, b)$ de numere naturale care verifică relația
$$
a^{2} - 6ab + 8b^{2} + 5b - 5 = 0
$$
Rezolvați în $\mathbb{R}$ ecuația $\frac{x^{2}-2x}{2020^{x}} + 2020^{x^{2}-2x} = 1$.

Fie triunghiul isoscel $ABC$ cu $AC = BC$ și $m(\angle C) = 80^\circ$. Punctul $P$ este în interiorul triunghiului astfel încât $m(\angle PAB) = 30^\circ$ și $m(\angle PBA) = 10^\circ$. Calculați măsura în grade a unghiului $\angle CPB$.
\sum_{\text{cyc}} \sqrt{\frac{a}{b+c+d}} > 2
Găsiți toate numerele întregi $m$ astfel încât $B=\sqrt[3]{m + \sqrt[3]{m - 1}}$ este un număr rațional.
Fie șirul $\left(b_{n}\right)_{n=0}^{\infty}$ cu $b_{1}=1$ și $b_{p+q} + b_{p-q} = \frac{1}{2}(b_{2p} + b_{2q})$, pentru orice $p \geq q \geq 0$. Să se calculeze $b_{2020}$.
\text{Fie } x, y \in [0,1]. \text{ Arătați că:} \quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+y^{2}}} \leq \frac{2}{\sqrt{1+x y}}

Se consideră șirul $\left(b_{n}\right)_{n=0}^{\infty}$, unde $b_{0}=1$, $b_{1}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$ și $b_{n}=2 b_{1} b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}$, $\forall n \geq 2$. Să se determine $b_{2020}$ și $\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{b_{n}}{n^{2}}$.
Fie $J_{n} = \int_{1}^{n} \frac{\lfloor x \rfloor}{x^{2}+1} dx$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $n \geq 2$. Calculați: $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{J_{n}}{\ln n}$.
Determinați o funcție $F:(1 ; +\infty) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ diferențiabilă astfel încât $F'(x) = \frac{x}{\sqrt[4]{(x-1)^{3}(x+1)^{5}}}$, pentru orice $x \in (1 ; +\infty)$.

Fie numerele complexe $z, w, v$ cu $|z|=|w|=|v|=1$ și $zwv \neq -1$. Demonstrați că expresia
$$
 rac{z + w + v + zw + zv + wv}{1 + zwv}
$$
este reală.
